> नयंतः । गर्भं । वनां । धियं । धुः । हिरिश्मश्रुं । न । अर्वाणं । धनअर्चं ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः त्वं जयंतं जेतव्याइत्रूञयंतं महां महांतं
> विपोधां मेधाविनो धर्तारमग्निं प्र भूः । प्रभव । समर्थो भव । स्तोतुमिति
> शेषः । उद्दीथस्तु भूर्जयंतमित्येकपदं मत्वा भूरादील्लोकाञयंतमिति
> व्याचकार । न केवलं त्वमेक एव आपि तु मूरा मूढाः सर्वॆऽपि पुरुषा अमूरममूढं पुरां दर्माणं दारकं ॥ औणादिको मनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥ गर्भमरण्योर्गर्भभूतं वनां वननीयं ॥ वा छंदसि । पा-६-१-१०६,१०७ । इति वचनादमि
> पूर्वाभावः ॥ हिरिश्मश्रुं नार्वाणं । नेत्युपमार्थीयः । श्मश्रुशब्दोऽत्र रोमसामान्यवचनः । हरितरोमोपेतमर्वाणमरणशीलमश्वमिव । उक्तलक्षणाश्ववद्धरितकेशस्थानीयज्वालोपेतं धनर्चं प्रीणनस्तुतिं ॥ शकंध्वादित्वात्पररूपत्वं ॥ ईदृशमग्निं नयंतो हविर्भिः साप्रयंतो धियं कर्म स्तोत्रं ना धुः । प्रापयंति ॥
> गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O praiser, be able (प्र भूः (*pra bhūḥ*)) to praise Agni", who is victorious, conquering the enemies to be conquered, great, and the sustainer of the wise. Uddītha, taking भूर्जयंतं (*bhūrjayaṃtaṃ*) as one word, explained it as "conquering the worlds, Bhūr and the rest". Not you alone: even all foolish men (मूराः (*mūrāḥ*)) praise him who is not foolish, the one who splits cities (पुरां दर्माणं (*purāṃ darmāṇaṃ*)). He is the embryo of the two fire-sticks, to be praised (वनां (*vanāṃ*)). हिरिश्मश्रुं नार्वाणं (*hiriśmaśruṃ nārvāṇaṃ*): न (*na*) is used for comparison; श्मश्रु (*śmaśru*) here means hair in general. He is like a swift horse with green-golden hair, that is, he has flames resembling green hair, and is a lover of the pleasing praise (धनर्चं (*dhanarcaṃ*)). Leading such an Agni with oblations, the priests bring about (धुः (*dhuḥ*)) the rite or the hymn (धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser, you) जयंतं (*jayaṃtaṃ*)—him who conquers enemies
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—the great one
- विपोधां (*vipodhāṃ*)—Agni, the sustainer of the wise priests
- प्रभूः (*prabhūḥ*)—be able to praise
- मूराः (*mūrāḥ*)—even foolish men
- अमूरं (*amūraṃ*)—the discerning one
- पुरां (*purāṃ*)—the enemy cities
- दर्माणं (*darmāṇaṃ*)—the splitter
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—he who is in the fire-sticks in the form of an embryo
- वनां (*vanāṃ*)—praised by all
- हिरिश्मश्रुं (*hiriśmaśruṃ*)—having hair gleaming like gold

### Printed p. 120

- अर्वाणं न (*arvāṇaṃ na*)—like a horse, accompanied by flames of golden hue
- धनर्चं (*dhanarcaṃ*)—Agni, the lover of praise, they praise
- नयंतः (*nayaṃtaḥ*)—the priests who serve with oblations and the like
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—for the performance of the sacrificial rite, or for hearing the hymns
- धुः (*dhuḥ*)—bring to the place of sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, be able to praise Agni, the great one, who sustains the wise priests. Even foolish men praise Agni, the discerning, the splitter of enemy cities, who is in the fire-sticks in the form of an embryo, praised by all, a horse-like one with a mass of hair gleaming like gold, accompanied by golden flames, a lover of praise. The priests who carry and offer oblations and the like bring Agni to the sacrificial altar for the performance of the sacrificial rite.

##### English translation
Be competent, (priest, to glorify) the victorious mighty Agni; the sustainer of the wise, (even) fools (adore) him, the exempt from folly, the demolisher of cities ; conducting the embryo of touchwood, (Agni), like a golden-haired, swift-moving (horse), loving praise and wealth, they bring him to the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि प॒स्त्या॑सु त्रि॒तः स्त॑भू॒यन्परि॑वीतो॒ योन्॑ सीददं॒तः ।  
> अतः॑ सं॒गृभ्या॑ वि॒शां दमू॑ना॒ विध॑र्मणायं॒त्रैरी॑यते॒न्यन् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । पस्त्यासु । त्रितः । स्तभुयन् । परिवीतः । योन् । सीदत् । अंतरिति ।  
> अतः । संगृभ्य । विशां । दमूनाः । विधर्मणा । अयंत्रैः । ईयते । न्यन् ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रितस्त्रिषु स्थानेषु गार्हपत्यादिषु तायमानः स्तभूयन् यजमानगृहान्
> स्तंभयितुमिच्छन् ॥ इच्छार्थे क्यचि तदंताच्छतरि रूपं ॥ परिवीतः परितो ज्वालाभि-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Trita, extended (तायमानः (*tāyamānaḥ*)) in the three places, the Gārhapatya and the others, is स्तभूयन् (*stabhūyan*), wishing to make the houses of the sacrificer firm; परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*) is "surrounded on all sides by flames".

### Printed p. 121

> व्याप्तः सन् पस्त्यासु यागगृहेषु योनावंतः स्वीये वेद्यात्मके स्थाने नि
> षीदत् । निषीदति । अतोर्स्मात्स्थानाद्विशां प्रजानां संबंधीनि हवींषि संगृभ्य
> संग्रहेंद्रादीनुद्दिश्य व्रत्तानि चरुपुरोडाशादीनि स्वीकृत्य दमूना देवेभ्यो
> दानमना यजमानाय वाभिमतप्रदानमना विधर्मणा तासां विविधेन कर्मणा
> निमित्तेन दानमना देवेभ्यो दानपक्षे विविधगमनरूपेण कर्मणायंत्रैः
> शत्रूणां नियमनैः सह नृंदेवानीयते । गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss begun on the previous page. Agni, surrounded all round by flames, sits down in the sacrificial houses, in his own place, the altar (योनावंतः (*yonāvaṃtaḥ*) ... निषीदत् (*niṣīdat*)). From this place he takes up the oblations of the people (विशां (*viśāṃ*)): the cooked offerings, cakes and the like, offered to Indra and the other gods. He is दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*): either intent on giving to the gods, or intent on granting the sacrificer's wishes. By विधर्मणा (*vidharmaṇā*) he does this through varied acts; or, on the view that he gives to the gods, through varied movement. With the *ayaṃtraiḥ*, the restraints of foes, he goes (ईयते (*īyate*)) to the gods (नृन् (*nṛn*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—Agni, established in the three fire-pits Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni
- स्तभूयन् (*stabhūyan*)—firmly establishing the houses of the sacrificers
- परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*)—pervaded by flames all round
- पस्त्यासु (*pastyāsu*)—in the sacrificial houses
- योन् (*yon*)—on the sacrificial altar in the middle
- नि षीदत् (*ni ṣīdat*)—sits down
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—sitting in this his own place
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—the oblations and the like offered by the people
- संगृभ्य (*saṃgṛbhya*)—having accepted; that is, having accepted the cooked offerings, cakes and the like offered in him with reference to Indra and the other gods, in order to convey them to those gods
- दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*)—desirous of giving those oblations to the gods, or desirous of giving the sacrificer his desired ends
- विधर्मणा (*vidharmaṇā*)—by various acts or by various paths
- यंत्रैः (*yaṃtraiḥ*)—holding the enemies in check
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—to the gods
- ईयते (*īyate*)—goes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, established in the three fire-pits Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni, makes the houses of the sacrificers firm, is pervaded by the flames spread all round, and sits on the sacrificial altar in the middle of the sacrificial house. While seated on this altar he accepts the oblations that the people offer in Agni for Indra and the other gods. Desiring to carry them to the gods, and holding his enemies in check, he goes to the gods by various acts or paths.

##### English translation
Occupying three (stations), consolidating (the dwelling of the worshipper), surrounded (by flames), he sits down upon the altar in the chambers (of sacrifice); from thence, having accepted (the oblations) of the people, with intent to give (them to the gods), in various ways, he (Agni) goes to the gods holding (his foes) in check.

### Printed p. 122

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Ṛk in hand praises Agni, described as Trita. For the word Trita Sāyaṇa gives the sense त्रिषु स्थानेषु गार्हपत्यादिषु तायमानः (*triṣu sthāneṣu gārhapatyādiṣu tāyamānaḥ*): the Agni who, being in the three places in three forms (Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya), protects the sacrifice. The seer named Trita has been dealt with earlier (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā vol. 8, p. 443-7). Here we examine which deity this epithet, used of a deity, refers to.

It is not easy to state a precise meaning for the word Trita used of a deity. Scholars who give etymologies following the Vedic tradition, and many English scholars as well, have discussed it, each giving a different meaning. If what Trita is can be learnt as far as possible from the Ṛksaṃhitā and other sources, the opinion of Yāska and the other Vedic commentators must be considered first.

The Nirukta-kāra gives an explanation of this word in two places. First there is an explanation concerning the seer:
त्रितं कूपेवहितमेतत्तूक्तं प्रतिबभौ । तत्र ब्रह्मतिहासमिश्रमृज्मिश्रं गाथामिश्रं भवति ॥ (*tritaṃ kūpevahitametattūktaṃ pratibabhau | tatra brahmatihāsamiśramṛjmiśraṃ gāthāmiśraṃ bhavati ‖*)
(Ni. 4-6)
An explanation concerning the seer, beginning thus, has been given earlier.

Likewise, in explaining Ṛk 1-187-1, Sāyaṇa takes क्षित्यादिस्थानेषु तायमानः इंद्रः (*kṣityādisthāneṣu tāyamānaḥ iṃdraḥ*) to mean Indra, the protector in the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven. The Nirukta-kāra, explaining the same Ṛk, says त्रिस्थान इंद्रः (*tristhāna iṃdraḥ*). He does not say what "three-placed" means; probably, as Sāyaṇa says, it is the three worlds beginning with the earth. Moreover, this epithet also belongs to Vāyu and Soma. We must therefore examine whether the word Trita has a meaning according to each context, or is an epithet denoting a single deity only.

The name Trita is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in forty places in all (the name does not occur in Maṇḍalas 3, 4 and 7). No sūkta is addressed to a deity named Trita, nor is there any context praising this deity alone; nor does the name occur among the deities classified by Yāska. Although they do not fully know the Vedic tradition, the opinions of some English scholars who have laboured and made inquiries from many points of view in this matter are given first.

### Printed p. 123
After that we examine whether those opinions are right or not.

"Indra and Trita both denote the same deity; Trita is an epithet specific to Indra alone," is the opinion of Kuhn. Roth has said it is "an epithet describing the nature of Vāyu."

"A deity who destroys the evil power and sends down rain. Soma is the strength-giving juice of this deity. Hence the power of the two deities Indra and Vāyu is manifest," Benfey has conjectured. There are many more such opinions.

The explanation and etymology that Yāska shows for this word are given above. In about twenty contexts Sāyaṇa has taken this word to mean Trita. In those places, stating the explanation त्रिषु स्थानेषु तायमानः (*triṣu sthāneṣu tāyamānaḥ*), he has taken it, according to each context, to refer to all of these deities: Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa and Agni.

Because of this variety of purport, one single precise meaning cannot be given for this word. Therefore, noting the contexts in which the word is used and examining what each context is, it is explained as best one can.

Of the forty uses in all:
1. (1) Sixteen times it is used together with Indra.
(2) Once only, individually, he is praised as the slayer of Vṛtra.
(3) Once identity with the Vāruṇa horse is stated.
(4) Four times association with the Maruts is stated.
(5) Seven times a distinction of Agni is praised.
(6) Once identity with Varuṇa is stated.
(7) Description of Soma's qualities in four places.
(8) Six times he is described as a deity dwelling in a hidden region.

1) In Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-24 Indra and Trita are described as together facing Vṛtra, and the Maruts are said to give Trita strength. Sāyaṇa explains Trita here as a royal seer, Trita Āptya. (The usage Trita Āptya will be explained later.)
2) In 1-52-4, 5 too a battle with the Asura Vala is described. Indra and Trita both face Vala and help the fall of rain. Sāyaṇa's explanation is that he is one of the three, Ekata, Dvita and Trita.

### Printed p. 124
3) 5-86-1 is a mantra praising Indra and Agni together. Sāyaṇa gives alternative explanations: "Trita, a seer; or Agni, existing in the three places": a seer, or Agni pervading all three places.
4) 5-8-7: the context of Trita preparing to fight Vṛtra. Sāyaṇa takes him as a seer; some others as Vāyu.
5) 5-8-8 and 9: the context in which Trita, impelled by Indra and receiving his help, faces and splits Viśvarūpa, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. He is also described as the maker of rain.
6) 10-99-6 त्रितोन्नोजसा वृधानो विषा वराहमयोअग्रया हन् (*tritonnojasā vṛdhāno viṣā varāhamayoagrayā han*): with an iron-tipped thunderbolt he destroyed the demon Varāha. Indra and Trita are identical.
7) 10-48-2 त्रिताय गा अजनयमहेरधि (*tritāya gā ajanayamaheradhi*): "For Trita I brought forth the cow from the serpent"; Indra himself declares the help he gave Trita. Sāyaṇa's explanation here is that it was help given to Trita Āptya, who had fallen into a well.
8, 9) 2-11-19, 20: as a result of Trita pressing Soma and offering it to Indra, Indra was stimulated and destroyed Vala. In this context some show identity of Trita and Soma. Here Sāyaṇa takes the word त्रितस्य (*tritasya*) as त्रिताय (*tritāya*): Indra hurled his discus for Trita; hence he holds that Trita here means the seer so named.
10) 8-12-16, 17: Sāyaṇa's view is that Trita Āptya is a royal seer.
11) 8-52-1: the same.
12-16) 9-32-2; 9-38-2; 9-34-4; 9-86-20; 1-163-2. Although these five contexts show the same meaning, the last Ṛk has a special sense. Sāyaṇa takes the first four places as a seer and shows the meaning Vāyu in the last Ṛk. For the sentence यमेन दत्तं त्रितः (*yamena dattaṃ tritaḥ*) the explanation is पृथिव्यादिषु त्रिषु स्थानेषु वर्तमानः तीर्णितनो वा वायुः (*pṛthivyādiṣu triṣu sthāneṣu vartamānaḥ tīrṇitano vā vāyuḥ*).

II. Unity with the Vāruṇa horse
17) असि यमोअस्यादित्यो अर्वन्नसि त्रितः (*asi yamoasyādityo arvannasi tritaḥ*) (1-163-2): here it is explained that the Vāruṇa horse has a share of three deities, Yama, Āditya and Trita. What the word Trita means

### Printed p. 125
Sāyaṇa has not stated precisely. He takes Yama to mean Agni. He holds that Trita may be Vāyu moving in the three regions, or else a seer.

III. Trita as slayer of Vṛtra
18) 1-187-1: it was stated above that Sāyaṇa conjectures the meaning of the word Trita here to be Indra.

IV. Contexts showing the association of Trita with the Maruts
19) 2-34-10: the purport of this Ṛk is that the Maruts, sons of Rudra, freed Trita from bondage. Many have tried to explain what the bondage was and who Trita is; no one has understood properly. In this context the scholar Max Müller, after great effort to state a precise meaning for the word, finally said "Its true meaning remains as unfathomable as ever": its meaning remained in the end obscure.
20-21) 2-34-14; 5-54-2. In these two contexts too the association with the Maruts is shown, as in the Ṛk cited above. The purport is probably a seer; but in explaining Ṛk 5-54-2 Sāyaṇa holds that त्रिषु स्थानेषु तायमानो मेघो मरुद्दणो वा (*triṣu sthāneṣu tāyamāno megho maruddaṇo vā*): a cloud, or the troop of Maruts, protecting by pervading the three places.
22) 10-115-4: the purport of the Ṛk is that the Maruts, eager for battle, discovered Agni, who lay hidden among the clouds in the form of Trita. Sāyaṇa too takes the word Trita here to mean Agni.

V. Identity or association of Trita with Agni
23) 5-9-5: in this Ṛk, in which Trita, dwelling in the atmosphere, gives impulse to the spread of Agni's flame extended in the atmosphere, some take the word Trita as Vāyu and some as Agni. By Sāyaṇa's method the meaning is Agni.
24) 5-41-4: a praise of Trita, who has come to our sacrifice together with Vāta, Agni and Pūṣan. Some hold that Trita and Agni are different; some hold that the word Trita is here a synonym of Agni. Sāyaṇa alone holds that it is an epithet of the word Vāta.

### Printed p. 126
25) 5-41-9, 10: the epithets Āptya and अपां नपातं (*apāṃ napātaṃ*) describe Agni in the form of Trita. Sāyaṇa too takes it as Agni.
26) 10-46-3: since the splendour of Trita is described here, some hold it to be Agni. Sāyaṇa takes it to mean a seer.
27) 10-46-6: this is the Ṛk in hand; its explanation is given above. Here it means Agni as lord of the house.
28) 10-64-3: both of these are addressed to the lightning fire.
29) 2-31-6: the same.

VI. Indication of identity of Trita with Varuṇa
30) 8-41-6: it may be Agni, the navel of the deities Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman and the rest; or, as Sāyaṇa says, it may be the deity Varuṇa. Here there is also a good opening to say it is the lightning fire.

VII. Identity or association of Trita with Soma
31-34) 9-37-4; 9-95-4; 9-102-2; 9-102-3: in all four contexts the close relation of Soma and Trita is stated. In some places it is stated that Trita pressed Soma and offered it to Indra. In others it is stated that Soma himself is in the form of Trita.

VIII. Trita hidden in the hidden atmosphere
35) 1-105-9: it is explained that Trita Āptya knows also the seven rays of Āditya (Agni). Earlier, in explaining the same Ṛk, it was stated that Trita Āptya is a seer. There is also scope for taking him as the lightning fire within the cloud. Likewise,
36-40) 1-105-17; 8-47-13; 8-47-14; 8-47-15; 8-47-16: in all these contexts there is scope for taking him as the lightning fire within the cloud.

In the sentences cited above the nature of Trita is described in many ways. The question whether he is of Indra's form, of Vāyu's form or of Agni's form arises naturally. But if all the above contexts are examined closely, only one element of Trita is found equally in all contexts.

The precise meaning that Trita is none other than the lightning fire finds support in all the above sentences.

### Printed p. 127
The battle of Indra with Vṛtra and the others has the purpose of loosening the cloud that was held bound and making rain fall. In this connection the help of Trita (the lightning-fire) must be present. For this very reason the Vāruṇa horse also bears the name Trita. It was stated earlier that this Vāruṇa horse is the divine light, a portion of the Sun. Since this lightning-fire is itself a portion of Agni, the identity of Agni and Trita comes about naturally. It was also explained earlier that Agni, who has three seats, is the one named Trita (1-45-1, 2). The same meaning is to be understood when identity with Soma, Varuṇa and the others is spoken of.

Therefore it would not be wrong to call the relation between Trita and Indra a description of the relation between Agni and Indra. Indra and Agni are often described together, and are praised together as slayers of the demon Vṛtra.

Above all, the epithet "Trita Āptya" is noteworthy. The matter of Agni's three brothers was explained earlier by citing a Taittirīya Saṃhitā passage. There the position of Trita and the meaning of the word "Trita" were stated, and earlier (in the Special Topics on Ṛk 10-45-2) the Śatapatha and Taittirīya Brāhmaṇas were also cited to explain Trita's specific position.

In sum, Sāyaṇa explains in the present Ṛk that Agni is called Trita because he pervades the three worlds.

#### Ṛk 7

### Printed p. 128

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र बहुत्वेन स्तूयते । अस्य यजमानस्य संबंधिनोऽजरासो जरारहिता
> डमां दमनीयानां रक्षःप्रभृतीनां॥ दमेः क्विपि सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं॥
> तेषामरित्रास्तारका अर्चद्दूमासोऽर्चंतोऽर्चनीया धूमा धूमोपलक्षिता
> ज्वाला ना एषां ते तथोक्ताः पावकाः शोधकाः श्वितीचयः श्वेतिमानमंचंतः ॥
> श्वितिः श्वेतः । औणादिक इः ॥ श्वात्रासः । क्षिप्रनामैतत् । क्षिप्रधर्मका भुरण्यवो भरणशीला वनर्षदो वनेषु सीदंतः । संहितायां छांदसं रुत्वं ॥ वायवो न
> सोमा गंतारः सोमा इव । हनिर्दातुर्यजमानस्य शीघ्रा भवंतीति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Agni is praised in the plural. The fires belonging to this sacrificer are undecaying, free from old age. They are अरित्राः (*aritrāḥ*), "rescuers" (*tārakāḥ*), of the दमां (*damāṃ*), the beings that are to be tamed, the rākṣasas and the like; the accent of the case-ending there is explained by the rule that the root दम (*dama*) takes the affix kvip. अर्चद्दूमासः (*arcaddūmāsaḥ*) means having worshipful smoke, that is, flame marked by smoke. They are purifiers. श्वितीचयः (*śvitīcayaḥ*) means moving with whiteness; श्विति (*śviti*) is white, with the Uṇādi affix इ (*i*). श्वात्रासः (*śvātrāsaḥ*) is a word for "swift": they have the nature of swiftness. भुरण्यवः (*bhuraṇyavaḥ*) means bearing, supporting by nature; वनर्षदः (*vanarṣadaḥ*) means sitting in the woods (the change of ending in the Saṃhitā is Vedic). They are वायवो न सोमाः (*vāyavo na somāḥ*): going, like Soma-juices, they become swift to the sacrificer who gives the oblation. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this sacrificer
- अजरासः (*ajarāsaḥ*)—free from old age, that is, without destruction
- दमां (*damāṃ*)—of enemies such as the rākṣasas
- अरित्राः (*aritrāḥ*)—those that hold back
- अर्चद्दू मासः (*arcaddū māsaḥ*)—those having worshipful smoke or flames
- पावकाः (*pāvakāḥ*)—purifiers
- श्वितीचयः (*śvitīcayaḥ*)—shining white
- श्वात्रासः (*śvātrāsaḥ*)—having the nature of quickly pervading everywhere
- भुरण्यवः (*bhuraṇyavaḥ*)—having the capacity to bear and nourish
- वनर्षदः (*vanarṣadaḥ*)—the fires, or fire-flames, hidden in the form of an embryo in the midst of trees and the like
- नायवो न (*nāyavo na*)—like swiftly blowing winds
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—like swiftly flowing Soma-juices, they come quickly and join the sacrificer who offers the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the fires or fire-flames belonging to the sacrificer, kindled on the sacrificial altar of the sacrificers, undecaying (that is, not quickly going out), holding back the rākṣasas and others so that they do not come to the altar, endowed with worshipful smoke or flames, purifying, shining, able to pervade quickly everywhere, bearing the sacrifice, and hidden in the midst of trees and the like, come and join the sacrificers who offer the oblation, like swiftly blowing winds and like swiftly flowing Soma-juices.

##### English translation
The undecaying fires of the worshipper, the rescuers from the humiliated (spirits of ill), having adorable smoke, purifying, becoming white, swift, bearing (the oblation), sitting in the wood, (are) like the fast-flowing juices of the Soma.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निर्ज्ह्वया ज्वालया वेपः । कर्मनामैतत् । कर्म प्र भरते तथा
> योऽग्निर्वयुनानि प्रज्ञानानि स्तोत्राणि पृथिव्या रक्षणाय चेतसानुग्रहयुक्तेन
> मनसा प्र भरते तमग्निमायवो गंतारो मनुष्याः शुचयंतं दीप्यमानं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who with his tongue, his flame, bears forward वेपः (*vepaḥ*) (a word for "rite") the rite; and who, for the protection of the earth, bears forward वयुनानि (*vayunāni*), knowledge, that is, hymns of praise, with a mind full of favour: that Agni the आयवः (*āyavaḥ*), the going ones, men, hold as shining, purifying, मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*) (worthy of praise), होतारं (*hotāraṃ*) (the caller, or the accomplisher of the oblation), and यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*), the one most to be worshipped, the best sacrificer. दधिरे (*dadhire*) means they hold.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (यः (*yaḥ*)) अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the Agni who
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his flame
- वेपः (*vepaḥ*)—the sacrificial rite
- प्र भरते (*pra bharate*)—bears and carries out
- (and) वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)—hymns of praise
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—for the protection of the earth
- चेतसा (*cetasā*)—with a mind of favour
- प्र (*pra*) (भरते (*bharate*))—accepts and carries to the gods
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Agni
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men
- शुचयंतं (*śucayaṃtaṃ*)—as the shining one
- पावकं (*pāvakaṃ*)—the purifier
- मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*)—the one worthy of praise
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the accomplisher of the oblation, or the one who invites the gods
- यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*)—the one worthy of worship, or the one who worships the gods
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they conceive and hold him as such

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who is able to carry out the sacrificial rite with his flame, and who, for the protection of the earth, carries the hymns of men to the gods with a mind of favour: that Agni men conceive and hold as the one who shines with great brilliance, the purifier, the one worthy of praise, the one who invites the gods, the one worthy of worship, or the one who worships the gods on behalf of men.

> व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ आपश्च यमुदपादयन्‌वैद्युतरूपेण त्वष्टा च यमजनयत् भृगवश्च यं सहोभिर्बलैः स्तोत्रादिसाधनैर्लब्धवंतः । भृगवोऽविंदन्निति
> ह्युक्तं । ऋ. १०-४६-२ । ईळेन्यं स्तुत्यं यं प्रथमं मातरिश्वा वायुरुदपादयत् अन्ये देवाश्च मनवे राज्ञे मनोरर्थाय यजत्रं यष्टव्यमग्निं ततक्षुः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni whom heaven and earth जनिष्टां (*janiṣṭāṃ*) produced (a verb with an irregular middle/active ending); whom the waters produced in the form of lightning; whom Tvaṣṭṛ produced; and whom the Bhṛgus obtained by their powers, the means such as hymns. For this it has been said: "the Bhṛgus found" (Ṛ. 10-46-2). That praiseworthy Agni whom Mātariśvan, the wind, first produced, and whom the other gods fashioned, brought to completion, for Manu, the king, as the one to be worshipped.

- मनवे (*manave*)—for the royal seer named Manu
- यजत्रं (*yajatraṃ*)—Agni, worthy of sacrifice
- ततक्षुः (*tatakṣuḥ*)—produced and obtained

The gods also produced and obtained that Agni for the royal seer named Manu.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, bearer of oblations, you whom the gods hold, and whom men hold as the one to be worshipped, पुरुस्पृहः (*puruspṛhaḥ*) desiring many wishes: you, in the यामन् (*yāman*), the sacrifice, give वयः (*vayaḥ*), food, to me who praise. O Agni, from you the worshipper who desires the gods obtains पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*), many, यशसः (*yaśasaḥ*), renown. Because the preverb सं (*saṃ*) is heard, a suitable verb must be supplied: he obtains indeed.

## Sūkta 47 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जगृभ्मा त इत्यष्टर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य सप्तगुनाम्म आर्षं
> त्रैष्टुभं । विकुंठा नामासुरस्त्री । सा चेंद्रसदृशं पुत्रं कामयमाना कृच्छ्रचांद्रायणादिकं तपस्तेपे । मत्सिदृशोऽन्यः कश्चिन्मा जनिष्टेति बुद्ध्वेंद्र एव
> तॆस्याः पुत्रोऽजायत । तादृशो वैकुंठ इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> जगृभ्माष्टौ सप्तगुर्वैकुंठमिंद्रं तुष्टावेत्यादि ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta जगृभ्मा ते (*jagṛbhmā te*) has eight Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. Its seer is Saptagu of the Āṅgirasa line; the metre is Triṣṭubh. Vikuṇṭhā was an Asura woman. Desiring a son like Indra, she performed austerities such as Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa. Indra, thinking that no one like himself should be born, was himself born as her son. The deity is Indra of that kind, Vaikuṇṭha. So the Anukramaṇī says: जगृभ्माष्टौ सप्तगुर्वैकुंठमिंद्रं तुष्टाव (*jagṛbhmāṣṭau saptagurvaikuṃṭhamiṃdraṃ tuṣṭāva*) and so on. The viniyoga is already stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning जगृभ्मा ते (*jagṛbhmā te*) is the fifth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Saptagu of the Āṅgirasa gotra; the metre is Triṣṭup. In ancient times there was an Asura woman named Vikuṇṭhā. Desiring that a son equal to Indra be born to her, she practised austerities for that purpose, observing rules such as Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa. Indra thought that no one else equal to himself should be born, and was himself born as a son to that Asura woman. This son became famous as Vaikuṇṭha Indra; he is the deity of this sūkta. That it is said in the Anukramaṇikā: जगृभ्माष्टौ सप्तगुर्वैकुंठमिंद्रं तुष्टाव (*jagṛbhmāṣṭau saptagurvaikuṃṭhamiṃdraṃ tuṣṭāva*)

Ṛṣi: Saptagu. Deity: Indra Vaikuṇṭha. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज॒गृ॒भ्मा ते॒ दक्षि॑णमिंद्र॒ हस्तं॑ वसू॒यवो॑ वसुपते॒ वसू॑नां ।  
> वि॒द्वा हि त्वा॒ गोप॑तिं शूर॒ गोना॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ चि॒त्रं वृष॑णं ॒ ॑
> रयिं दाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जगृभ्य । ते । दक्षिणं । इंद्र । हस्तं । वसुयवः । वसुपते । वसूनां ॥  
> विद्म । हि । त्वा । गोऽपतिं । शूर । गोनां । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसूनां वसुपते बहूनां धनानां स्वामिन्निंद्र ते तव दक्षिणं हस्तं
> वसूयवो वसुकामा वयं जगृभ्य गृह्णीमः । यथा बहुप्रदस्यार्थिनो
> मह्यमदत्वा न गंतव्यमिति हस्तं गृह्णंति तद्वत् । हे शूर विक्रांतेंद्र त्वा त्वां
> गोनां गोपतिं । अत्र वृत्तवृत्तिभ्यां स्वामित्वं बहुत्वं च प्रतिपाद्यते । बह्नीनां
> गवां गोपतिं विद्म । जानीमः । अतोऽस्मभ्यं चित्रं चायनीयं वृषणं वर्षकं
> रयिं धनं दाः । देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Lord of many riches, Indra, we who desire wealth seize your right hand" — as people who want something from a generous giver take his hand, saying "you must not leave without giving to me." "O hero, valiant Indra, we know you as lord of cattle." Here, through the compound and the suffix, both lordship and plurality are conveyed: we know you as lord of many cows. Therefore give us wealth that is wonderful (चायनीयं (*cāyanīyaṃ*), worthy of reverence) and showering.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—to abundant riches
- वसुपते (*vasupate*)—O Indra, lord
- ते (*te*)—your
- दक्षिणं हस्तं (*dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ*)—right hand
- वसूवयः (*vasūvayaḥ*)—we who desire wealth
- जगृभ्य (*jagṛbhya*)—we seize
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- गोनां (*gonāṃ*)—of many cows
- गोपतिं (*gopatiṃ*)—as the lord
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we know
- (therefore) अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—rain-giving
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

### Printed p. 134

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of abundant riches, we who desire wealth seize your right hand (so that you may not go away without giving us wealth). O valiant Indra, we know you as lord of many cows. Therefore give us wealth of many kinds, granting what we desire.

##### English translation
Indra, lord of abundant wealth, we desiring wealth, seize hold of your right hand ; we know you. hero, lord of abundant cattle, give us various fertilizing riches.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वा॒यु॒धं स्वव॑शं सुनी॒थं चतुः॑समुद्रं ध॒रुणं॑ रयि॒णां ।  
> च॒र्कृत्यं॒ शंस्यं॒ भूरि॑वारम॒स्मभ्यं॑ चि॒त्रं वृष॑णं र॒यिं दाः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुआयुधं । सुअवसं । सुनीथं । चतुःसमुद्रं । धरुणं । रयीणां ।  
> चर्कृत्यं । श्यंसं । भूरिवारं । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वायुधं शोभनवज्राद्यायुधं स्ववसं शोभनरक्षणं सुगमनं वा सुनीथं
> सुनयनं चतुःसमुद्रं चतुरः समुद्रान्नो यशसा व्याप्नोति तं धरुणं धारकं
> केषां । रयीणां धनानां । चर्कृत्यं पुनःपुनः कर्तव्यं शंस्यं स्तुत्यं भूरिवारं
> भूरीणां दुःखानां वारकं बहुभिर्वर्णीयं वा त्वां विद्मेति शेषः । तादृशोऽस्मभ्यमित्यादि पूर्ववत् । यद्वा । हे इंद्र उक्तगुणविशिष्टं पुत्राख्यं रयिं दाः ।
> देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses: स्वायुधं (*svāyudhaṃ*), one with a fine weapon such as the thunderbolt; स्ववसं (*svavasaṃ*), one of fine protection, or of good going; सुनीथं (*sunīthaṃ*), a good leader; चतुःसमुद्रं (*catuḥsamudraṃ*), one who pervades the four oceans with his fame; धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*), the supporter, of riches; चर्कृत्यं (*carkṛtyaṃ*), to be done again and again; शंस्यं (*śaṃsyaṃ*), praiseworthy; भूरिवारं (*bhūrivāraṃ*), warder-off of many sorrows, or one to be chosen by many. The words "we know you" are to be supplied. Such a one — "to us" and so on as before. Alternatively: O Indra, give wealth called a son, endowed with the qualities stated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra, we) स्वायुधं (*svāyudhaṃ*)—one with an excellent thunderbolt weapon
- स्ववसं (*svavasaṃ*)—a giver of excellent protection
- सुनीथं (*sunīthaṃ*)—an excellent guide
- चतुः समुद्रं (*catuḥ samudraṃ*)—one whose fame spreads to the four oceans
- रयाणां (*rayāṇāṃ*)—of riches
- धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)—the supporter
- चर्कृत्यं (*carkṛtyaṃ*)—to be done again and again
- शंस्यं (*śaṃsyaṃ*)—worthy of praise
- भूरिवारं (*bhūrivāraṃ*)—remover of sorrows, or one desired by many
- (त्वां विद्म (*tvāṃ vidma*)—we know you,

### Printed p. 135
 O Indra) अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—consisting of offspring such as sons
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we know you as one with an excellent thunderbolt, a giver of excellent protection, an excellent guide, renowned as far as the four oceans, the supporter of riches, worthy again and again of praise, remover of sorrows or worthy of the regard of many people. Therefore, O Indra, give us wealth of many kinds and offspring such as sons.

##### English translation
(We know you to be) well armed, a sure protector, a safe guide, (renowned throughout) the four oceans, the depositary of riches, deserving of repeated worship. adorable, the preventer of many (ills): grant us various fertilizing riches.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒ब्रह्मा॑णं दे॒ववं॑तं बृ॒हंत॑मु॒रुं ग॑भी॒रं पृ॒थुबु॑ध्नमिंद्र  
> शृ॒तऋ॑षिमु॒ग्रम॑भिमाति॒षाह॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ चि॒त्रं वृष॑णं र॒यिं  ॑
> दाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुब्रह्माणं । देववंतं । बृहंतं । उरुं । गभीरं । पृथुबुध्नं । इंद्र ।  
> श्रुतऋषिं । उग्रं । अभिमाति सहं । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं सुब्रह्माणं । ब्रह्म परिवृढं स्तुतिलक्षणं कर्म । शोभनस्तुतिकमित्यर्थः । देववंतं बृहंतं महांतमुरुं विस्तीर्णं गंभीरमसुरादिभिरगम्यं
> पृथुबुद्धं विस्त्रतमूलं श्रुतऋषिं श्रुता ऋषयो येन तादृशमृषीणां ख्यापयितारं प्रथितज्ञानं वोग्रमुद्गूर्णबलं अत एवाभिमातिषाहमभिमातीनां शत्रुणामभिभवितारं हंतारमस्मभ्यं चित्रं पूज्यं वृषणं वर्षकं पुत्रं रयिं धनं
> दाः । देहि । अथवा विशेषणविशेष्यभावः । उक्तलक्षणं पुत्राख्यं रयिं दाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are सुब्रह्माणं (*subrahmāṇaṃ*): ब्रह्म (*brahma*) is the rite consisting of praise, so one with fine praise; देववंतं (*devavaṃtaṃ*), accompanied by gods; बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*), great; उरुं (*uruṃ*), wide; गभीरं (*gabhīraṃ*), unapproachable by Asuras and others; पृथुबुद्धं (*pṛthubuddhaṃ*), of broad root; श्रुतऋषिं (*śrutaṛṣiṃ*), one by whom the seers are made known, the proclaimer of the seers, of widely known wisdom; उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), of towering strength; therefore अभिमातिषाहं (*abhimātiṣāhaṃ*), the overcomer and slayer of enemies. Give us wonderful (worshipful), showering wealth in the form of a son. Or else there is a relation of qualifier and qualified: give wealth called a son, of the nature stated.

### Printed p. 136

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra, you
- सुब्रह्माणं (*subrahmāṇaṃ*)—praised through the rite called Subrahmaṇya, a praise of Brahman
- देवयंतं (*devayaṃtaṃ*)—accompanied by the gods
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—of great nature
- उरुं (*uruṃ*)—of vast body
- गभीरं (*gabhīraṃ*)—not to be conquered by Asuras and others
- पृथुबुध्नं (*pṛthubudhnaṃ*)—of wide root
- श्रुतऋषिं (*śrutaṛṣiṃ*)—one who knows the seers, or of excellent knowledge
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—of great strength
- अभिमातिषाहं (*abhimātiṣāhaṃ*)—the conqueror of enemies; thus we know you. Therefore
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—worshipful
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granting what is desired
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we know you as worthy of the praise that is a hymn to Brahman, as dwelling with the gods, of great nature, of vast body, unconquerable by Asuras and others, of wide root, as one who knows the seers or is of excellent knowledge, of great strength, and therefore as the conqueror of enemies. Therefore, O Indra, give us worshipful wealth that grants what we desire.

##### English translation
Grant us, Indra, various fertilizing riches, the fit object of prayer, honoured by the gods, large, vast, profound, wide-rooted, by means of which the Rishis are heard, fierce, the subduer of your foes.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒नद्वा॑जं॒ विप्र॑वीरं॒ तरु॑त्रं धन॒स्पृतं॑ शूशु॒वांसं॑ सु॒दक्षं॑ ।  
> द॒स्यु॒हनं॑ पू॒र्भिद॑मिंद्र स॒त्यम॒स्मभ्यं॑ चि॒त्रं वृष॑णं र॒यिं  ॑
> दाः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सनत्वाजं । विप्रवीरं । तरुत्रं । धनस्पृतं । शूशुवांसं । सुदक्षं ॥  
> दस्युहनं । पूभिधं । इंद्र । सत्यं । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सनद्वाजं लब्धान्नं विप्रवीरं मेधाविनं पुत्रं तरुत्रं तारकं धनस्पृतं
> धनानां पूरकं सृष्टारं वा ॥ स्पृणतेः स्पृशतेवोत्तरपदं ॥ शूशुवांसं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सनद्वाजं (*sanadvājaṃ*), one who has obtained food; विप्रवीरं (*vipravīraṃ*), one having a wise son; तरुत्रं (*tarutraṃ*), a rescuer; धनस्पृतं (*dhanaspṛtaṃ*), a filler or creator of riches (the latter member of the compound is from स्पृणतेः (*spṛṇateḥ*) or स्पृणतेः (*spṛṇateḥ*)); शूशुवांसं (*śūśuvāṃsaṃ*)

### Printed p. 137

> वर्धमानं सुदक्षं शोभनबलं दस्युहनं शत्रोणां हंतारं पूर्भिदं शत्रोणां
> पुरां भेत्तारं सत्यं सत्यकर्माणं । शिष्टमुक्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

growing; सुदक्षं (*sudakṣaṃ*), of fine strength; दस्युहनं (*dasyuhanaṃ*), slayer of enemies; पूर्भिदं (*pūrbhidaṃ*), breaker of the cities of enemies; सत्यं (*satyaṃ*), one of true deeds. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra, you
- सनद्वाजं (*sanadvājaṃ*)—one who possesses food and other provisions
- विप्रवीरं (*vipravīraṃ*)—one who has a wise son
- तरुत्रं (*tarutraṃ*)—one who carries across sorrows and the like
- धनस्पृतं (*dhanaspṛtaṃ*)—one filled with riches
- शूशुवासं (*śūśuvāsaṃ*)—one who attains increase
- सुदक्षं (*sudakṣaṃ*)—of excellent strength
- दस्युहनं (*dasyuhanaṃ*)—slayer of enemies
- पूर्विदं (*pūrvidaṃ*)—splitter of the enemies' cities
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of true nature; thus we know you. Therefore
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granting what is desired
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we know you as one who has food and other provisions, who has a wise son, who brings people across sorrows and the like, who provides riches to the praisers, who causes increase, who slays enemies, who destroys the cities of enemies, and who is of true nature. Therefore, O Indra, give us wealth of many kinds that grants what we desire.

##### English translation
Grant us Indra, various fertilizing riches, dispensing food, comprising intelligent male offspring, the protector, filling men with wealth, the granter of increase, the very powerful, the slayer of the Dasyus, the destroyer of cities the observer of truth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अश्वा॑वंतं र॒थिनं॑ वी॒रवं॑तं सह॒स्रिणं॑ श॒तिनं॒ वाज॑मिंद्र ।  
> भ॒द्रव्रा॑तं॒ विप्र॑वीरं स्व॒र्षाम॒स्मभ्यं॑ चि॒त्रं वृष॑णं र॒यिं दाः॑

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्ववंतं । रथिनं । वीरवंतं । सहस्रिणं । शतिनं । वाजं । इंद्र ।  
> भद्रव्रातं । विप्रवीरं । स्वःसां । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः ॥

### Printed p. 138

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अश्वावंतं बहुभिरश्वैरुपेतं रथिनं रथवंतं वीरवंतं वीरैः पुरुषैरुपेतं
> सहस्रिणं सहस्रवंतं शतिनं शतवंतं । असंख्यातगवादियुक्तमित्यर्थः । भद्रव्रातं
> भद्रगणं कल्याणैः सेवकैः परिवृतं विप्रवीरं विप्रैर्वीरैश्चोपेतं स्पर्षां सर्वास
> संभक्तारं वाजं बलवंतं हे इंद्र । शिष्टमुक्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अश्वावंतं (*aśvāvaṃtaṃ*), endowed with many horses; रथिनं (*rathinaṃ*), possessing a chariot; वीरवंतं (*vīravaṃtaṃ*), accompanied by heroic men; सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*), possessing thousands; शतिनं (*śatinaṃ*), possessing hundreds, that is, endowed with countless cattle and the like; भद्रव्रातं (*bhadravrātaṃ*), with a company of good ones, surrounded by auspicious attendants; विप्रवीरं (*vipravīraṃ*), accompanied by sages and heroes; स्पर्षां (*sparṣāṃ*), the sharer of all; वाजं (*vājaṃ*), strong; O Indra. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra, you
- अश्वावंतं (*aśvāvaṃtaṃ*)—one with many horses
- रथिनं (*rathinaṃ*)—one with a chariot
- वीरवंतं (*vīravaṃtaṃ*)—one accompanied by heroic men
- सहस्रिणं शतिनं (*sahasriṇaṃ śatinaṃ*)—one possessed of hundreds or thousands of cattle as wealth
- भद्रव्रातं (*bhadravrātaṃ*)—one served by excellent attendants
- विप्रवीरं (*vipravīraṃ*)—one accompanied by men who are sages and heroes
- स्वर्षां (*svarṣāṃ*)—one who possesses all wealth
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—the mighty one; thus we know you. Therefore
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granting what is desired
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we know that with you are many horses, a chariot, heroic men, hundreds or thousands of cattle, excellent attendants, wise heroes, all wealth and strength. Therefore, O Indra, give us worshipful wealth that grants what we desire.

##### English translation
Grant us, Indra, various fertilizing wealth, consisting of horses, of chariots, of valiant followers, of thousands, of hundreds (of cattle), surrou- ded by beautiful attendants, endowed with sages and heroes, the enjoyer of all (benefits).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्तगुं मां मतिः स्तुतिर्देवविषयाच्छा जिगाति । कीदृषं सप्तगुं ।
> यतधीतिं सत्यकर्माणं सुमेधां शोभनप्रज्ञं बृहस्पतिं बृहतो मंत्रस्य
> स्वामिनं । यः सप्तगुरांगिरसोऽंगिरोगोत्रोत्पन्नोऽहं नमसा नमस्कारेण
> देवानुपसद्यः । उपगतः । यद्वा । नमसान्नेनोपसद्य उपसदनीयः । देवैरनु
> ग्राह्य इत्यर्थः । तादृशायास्मभ्यं मह्यं चित्रं वृषणं रयिं दाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)) directed to the gods comes to me, Saptagu. Sāyaṇa describes the one it comes to: one whose works are true (यतधीतिं (*yatadhītiṃ*) in the block), of good wisdom, and lord (बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)) of a great mantra. "I, Saptagu, born in the family of Aṅgiras, have approached the gods with homage." Alternatively, उपसद्यः (*upasadyaḥ*) means "to be approached with offered food", that is, one to be favoured by the gods. "To such a one, to me, give wealth that is wonderful and showering (desired things)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतधीतिं (*ṛtadhītiṃ*)—one who does only true works
- सुमेधां (*sumedhāṃ*)—one who possesses excellent knowledge
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—lord of many mantras, that is, the maker of many mantras
- सप्तगुं (*saptaguṃ*)—me, who am named Saptagu
- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—the thought of praising the gods
- अच्छ जिगाति (*accha jigāti*)—comes and joins
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—born in the Aṅgiras family
- यः (*yaḥ*)—I, Saptagu, who
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with homage, or endowed with oblation
- उपसद्यः (*upasadyaḥ*)—have approached the gods (therefore, O Indra)
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granting desired ends
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To me, the seer named Saptagu, who am devoted to true works, of excellent knowledge and the author of many mantras, the thought of praising the gods arises. Therefore I, named Saptagu, approach the gods with homage and with oblations and the like. O Indra, give us wealth that is attractive and grants desired ends.

##### English translation
The praise (adressed to the gods) comes to the presence of Saptagu, the observer of the truth, the intelligent, the lord of much (praise), who being of the family of Angiras, has approached (the gods) with oblations: (Indra), grant me various fertilizing riches.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वनीवानो वननवंतः ॥ छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्त्वर्थीयोवनिप् ॥ मम सप्तगोर्दूतासो दूतसदृशाः दूता यथा भर्तुरभिमतार्थं प्रापणीयं प्रापयंति
> तद्वत्सुत्यान्गुणान्प्रायंतः स्तोमाः स्तवाः सुमतीस्तस्येंद्रस्यास्मद्विषया
> अनुकूला बुद्धीरियाना याचमाना इद्रं चरंति । प्राप्पुवंति । पुनश्च त एव
> विशेष्यंते । हृदिस्पृशो हृदये स्पृशंतः । स्तुत्यस्य प्रियभूता इत्यर्थः ॥
> हृद्धुभ्यामित्युपसंख्यानात् जीरलुक् ॥ मनसा सत्योद्रिक्तेन वच्यमाना
> उच्यमानाः । अस्मभ्यमित्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वनीवानः (*vanīvānaḥ*) means "possessing desire". My (Saptagu's) praises are like messengers: as messengers bring to the master the desired thing that is to be brought, so the praises, proclaiming the qualities of the praiseworthy one, are the favourable thoughts of that Indra towards us. Asking, they go to Indra and reach him. These same praises are again qualified: हृदिस्पृशः (*hṛdispṛśaḥ*), touching the heart, that is, dear to the one praised; वच्यमानाः (*vacyamānāḥ*), spoken by a mind filled with truth. The rest, अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) and so on, has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वनीवानः (*vanīvānaḥ*)—desiring Indra's favour
- मम (*mama*)—my
- दूतासः (*dūtāsaḥ*)—going out from my mouth like messengers and coming to Indra
- हृदिस्पृशः (*hṛdispṛśaḥ*)—touching the heart
- मनसा (*manasā*)—by the mind alone, that is, wholeheartedly
- वच्यमानाः (*vacyamānāḥ*)—uttered
- स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)—of the nature of hymns
- सुमतीः (*sumatīḥ*)—our words of praise, made with thought
- इयानाः (*iyānāḥ*)—(asking for desired ends)
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The words of praise, which desire Indra's favourable thought, go out from my mouth like messengers and go to Indra, touch Indra's heart, are uttered wholeheartedly and are of the nature of hymns; they go to Indra asking for desired ends

> अभिः । तत् । द्यावापृथिवी इति । गृणीतां । अस्मभ्यं । चित्रं । वृषणं । रयिं । दाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां यद्वक्षमाणं यामि याचामि ॥ वर्णलोपश्रांदसः ॥
> याच्यमानं तद्दद्धि । देहि ॥ ददातेर्लोटि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । बहुलं
> छंदसीति शपो लुक् ॥ तदिति सामान्येन निर्दिष्टं विशेषयति । बृहंतं महांतं
> क्षयं निवासं जनानामन्येषामसममसाधारणं देहि । त्वया दातव्यं द्यावापृथिवी अभि गृणीतां । अस्मभ्यमित्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, what I ask of you, namely what is about to be said, that give." Sāyaṇa takes यामि (*yāmi*) as "I ask" (loss of a letter being Vedic), दद्धि (*daddhi*) as "give", an imperative of the root *dadāteḥ* with a reversal of voice. "That" is stated in a general way, and he now specifies it: a great dwelling (क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)), unequalled, not common to other men, give. May heaven and earth approve what is to be given by you. The rest, अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) and so on, has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- यत् (*yat*)—for which (what)
- यामि (*yāmi*)—I ask
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दद्धि (*daddhi*)—give
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—that which is large
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—(like the houses) of other people
- असमं (*asamaṃ*)—not ordinary, that is, far better than the houses of all
- क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—give a house fit to dwell in
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- अभि गृणीतां (*abhi gṛṇītāṃ*)—may they approve (the house you give); O Indra
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—attractive
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granting desired ends
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, give us what we ask you to give; that is, give me a dwelling that is large and, unlike the houses of others, not ordinary but most excellent.

### Printed p. 142

## Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The forty-eighth sūkta. Introduction. In this sūkta and in the next, Indra himself praises the many valiant deeds he has done. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes as follows how Indra, famous for many valiant deeds, beginning with the slaying of the demon Vṛtra, came to be given the title Mahān Indra.

The reason Indra got the name Mahān Indra. There is an ancient story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa about how the title Mahān (great) came to Indra.
इंद्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा सर्वा विजितीर्विजित्याब्रवीत्प्रजापतिमहमेतद सानि यत्त्वमहं महासनानीति स प्रजापतिरब्रवीदथ कोऽहमिति यदैवैतदवोच इत्यब्रवीत्ततो वै को नाम प्रजापतिरभवत्को वै नाम प्रजापतिर्यन्महानिंद्रोऽभवत्तन्नहेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं । (*iṃdro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā sarvā vijitīrvijityābravītprajāpatimahametada sāni yattvamahaṃ mahāsanānīti sa prajāpatirabravīdatha ko 'hamiti yadaivaitadavoca ityabravīttato vai ko nāma prajāpatirabhavatko vai nāma prajāpatiryanmahāniṃdro 'bhavattannaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ |*) (Ai. Brā. 12-21)
Formerly, after Indra had slain Vṛtra, he conquered all the regions of the earth, and said to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, you have now gained a great station and are worshipful. Henceforth I want your great position." Prajāpati asked, "If you take my position, who (कः (*kaḥ*)) am I? What is my station?" To this Indra said: "O Prajāpati, as you yourself have just said, your name henceforth shall be Ka (who); that is, you will be denoted by the word Ka." Therefore from that time Prajāpati became denoted by the word Ka. This is well known. For that very reason the matter is stated in the pratigraha mantras, to be recited when one accepts any gift, that is, क इदं (*ka idaṃ*)
### Printed p. 143
कस्मा अदादित्याह । प्रजापतिर्वै कः । प्रजापतय एव तद्ददाति (*kasmā adādityāha | prajāpatirvai kaḥ | prajāpataya eva taddadāti*) is the Brāhmaṇa sentence of the other Vedas. Since the word Ka has the meaning "happiness", in dealings and matters concerning Prajāpati he is said to be of the nature of happiness. Since Indra thus took over the greatness of Prajāpati, the designation Mahān came to Indra; that is, Indra became Mahān Indra. This is stated in the other Vedas: इंद्रो वृत्रमहन्तं देवा अब्रुवन्महान्वा आयमभूद्यो वृत्रमवधीदिति तन्नहेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं । (*iṃdro vṛtramahantaṃ devā abruvanmahānvā āyamabhūdyo vṛtramavadhīditi tannaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ |*). The gods, praising Indra's slaying of Vṛtra, said: since this Indra slew Vṛtra he has become Mahendra (gained a great position), that is, he has become the best of all the gods. This is said to be the reason why the name Mahendra came to Indra.

स महान्भूत्वा देवता अब्रवीदुद्धारं म उद्धरतेति यथाप्येतर्हिच्छतियो वै भवति यः श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते स महान्भवति तं देवा अब्रुवन् स्वयमेव ब्रूष्ट यत्ते भविष्यतीति स एतं माहेंद्रं ग्रहमब्रूत माध्यंदिनं सवनानां निष्केवल्यमुक्तानां त्रिष्टुभं छंदसां पृष्ठं साम्नां तमस्मा उद्धारमदहरन् उदस्मा उद्धारं हरंति य एवं वेद ॥ (*sa mahānbhūtvā devatā abravīduddhāraṃ ma uddharateti yathāpyetarhicchatiyo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatāmaśnute sa mahānbhavati taṃ devā abruvan svayameva brūṣṭa yatte bhaviṣyatīti sa etaṃ māheṃdraṃ grahamabrūta mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanānāṃ niṣkevalyamuktānāṃ triṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ sāmnāṃ tamasmā uddhāramadaharan udasmā uddhāraṃ haraṃti ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
Then Indra, having gained a great position as described above, called the gods and said: "O gods, since I have gained a great position, arrange on this account, that is, to honour me, some ceremony of respect." Even in worldly dealings, when a man obtains unequalled prosperity, or distinction in learning and the like, or the king's honour, he becomes known as a person of esteem among people, and so it is the custom for people to arrange a gathering of honour to congratulate such a man. In the same way Indra put the question to the gods about this. The gods too welcomed Indra's words and said: "O Indra, how should this ceremony of honour be done? How would it please you? You yourself must tell us. We shall act accordingly." Indra then said: among the grahas (a graha is a special vessel for drinking soma) the Māhendra graha (the soma vessel offered to me, who have become Mahendra) must be the best of all the grahas. Likewise, among the three savanas, the morning, midday and third savanas, the midday savana; among the śastras (mantras) such as the Āśvina and Marutvatīya, the niṣkevalya śastra; among the metres such as Gāyatra, the Triṣṭubh metre; and among the sāman chants, the Bṛhad-rathantara sāman, which produces the pṛṣṭha stotra: "you must approve these as the best, for all of them are dear to me. This is the honour you will do me." The gods agreed that it be so, and approved the pre-eminence of the Māhendra graha and the rest in sacrifices and the like. This matter is stated also in the other Vedas: स एतं माहेंद्रमुदहरत वृत्रं हत्वान्यासु (*sa etaṃ māheṃdramudaharata vṛtraṃ hatvānyāsu*)

### Printed p. 144
देवतास्वधीति यन्माहेंद्रो गृह्यत उद्धारमेव तं यजमान उद्धरते न प्रजास्वधि (*devatāsvadhīti yanmāheṃdro gṛhyata uddhārameva taṃ yajamāna uddharate na prajāsvadhi*) The sacrificer who performs a sacrifice and knows this matter obtains pre-eminence and a place of esteem among people.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहंभुवमित्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । पूर्वसूक्तेन सप्तगुना स्तुतो
> हृष्टः सन्निदमादिसूक्तत्रयेण स्वयमात्यानमस्तौत् । तस्माद्वैकुंठस्येंद्रस्य वाक्यत्वाद्यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिरिति परिभाषायेंद्र ऋषिः । वैकुंठस्येंद्रस्य च स्तूयमानत्वाद्या तेनोच्यते सा देवतेति परिभाषायेंद्र एव देवता। दशम्येकादशीसप्तम्य
> स्त्रिस्ष्टुभः । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुबंतपरिभाषया जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । स सप्तगुस्तुतिसंहृष्ट आत्मानमुत्तरैस्तिभिस्तुष्टावाहं भुवॆमेकादशांत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ सप्तमी चेति ॥
> अतिरात्रे द्वितीयपर्याये होतुः शस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । अहं भुवमपाय्क्य स्यांधसो मदायेति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥ समूळ्हस्य दशरात्रस्य तृतीये छंदोमे निष्केवल्येऽप्येतत्तूक्तं । अहं भुवं तत्त इंद्रियमिति निष्केवल्यं ।
> आ. ८-७ । इति सूत्रितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अहंभुवं (*ahaṃbhuvaṃ*) is the sixth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks. Indra, praised by Saptagu in the previous sūkta and delighted, praised himself in this and the next two sūktas. Because the sūkta is the speech of Indra Vaikuṇṭha, Indra is the seer by the rule यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिरिति (*yasya vākyaṃ sa ṛṣiriti*); and because Indra (Vaikuṇṭha) is the one praised, Indra alone is the deity by the rule या तेनोच्यते सा देवतेति (*yā tenocyate sā devateti*). The tenth, eleventh and seventh Ṛks are Triṣṭubh; the rest are Jagatī by the rule that a Ṛk ending in Triṣṭubh pādas is Jagatī. So the Anukramaṇī says; Sāyaṇa quotes it. The sūkta is the hotṛ's śastra in the second paryāya of the Atirātra, and the sūtra says: अहं भुवमपाय्क स्यांधसो मदायेति याज्या (*ahaṃ bhuvamapāyka syāṃdhaso madāyeti yājyā*) (Ā. Sū. 6-4). In the third chandoma of the Samūḷha Daśarātra it is also the niṣkevalya, as the sūtra says: अहं भुवं तत्त इंद्रियमिति निष्केवल्यं (*ahaṃ bhuvaṃ tatta iṃdriyamiti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-7).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta अहं भुवं (*ahaṃ bhuvaṃ*) is the sixth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Indra, praised in the previous sūkta by the seer Saptagu, was satisfied with the seer's praise and praised himself in this sūkta and in the next two sūktas. Therefore, since the subject of this sūkta is the speech of Indra, named Vaikuṇṭha, by the rule "यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिः (*yasya vākyaṃ sa ṛṣiḥ*): he whose speech is in the mantras is the seer of that mantra," Indra is the seer of this sūkta; since Indra is the one praised in this sūkta, by the rule "*yā tenocyate sā devatā*: that which is propounded in the mantra is the deity of that mantra," Indra is the deity of this sūkta. The tenth, eleventh and seventh Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. The Anukramaṇī says so. For the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called hotṛ in the second paryāya of the sacrifice called Atirātra, the use of this sūkta is set out in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अहं भुवमपाय्स्यांधसो मदायेति याज्या (*ahaṃ bhuvamapāysyāṃdhaso madāyeti yājyā*) (Ā. Sū. 6-4). For the niṣkevalya śastra mantras in the third chandoma of the ten-day sacrifice called Samūḷha, the use of this sūkta is set out in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अहं भुवं तत्त इंद्रियमिति निष्केवल्यं (*ahaṃ bhuvaṃ tatta iṃdriyamiti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-7).

> अहंभुवमित्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । पूर्वसूक्तेन सप्तगुना स्तुतो
> हृष्टः सन्निदमादिसूक्तत्रयेण स्वयमात्यानमस्तौत् । तस्माद्वैकुंठस्येंद्रस्य वाक्यत्वाद्यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिरिति परिभाषायेंद्र ऋषिः । वैकुंठस्येंद्रस्य च स्तूयमानत्वाद्या तेनोच्यते सा देवतेति परिभाषायेंद्र एव देवता। दशम्येकादशीसप्तम्य
> त्रिष्टुभः । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुबंतपरिभाषया जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । स सप्तगुस्तुतिसंहृष्ट आत्मानमुत्तरैस्तिभिस्तुष्टावाहं भुवॆमेकादशांत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ सप्तमी चेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The same introduction as in the preceding block, repeated: sixth sūkta of eleven Ṛks; Indra, pleased with Saptagu's praise, praises himself; Indra is seer and deity by the two rules; Ṛks ten, eleven and seven are Triṣṭubh, the rest Jagatī; the Anukramaṇī is quoted; use in the Atirātra (Ā. Sū. 6-4) and in the niṣkevalya of the Samūḷha Daśarātra (Ā. Sū. 8-7). **NOTE**

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I, Indra, have become the chief, the unshared lord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)) of wealth (वसुनः (*vasunaḥ*))." भुवं (*bhuvaṃ*) means "I became"; the lug-ending of the root भू (*bhū*) is used and so on (grammar omitted). Likewise, "I win together (सं (*saṃ*) expresses unity) the wealth of शश्वतः (*śaśvataḥ*)", this being a word for "many", that is, the wealth belonging to many enemies. Moreover living beings, the sacrificers, call upon me alone, as sons call upon a father. I distribute (give) food to the giver (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), the sacrificer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसुनः (*vasunaḥ*)—of wealth
- पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—chief (unshared)

- भुवं (*bhuvaṃ*)—I have become
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- शश्वतः (*śaśvataḥ*)—of many enemies
- धनानि (*dhanāni*)—the wealth
- सं जयामि (*saṃ jayāmi*)—I win and bring
- जंतवः (*jaṃtavaḥ*)—living beings, sacrificers and others
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- पितरं न (*pitaraṃ na*)—as sons call their father with trust
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—they call

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers me oblations
- भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*)—food

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, Indra, am the chief of all wealth, that is, its sole master. I win and bring the wealth of enemies. All beings, that is, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, call upon me with love and respect, as sons call their father. To the sacrificer who offers me oblations I provide food fit for enjoyment.

##### English translation
I am the principal lord of wealth : I conquer the treasure of many (adversaries) : living beings call upon me as (sons call upon) a father ; I bestow food on the donor of oblations.

> मधुविद्यां कस्य चिन्न ब्रूया इति नियमितवान् । यदि ब्रूयस्ते शिरो हरामीत्युक्तवान् । स चाथर्वणोऽश्विभ्यामुवाच । इदं वै तन्मधु दध्यज्ञाथर्वणोऽश्विभ्यामुवाच । शत-१४-५-५-१६ । अश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच । ऋ-१-११६-१२ । इति हि

They tell the legend of the first pāda. Indra went to Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, who possessed the Madhuvidyā, and bound him by a rule: "You must not teach the Madhuvidyā to anyone; if you teach it, I shall cut off your head." That son of Atharvan nevertheless taught it to the Aśvins. For this the Śruti is इदं वै तन्मधु दध्यज्ञाथर्वणोऽश्विभ्यामुवाच । शत-१४-५-५-१६ । (*idaṃ vai tanmadhu dadhyajñātharvaṇo 'śvibhyāmuvāca | śata-14-5-5-16 |*) and अश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच । ऋ-१-११६-१२ । (*aśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvāca | ṛ-1-116-12 |*)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa gives the legend of the first pāda: Indra forbade Dadhyañc, Atharvan's son, who knew the Madhuvidyā, to teach it, on pain of losing his head. Dadhyañc taught it to the Aśvins, as stated in Śa. 14-5-5-16 and Ṛ. 1-116-12. The account continues in the next block.

> मातरिश्वनः पुत्राय दधीच एतन्नामकायर्षये वर्षकामाय प्रवर्षयितुमिच्छन्

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Śruti says that Indra came and cut off Dadhīca's head; to that the verse refers. "I, Indra, am the रोधः (*rodhaḥ*), the obstructor, that is, the remover, of the वक्षः (*vakṣaḥ*) of Atharvan's son Dadhīca", meaning the head, which is marked by the chest. Likewise for Trita, a sage of that name, of the Āptya family, who had fallen into a well, I generated (अजनयं (*ajanayaṃ*), produced) the waters (गाः (*gāḥ*)) from above the cloud (अहेः (*aheḥ*)) so as to raise him out. Trita's prayer to Indra for rescue as he lay in the well is set out in सं मा तपंत्यभितः । ऋ. १०-३३-२ । (*saṃ mā tapaṃtyabhitaḥ | ṛ. 10-33-2 |*). Likewise I took (आ ददे (*ā dade*)) wealth from the Dasyus, the enemies who destroy. What was I doing? Chastising (शिक्षन् (*śikṣan*), restraining) the गोत्रा (*gotrā*), the clouds that guard the waters. For what purpose? For Mātariśvan's son, the sage named Dadhīca, who desired rain, wishing to make it rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अथर्वणः (*atharvaṇaḥ*)—of the sage Dadhīca, the son of the sage Atharvan
- वक्षः (*vakṣaḥ*)—the head
- रोधः (*rodhaḥ*)—I have cut off
- त्रिताय (*tritāya*)—for raising the sage Trita who had fallen into a well
- अहेः (*aheḥ*)—of the cloud
- अधि (*adhi*)—upon (having struck)
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the waters
- अजनयं (*ajanayaṃ*)—I have produced
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- दस्युभ्यः (*dasyubhyaḥ*)—from the Dasyus, the enemies
- नृम्मं (*nṛmmaṃ*)—wealth
- आ ददे (*ā dade*)—I have snatched and brought
- मातरिश्वने (*mātariśvane*)—son of Mātariśvan
- दधीचे (*dadhīce*)—as the sage Dadhīca prayed, to make rain fall
- गोत्रा (*gotrā*)—the clouds
- शिक्षन् (*śikṣan*)—I have chastised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, Indra, have cut off the head of the sage Dadhīca, son of the sage Atharvan. When the sage Trita had fallen into a well and was suffering from thirst, I struck the cloud for him and made a rain of water fall. I have snatched and brought away the wealth of the Dasyus, the enemies. As the sage Dadhīca, son of Mātariśvan, prayed, I have struck the clouds so that they pour rain.

##### English translation
I, Indra, am the striker off of the head of the son of Atharvan. I generated the waters from above the cloud for the sake of Trita. I carried off their wealth from the Dasyus; taming the clouds for Dadhyanch, the son of Matarishwan.

> मम । अनेकं । सूर्यस्य इव । दुस्तरं । मां । आर्यंति । कृतेन । कर्त्वेन । च ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मह्यं मदर्थं त्वष्टा देव आयसमयोमयं वज्रमायुधमतक्षत् ।
> संपादितवान् । देवा मयि विषये क्रतुं स्वविरोधिहननरूपं कर्माप्यवृजन् ।
> समपादयन् । ममानीकं सेनासमूहं सूर्यानीकमिव दुष्टरं । अन्येन
> तरीतुमशक्यं । मामेव कृतेन कर्मणा कर्त्वेनेतः परं कर्तव्येन वृत्रवधादिरूपेणार्यंति । गच्छंति । आर्यतिर्गतिकर्मा । यद्वा । आर्यमीश्वरं कुर्वते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For me the god Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the आयसं (*āyasaṃ*), iron, vajra weapon. The gods in me (मयि (*mayi*)) brought about (अवृजन् (*avṛjan*)) the क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*), the work that consists in slaying their own enemies. My अनीकं (*anīkaṃ*), my host of armies, is hard to cross, like the Sun's host, impossible for another to cross. People go to (आर्यंति (*āryaṃti*)) me alone on account of what has been done (कृतेन (*kṛtena*)) and of what is to be done hereafter (कर्त्वेन (*kartvena*)), such as the slaying of Vṛtra and the like; आर्यति (*āryati*) is a root of motion. Or else: they make me their lord (आर्यं (*āryaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—the god Tvaṣṭṛ
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me
- आयसं (*āyasaṃ*)—made of steel
- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—the vajra weapon
- अतक्षत् (*atakṣat*)—has made and given
- (देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods)
- मयि (*mayi*)—in me
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—the work of slaying enemies
- अपि अवृजन् (*api avṛjan*)—have concentrated
- मम (*mama*)—my
- अनीकं (*anīkaṃ*)—army
- सूर्यस्येव (*sūryasyeva*)—like the sharp rays of the Sun
- दुस्तरं (*dustaraṃ*)—impossible to withstand
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- कृतेन (*kṛtena*)—on account of what has now been done
- कर्त्वेन (*kartvena*)—on account of the Vṛtra-slaying and other deeds to be done hereafter
- आर्यंति (*āryaṃti*)—they approach, regarding me as lord

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Tvaṣṭṛ made for me a vajra weapon of steel. The gods have concentrated and established in me all works of the power to destroy enemies. My army is insupportable, like the sharp rays of the Sun. On account of the deeds of valour that I have now done and shall do hereafter, people approach me, regarding me as their lord.

##### English translation
For me Twashtri fabricated the iron thunderbolt: in me the gods have concentered pious acts : my lustre is insupportable, like that of the

### Printed p. 149
Sun : men acknowledge me as lord ia consequence of what I have done, and of what I shall do.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हमे॒तं ग॒व्यय॒मश्वं॑ प॒शुं पु॑री॒षिणं॒ साय॑केना हिर॒ण्ययं॑  
> पु॒रू स॒हस्रा॒ नि शि॑शामि दा॒शुषे॒ यन्मा॒ सोमा॑स उ॒क्तिनो॒  ॑
> अमंदिषुः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । एतं । गव्ययं । अश्वं । पशुं । पुरीषिणं । सायकेन । हिरण्ययं ॥  
> पुरु । सहस्रा । नि । शिशामि । दाशुषे। यत् । मा । सोमासः । उक्तिनः । अमंदिषुः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहमेतं गव्ययं गोमयमश्वमश्वमयं हिरण्ययं हिरण्यालंकारो
> पेतं पुरीषिणं। पुरीषमुदकं क्षीररूपं। तद्वंतं पशुं शत्रुसंबंधिनं । जात्येकवचनं । पशुसंघमित्यर्थः । तं । सायकेनायुधेनाजयं । तथा पुरु पुरूणि
> सहस्रा सहस्राणि शस्त्राणि नि शिशामि संस्करोमि दाशुशे हर्विदत्तवते यजमानाय+
> वैरिनाशायेत्यर्थः । कदेति उच्यते । यद्यदा मा मां सोमासः सोमा उक्किनः
> शस्त्रोपेताः संतः अथवा सोमेन शस्त्रैश्चोपेता यजमाना अमंदिषुः
> तर्पयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I conquered with the arrow (सायकेन (*sāyakena*)), the weapon, this पशुं (*paśuṃ*) of the enemy": गव्ययं (*gavyayaṃ*) means consisting of cows, अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*) consisting of horses, हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*) furnished with golden ornaments, पुरीषिणं (*purīṣiṇaṃ*) having पुरीष (*purīṣa*), which here is water in the form of milk. The singular पशुं (*paśuṃ*) is generic, meaning a herd of cattle. Likewise I sharpen (नि शिशामि (*ni śiśāmi*), prepare) many thousands of weapons for the sacrificer who has given oblations, that is, for the destruction of his foes. When? यत् (*yat*), when the Somas, together with praises (उक्तिनः (*uktinaḥ*), furnished with śastras), or the sacrificers furnished with Soma and śastras, have delighted (अमंदिषुः (*amaṃdiṣuḥ*), satisfied) me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- मा (*mā*)—me
- सोमासः (*somāsaḥ*)—the Soma juices
- उक्तिनः (*uktinaḥ*)—offered by the sacrificers with mantras
- अमंदिषुः (*amaṃdiṣuḥ*)—satisfy; then
- आहं (*āhaṃ*)—I
- गव्ययं (*gavyayaṃ*)—that which has cows
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—that which has horses
- हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*)—that which is furnished with golden ornaments
- पुरीषिणं (*purīṣiṇaṃ*)—that which has milk
- पशुं (*paśuṃ*)—the herd of cattle in the enemy's possession
- सायकेन (*sāyakena*)—with the weapon I shall conquer (and for the slaying of enemies)
- पुरु (*puru*)—great
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—thousands of weapons
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—for the sacrificer who has offered me oblations
- नि शिशामि (*ni śiśāmi*)—I shall sharpen

### Printed p. 150

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When I am satisfied with the Soma juices that the sacrificers offer me with mantras, then, in order to win from the enemies, for the sacrificers who have offered me oblations, the cows, horses, golden ornaments and cows that give much milk which the enemies possess, I shall sharpen my weapon, and with those great thousands of weapons I shall conquer the enemies.

##### English translation
(I conquered) by my shaft this (wealth) comprehending cows, horses, herds, water, and gold; I give many thousands to the donor(of the oblation) when libations and praises have afforded me delight.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रो धनस्य सर्वस्य स्वाम्यहं धनमात्मीयं न परा जिग्य इत् । नैव
> पराभावयामि । मदीयं धनं न पराभूयत इत्यर्थः । किंचाहं मृत्यवे
> सर्वेषां मारकाय कदा चन कदापि नाव तस्थे । नावस्थितो भवामि । इंद्रभक्ता न
> मृत्युभाजो भवंति किल किमु वक्तव्यमिंद्रस्य मृत्युविरहे । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्सोमं सुन्वंतो हे यजमानाः वसु युष्मदभिमतं धनं मेन्मामेव
> याचत । हे पूरवो मनुष्याः मे सख्ये न रिषाथन । मा रिष्टा भवथ । मत्सख्यं
> मा विनाशयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Indra, lord of all wealth, never let my wealth be overcome (परा जिग्ये (*parā jigye*)): my wealth is not defeated. Moreover I never (कदा चन (*kadā cana*)) submit (अव तस्थे (*ava tasthe*)) to मृत्यवे (*mṛtyave*), death, the slayer of all. Devotees of Indra do not partake of death, so what need to speak of Indra, who is without death? Therefore, O sacrificers who press Soma, ask (याचत (*yācata*)) me alone for the wealth (वसु (*vasu*)) you desire. O पूरवः (*pūravaḥ*), men, do not suffer harm (रिषाथन (*riṣāthana*)) in my friendship; do not destroy my friendship.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- न जिग्यॆ इत् (*na jigyè it*)—I do not allow to be snatched away
- मृत्यवे (*mṛtyave*)—for the destruction of all

- न अव तस्थे (*na ava tasthe*)—I make no effort (therefore)
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- सुन्वंतः (*sunvaṃtaḥ*)—O sacrificers who press it for me
- वसु (*vasu*)—to obtain the wealth you need
- मा इत् (*mā it*)—me alone
- याचत (*yācata*)—ask
- पूरवः (*pūravaḥ*)—O men

- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—friendship
- न रिषाधन (*na riṣādhana*)—do not lose

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the lord of all wealth, do not allow anyone else to win my wealth. I never exert myself to destroy my devotees. Therefore, O sacrificers who press the Soma juice for me, ask me alone for the wealth you need. O men, do not lose my friendship.

##### English translation
I, Indra, am not surpassed in affluence; I never yield to death: pouring forth the Soma libation, ask of me wealth; O men, forfeit not my friendsbip.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Indra, say: these (enemies about to be named), breathing hard, that is, puffing with swollen strength, I have slain two by two, in pairs; the connection is with *tānahanam* "I slew them". Who are "these"? Those enemies who have made Indra, the cleaver of enemies (Nirukta 10-8: Indra is the one who tears enemies apart), the wielder of such a thunderbolt, the mighty (or the one possessed of the vajra), their opponent for battle. And again of what kind? Those who challenge, saying "Come, fight".

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Though they are humble, being strong with bowing power, I, unbending, uttering firm, fearsome, steady words, have slain them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I, Indra
- ये (*ye*)—which enemies
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—me, who cleave enemies in battle

- अकृण्वत (*akṛṇvata*)—call

- द्वाद्वा (*dvādvā*)—I slay two at a time, and
- आह्वयमानान् (*āhvayamānān*)—those enemies who call me to battle
- नमस्विनः (*namasvinaḥ*)—bending by my strength
- अनमस्युः (*anamasyuḥ*)—but I, not bending to them
- दृळ्हा (*dṛḷhā*)—firm and fearsome heroic words
- वदन् (*vadan*)—speaking
- अहनं (*ahanaṃ*)—I slay

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those enemies who, intoxicated with strength, call me, Indra, the cleaver of enemies and bearer of the thunderbolt, to battle, I kill two at a time. Unbending to anyone, I bend with my strength the enemies who challenge me to battle, and uttering fearsome heroic words I destroy them.

##### English translation
I destroy those powerful (enemies) two by two who defy the (wielder of the) thunderbolt, Indra, to battle. I slew them challenging (me to fight) with (great) slaughter, the unbending (slaying) the bending, uttering stern (menaces).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहमिदमिदानीमेकं शत्रुमेकोऽसहाय एव सन्नभ्यस्मि । अभिभवामि ।
> किंच निष्पाट् सपत्नान्निःषहमाणोऽहं द्वा द्वावप्यसहौ शत्रू अभ्यस्मि । किमु किं
> वा त्रयः शत्रवः करंति । कुर्वंति । तानस्यभिभवामीत्यर्थः । किं बहुना । खले न
> खलनिष्पादने यथा जीर्णव्रीह्यादिस्तंबाननायासेन प्रतिहंति कर्षकः तद्वत्पर्षान्निष्टुरान्भूरि बहून्यत्रून्प्रति हन्मि । मा मामनिंद्रा इंद्ररहिता इंद्रमजानंत
> इंद्रविरोधिनः शत्रवो मामिंद्रं किं निंदंति । निंदितुमशक्ता इत्यर्थः । अत्राभिभवामीत्यादि निरुक्तं द्रष्टव्यं ॥ नि. ३-१० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, now, alone, without helper, overcome a single enemy. Further, being the vanquisher of rivals, I overcome even two invincible enemies. Or what can three enemies do? I overcome them. Why say more? As a farmer without effort strikes down the stalks of ripe rice and the like at the threshing-floor, so I strike down the many harsh enemies. Why should enemies who are अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*)—without Indra, not knowing Indra, hostile to Indra—revile me, Indra? They are unable to. Here the Nirukta on अभिभवामि (*abhibhavāmi*) and the rest is to be seen (Ni. 3-10).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I)
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—now
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—one enemy
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—alone, that is, without anyone's help
- अभि अस्मि (*abhi asmi*)—I shall defeat
- निष्षाट् (*niṣṣāṭ*)—I, who have the power to defeat enemies
- द्वा (*dvā*)—two mighty enemies (together)
- अभि (*abhi*)—I shall defeat (not only that)
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—even three enemies
- किमु करंति (*kimu karaṃti*)—what can they do (to me)?
- खले न (*khale na*)—as a farmer easily beats out and separates the grains in the ear
- पर्षान् (*parṣān*)—those intoxicated with strength
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—and many enemies
- प्रति हन्मि (*prati hanmi*)—I kill
- अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*)—those who do not know Indra's power
- शत्रवः (*śatravaḥ*)—enemies
- मा (*mā*)—me
- किं निंदंति (*kiṃ niṃdaṃti*)—are they able to revile?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, Indra, now, without another's help, alone will defeat one enemy. Being the defeater of enemies, I can defeat even two mighty enemies at the same time. Why only that? Even if there are three enemies, what can they do to me? As a farmer effortlessly beats out the grains in the ear of corn, so I shall kill many enemies maddened with strength. Are opponents who do not know my power and capacity able to revile me?

##### English translation
Single, I overcome my single (adversary) : (over-powering them) I overcome two foes ; what can three effect (against me)? I smite numerous (adversaries) like sheaves (of grain) on the threshing-floor ; can my enemies who know not Indra revile me?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To explain the meaning of the word खल (*khala*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given an etymological explanation of this Ṛk.

### Printed p. 154
अभिभवामिदमेकमेकोऽस्मि निष्पहमाणः सपत्ना नभिभवामि । द्वौ किं मा त्रयः कुर्वंति । एक इता संख्या । द्वौ द्रुततरा संख्या । त्रयस्तीर्णतमा संख्या । चत्वारश्चलिततमा संख्या । अष्टावश्नोतेः । नव न वननीया नावाप्ता वा । दश दस्ता दृष्टार्था वा । विशंतिर्द्विर्दशतः । शतं दशदशतः । सहस्रं सहस्वत् । आयुतं नियुतं प्रयुतं तत्तदभ्यस्तं । अर्बुदो मेघो भवति । अरणमंबु तद्दोऽम्बुदः । अंबुमद्भातीति वा । अंबुमद्भवतीति वा । स यथा महान् बहुर्भवति वर्षंस्तदिवार्बुदं । खले न पर्षान् प्रतिहन्मि भूरि । खल इव पर्षान् प्रतिहन्मि भूरि । खल इति संग्रामनाम । खलतेर्वा स्थलतेर्वा । अयमपीतरः खल एतस्मादेव समास्कन्नो भवति । किं मा निंदंति शत्रवोऽनिंद्राः । य इंद्रं न विविदुरिंद्रो ह्यहमस्म्यनिंद्रा इतर इति वा ॥ (*abhibhavāmidamekameko 'smi niṣpahamāṇaḥ sapatnā nabhibhavāmi | dvau kiṃ mā trayaḥ kurvaṃti | eka itā saṃkhyā | dvau drutatarā saṃkhyā | trayastīrṇatamā saṃkhyā | catvāraścalitatamā saṃkhyā | aṣṭāvaśnoteḥ | nava na vananīyā nāvāptā vā | daśa dastā dṛṣṭārthā vā | viśaṃtirdvirdaśataḥ | śataṃ daśadaśataḥ | sahasraṃ sahasvat | āyutaṃ niyutaṃ prayutaṃ tattadabhyastaṃ | arbudo megho bhavati | araṇamaṃbu taddo 'mbudaḥ | aṃbumadbhātīti vā | aṃbumadbhavatīti vā | sa yathā mahān bahurbhavati varṣaṃstadivārbudaṃ | khale na parṣān pratihanmi bhūri | khala iva parṣān pratihanmi bhūri | khala iti saṃgrāmanāma | khalatervā sthalatervā | ayamapītaraḥ khala etasmādeva samāskanno bhavati | kiṃ mā niṃdaṃti śatravo 'niṃdrāḥ | ya iṃdraṃ na vividuriṃdro hyahamasmyaniṃdrā itara iti vā ‖*) (Ni. 3-10)
This is Indra's utterance: "This one enemy before me I can defeat alone (without others' help); likewise, warding off the blows of many enemies, I defeat them all." Here the word एक (*eka*) denotes a number. The word एक (*eka*) is derived from the root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) (to go). When one counts "one", the number one passes away; that is, leaving it, we recite the next number, two. द्वौ द्रुततरा संख्या (*dvau drutatarā saṃkhyā*): द्वौ (*dvau*) means two; the word is derived from the root द्रु (*dru*) meaning "run". Because "two" is counted quickly right after one, the word द्वौ (*dvau*) has the sense of two.
त्रयस्तीर्णतमा संख्या (*trayastīrṇatamā saṃkhyā*): the word त्रयः (*trayaḥ*), three, is derived from the root तृ (*tṛ*), to cross. After the number two has been crossed, the number three, त्रयः (*trayaḥ*), is indicated. चत्वारश्चलिततमा संख्या (*catvāraścalitatamā saṃkhyā*): the number चत्वारः (*catvāraḥ*), four, is derived from the root चलति (*calati*) meaning "move"; as soon as three is done, four; as soon as four is done, five—thus it indicates movement. अष्टावश्नोतेः (*aṣṭāvaśnoteḥ*): the word अष्टौ (*aṣṭau*), eight, is derived from the root अश्नोति (*aśnoti*) (अश् (*aś*), to pervade); because this number includes the numbers from one to seven, अष्टौ (*aṣṭau*) denotes eight. नव नवननीया नावाप्ता वा (*nava navananīyā nāvāptā vā*): the word नव (*nava*), nine, is derived from वन् (*van*), to win, or from न+अ+आप्ल् (*na+a+āpl*), "not to obtain"; that is, the ninth lunar day is not favourable for any good work, hence the name नव (*nava*). **NOTE**
दश दस्ता दृष्टार्था वा (*daśa dastā dṛṣṭārthā vā*): the word दश (*daśa*), ten, may be derived from the root दस् (*das*) (to end, perish) or from दृशिर् (*dṛśir*) (to see, look). For after the number ten has passed,

### Printed p. 155
in the following numbers 11, 12, 13 and so on, the earlier numbers 1, 2, 3 etc. are seen to come again and again. Therefore, from repeated seeing, this number got the name दश (*daśa*). विंशतिर्द्विर्दशतः (*viṃśatirdvirdaśataḥ*): विंशति (*viṃśati*), twenty, means two tens. शतं दशदशतः (*śataṃ daśadaśataḥ*): शतं (*śataṃ*), hundred, means ten times ten. सहस्रं सहस्वत् (*sahasraṃ sahasvat*): सहः (*sahaḥ*) means strength or power. सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*), thousand, includes many numbers and so is very strong; because it is strong it is called सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*). आयुतं (*āyutaṃ*) means ten thousand. Likewise अयुतं, नियुतं, प्रयुतं, तत्तदभ्यस्तं (*ayutaṃ, niyutaṃ, prayutaṃ, tattadabhyastaṃ*): the words अयुतं नियुतं प्रयुतं (*ayutaṃ niyutaṃ prayutaṃ*) indicate numbers each ten times the one before: अयुतं (*ayutaṃ*) ten thousand, नियुतं (*niyutaṃ*) one lakh, प्रयुतं (*prayutaṃ*) ten lakhs, and so on. The word अर्बुद (*arbuda*) means a cloud. अरण (*araṇa*) or अंबु (*aṃbu*) is water; since it gives, that is, pours water, अर्बुद (*arbuda*) is a cloud. As a cloud grows very large in the sky and spreads, so the word अर्बुद (*arbuda*), which denotes a cloud, has the numerical sense of a crore. Or, for the word अर्बुद (*arbuda*) there are two explanations: अंबुमद्भातीती वा (*aṃbumadbhātītī vā*), it shines like water, hence is called cloud; or अंबुमद्भवतीती वा (*aṃbumadbhavatītī vā*), it is like water, hence called cloud. As in the rains the अर्बुद (*arbuda*), the cloud, pours much rain, so when the word is given a numerical sense it means an exceedingly large number, a crore.
In the phrase खले न पर्षान् प्रतिहन्नि भूरि (*khale na parṣān pratihanni bhūri*) the word खल (*khala*) means battle or war. The word खल (*khala*) may be derived from the root खलति (*khalati*) meaning "fall" or from स्खलित (*skhalita*) meaning "kill". This is Indra's statement: "As the chaff of grain is winnowed on the threshing-floor, so I scatter and kill the enemies in battle." Thus because warriors die and fall on the battlefield, the word खल (*khala*) is derived from the root खलति (*khalati*) "fall"; or because in battle they kill one another, खल (*khala*) may be derived from the root स्खलति (*skhalati*) "kill". In this sense खल (*khala*) means battle or war. Besides, the word is also used in the sense of beating grain. In the phrase किं मा निंदंति शत्रवोऽनिंद्राः (*kiṃ mā niṃdaṃti śatravo 'niṃdrāḥ*) the word अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*) means those who are without Indra or who do not worship Indra. How can enemy people, without Indra on their side, that is, without Indra's grace, revile me, Indra? Or, those without Indra's grace—how can they know that I am Indra? How then can such people revile me? This is the main import of the etymology.
