#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> को मा ददर्श कतमः स देवो यो मे तन्नो बहुधा  
> पर्यपश्यत् ।  
> क्वाह॑ मित्रावरुणा क्षियंत्य॒ग्निर्विश्वाः॑ स॒मिधो॑ देव॒यानीः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । मा । ददर्श । कतमः । सः । देवः । यः । मे । तन्वः । बहुधा । परि अपश्यत् ॥  
> क्व । अह । मित्रावरुणा । क्षियंति । अग्नेः । विश्वाः । सं इथः । देवयानीः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदमग्नेर्वाक्यं । एको देवोऽपश्यदित्युक्ते पृच्छति । को मा मां ददर्श
> दृष्टवान् । स देवः कतमः । यो मे मम तन्नस्तनूर्बहुधा बहुप्रकारं स्थिताः
> पर्यपश्यत् परिदृष्टवान् । हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ अग्नेर्मम विश्वाः सर्वाः
> समिधो दीप्ता देवयानीर्देवयानसाधनभूतास्त्वनो दृष्टा इत्युक्तं यदि
> दृष्टाश्चेत्तर्हि क्व क्षियंति क्व निवसंतीत्येवं देवानां पुरतो वर्तमानौ मित्रावरुणावाहाग्निः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is Agni's speech. When told that a single god had seen him, he asks: who has seen me, and which god is it who has seen my bodies, existing in many ways, from all sides? Addressing Mitra and Varuṇa, he asks where all his kindled flames, which serve as the means of the gods' path (देवयानीः (*devayānīḥ*)), have been seen. If they have been seen, where do they dwell? Thus Agni speaks to Mitra and Varuṇa, who stand before the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कः (*kaḥ*)—who
- मा (*mā*)—me
- ददर्श (*dadarśa*)—has seen?
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- मे (*me*)—my
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—bodies
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—that exist in many ways
- पर्यपश्यत् (*paryapaśyat*)—has beheld
- सः (*saḥ*)—such
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—god
- कतमः (*katamaḥ*)—who among the gods?
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of me, who am Agni
- समिधः (*samidhaḥ*)—luminous
- विश्वाः देवयानीः (*viśvāḥ devayānīḥ*)—all the means of carrying the oblation to the gods
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- क्षियंति (*kṣiyaṃti*)—do they dwell?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni: Who has truly known my nature? Who among the gods has known my many kinds of bodies? O Mitra and Varuṇa, where are all my luminous means, those that carry the oblation to the gods?

### Printed p. 261

##### English translation
(Agni speaks :) Who has beheld me ? Which is it of the deities who has fully seen my manifold forms ? Where, Mitra and Varvna, do Agni's luminous vehicles of the gods abide ?

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऐच्छा॑म त्वा बहु॒धा जा॑तवेदः॒ प्रवि॑ष्टमग्ने अ॒प्पोष॑धीषु ।  
> तं त्वा॑ य॒मो अ॑चिकेच्चित्रभानो दशांतरु॒ष्याद॑ति॒रोच॑मानं ॥ ३ ॥

> तं । त्वा । यमः । अचिकेत् । चित्रभानो इति चित्रभानो । दशअंतरुष्यात् ।  
> अतिरोचमानं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवमग्निना पृष्टा देवा अग्निं ब्रुवंति । हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञाग्ने त्वा
> त्वामन्वैच्छाम । कीदृशं त्वां । अप्सूदकेष्टोषधीषु च बहुधा प्रविष्टं । अन्विष्य
> च तं तादृशं प्रविष्टं त्वा त्वां यमो देवोऽचिकेत् ज्ञातवान् हे चित्रभानो
> चायनीयरश्मे । कुत्र स्थितं ज्ञातवानिति तदुच्यते । दशांतरुष्यात् । अंतरुष्यं
> गूढमावासस्थानं तच्च स्थानं दशसंख्योपेतं। तादृशं स्थानमतिरोचमानमतीत्य
> प्रकाशमानं । अग्निर्हि गूढानि दश स्थानानि भवंति पृथिव्यादयस्त्रयो लोका अग्निवाय्वादित्यास्त्रयो देवा आप ओषधयो वनस्पतयः प्राणिशरीरमिति दश स्थानानि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Questioned thus by Agni, the gods reply. O Jātavedas, O Agni of born wisdom, we sought you, who had entered in many ways into the waters and the plants. Having sought you, you thus entered, Yama the god recognised you. O Agni of wondrous (adorable) rays, where you were hidden is now told: दशांतरुष्यात् (*daśāṃtaruṣyāt*)—अंतरुष्यं (*aṃtaruṣyaṃ*) is a hidden dwelling-place, and these places are ten in number; Yama knew you shining beyond such a place. Agni has ten hidden places: the three worlds beginning with the earth; the three gods Agni, Vāyu and Āditya; the waters, the plants, the trees, and the bodies of living beings. These are the ten places.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni in the form of Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—in the waters
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the creepers and plants
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways
- प्रविष्टं (*praviṣṭaṃ*)—who had entered
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- ऐच्छाम (*aicchāma*)—we desired to know and sought
- चित्रभानो (*citrabhāno*)—O Agni of adorable (attractive) radiance
- दशांतरुष्यात् (*daśāṃtaruṣyāt*)—from your ten secret dwelling-places
### Printed p. 262
- अतिरोचमानं (*atirocamānaṃ*)—shining forth
- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you, the renowned
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama
- अचिकेत् (*aciket*)—has known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods: O Agni, Jātavedas, we all desired to know you, who had entered in many ways into the waters and the plants, and sought you. O Agni of attractive radiance, Yama has known you, the renowned, shining forth from your ten secret dwelling-places: earth, atmosphere, heaven, fire, wind, sun, waters, plants, trees and the bodies of living beings.

##### English translation
(The gods :) We sought for you, Agni Jatavedas, who had entered in many ways into the waters, into the plants : Yama recognized you, who have adorable rays, blazing from your ten hiding-places.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हो॒त्राद॒हं व॑रुण॒ बिभ्य॑दायं॒ नेदे॒व मा॑ यु॒नज॒न्नत्र॑  ॒
> देवाः ।  
> तस्य॑ मे त॒न्नो॑ बहु॒धा निवि॑ष्टा ए॒तमर्थं॒ न चि॑केता॒हम॒ग्निः ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> होत्रात् । अहं । वरुण । बिभ्यत् । आयं । न । इत् । एव । मा । युनजन् । अत्र ।  
> देवाः ॥  
> तस्य । मे । तन्नः । बहुधा । निऽविष्टाः । एतं । अर्थं । न । चिकेत । अहं । अग्निः ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया देवगणा मां ज्ञातवंत इति निश्चित्य गूहनस्य प्रयोजनमाह । हे
> वरुण देव अहं होत्राद्धोतव्यात् । हनिर्वहनादित्यर्थः । तस्माद्भिभ्यदायं ।
> आगतवानस्मि । अतो मा मामेवैवं पूर्वप्रकारेणात्रास्मिन्हनिर्वहनप्रयोजने
> नेद्युनजन् मैव योजयंत देवाः । तस्य तादृशस्य बिभ्यतो मे तन्नो बहुधा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Concluding that the company of gods has recognised him by this, Agni states the purpose of his hiding. O Varuṇa, I have come afraid of the होत्रात् (*hotrāt*), that which is to be offered, that is, the carrying of the oblation. Therefore the gods must not again employ me, as before, in this task of carrying the oblation. Of me, afraid in this way, the bodies have entered in many ways into the waters.
### Printed p. 263

> निविष्टा अप्पु । एतमर्थमेतद्धनिर्वहनकार्यमग्निरहं न चिकेत । न बुध्ये ।
> नांगीकरोमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Agni, do not know (न चिकेत (*na ciketa*)), that is, I do not accept, this matter, this task of carrying the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- होत्रात् (*hotrāt*)—from the work of carrying the oblation
- बिभ्यत् (*bibhyat*)—being afraid
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—have come here
- मा (*mā*)—me
- एव (*eva*)—as before
- अत्र (*atra*)—in the work of carrying the oblation
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- न युनजन् इत् (*na yunajan it*)—will certainly not employ
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of one similarly frightened
- मे तन्निः (*me tanniḥ*)—my bodies
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways
- निविष्टाः (*niviṣṭāḥ*)—are hidden (in the waters and the like)
- एतमर्थं (*etamarthaṃ*)—for this task
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- न चिकेत (*na ciketa*)—certainly do not consent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni: O Varuṇa, I have come here frightened by the work of carrying the oblation. The gods will certainly not again associate me with it as before. For that very reason my frightened bodies are hidden in many ways in the waters and the like. I certainly do not consent to this task.

##### English translation
(Agni:) Divine Varuna, I have come hither, being afraid of Hotra, lest the gods should again associate me with him ; my forms have therefore entered (into the waters)in various places. I, Agni, do not consent (to undertake) that office.

> सु॒गान्प॒थः कृ॑णुहि देव॒याना॒न्वह॑ ह॒व्यानि॑ सुमन॒स्यमा॑नः ॥५॥

> सुगान् । पथः । कृणुहि । देवयानान् । वह । हव्यानि । सुमनस्यमानः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 264

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्नि नैवमुक्ता देवाः पुनरग्निमाह्वयंति । हे अग्ने एहि । आगच्छ । मनुर्मनुष्यो यष्टा मननीयो मनू राजा वा देवयुर्देवान्यष्टुमिच्छन् यज्ञकामश्च भवति । अत एहि । किं कुर्वन् यज्ञकामो भवतीति चेत् उच्यते । अरंकृत्य केवलं तेजःपुंजमेवालंकुर्वन् । यद्वेदमुत्तरत्र संबध्यते । त्वमलंकृत्यात्मानमलंकुर्वन् तमस्यनैर्ज्ञातुमशक्केंधकारे क्षेषि । निवससि । हे अग्ने
> आगत्य च देवयानान् देवास्प्रति यैर्मनुष्या गच्छंति तान्पथो मार्गान् सुगान्कृणुहि । कुरु ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । धिन्विकृण्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः ॥ संमत्या
> नो यज्ञनिष्पत्तेर्देवयानाः सुषथा भवंति । वह हव्यान्यस्मदीयानि सुमनस्यमानः सौमनस्यमाचरंस्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressed thus by Agni, the gods call him again: O Agni, come. Manu, the man who sacrifices, or Manu the king worthy of thought, is देवयुः (*devayuḥ*), wishing to worship the gods, and is desirous of sacrifice; therefore come. If asked what he does in being desirous of sacrifice, it is said: अरंकृत्य (*araṃkṛtya*), adorning only a mass of brilliance. Or else the word is connected with what follows: adorning yourself, unable to be known by others, you dwell in darkness. And having come, O Agni, make easy the paths along which men go to the gods, the देवयानान् (*devayānān*) paths. By the agreement of the gods the paths to them become good for the accomplishment of the sacrifice. Carry our oblations, acting with a kindly mind.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- एहि (*ehi*)—be pleased to come
- मनुः (*manuḥ*)—Manu the king (or a man of his line)
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—desirous of worshipping the gods
- यज्ञकामश्च (*yajñakāmaśca*)—and desirous of performing the sacrifice
- अरंकृत्य (*araṃkṛtya*)—adorning only yourself
- तमसि (*tamasi*)—in a secret place unknown to anyone
- क्षेषि (*kṣeṣi*)—you dwell
- देवयानान् (*devayānān*)—along which the gods travel
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—the paths
- सुगान् (*sugān*)—as fit to be travelled
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make
- सुमनस्यमानः (*sumanasyamānaḥ*)—wishing to do us good
- हव्यानि (*havyāni*)—the oblations
- वह (*vaha*)—carry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods: O Agni, accept our prayers and be pleased to come. King Manu wishes to perform the sacrifice and worship the gods. Adorning only yourself, you dwell in a secret place unknown to anyone. Come here and make the paths along which the gods travel fit for travelling. Wishing to do us good, carry the oblations.

##### English translation
(The gods:) Come, Agni, the devout Manu (is) desirous of offering sacrifice adorning yourself, you abide in darkness: make straight the paths traversed by the gods, and with a benevolent mind convey our oblations,

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 265

> तस्माद्भिया वरुण दूरमायं गौरो न क्षेप्पोरविजे  
> ज्यायाः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्नेः । पूर्वे । भ्रातरः । अर्थं । एतं । रथीऽइव । अध्वानं । अनु । आ ।  
> अवरीवुरिति ॥  
> तस्मात् । भिया । वरुण । दूरं । आयं । गौरः । न । क्षेप्पोः । अविजे । ज्यायाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयाग्निः स्वपलायननिमित्तमाह । हे देवा अग्ने र्मम पूर्वे पूर्वमुत्पन्ना भ्रातरो भूपतिर्भुवनपतिर्भूतानां पतिरिति त्रयोऽग्रजा एतमर्थं
> हनिर्वहनाख्यमर्थमन्वावरीवुः । अनुक्रमेण वृतवंतः ॥ तत्र वृणोतेर्यज्लुगंताल्लुजि झेश्छांदसो लुक् । बहुलं छंदसीत्युक्तं ॥ आवरणे दृष्टांतः ।
> रथीनाध्वानं । अध्वानं यथा रथी वृणुते तद्वत् । ते भ्रातरस्तथा कुर्वंतो
> हताः । तस्मान्मरणाद्भिया भीत्या हे वरुण दूरं देशमायं । किं च क्षेप्नोरिसुक्षेपुर्धनुषो ज्यायाः सकाशादौरो न मृग इव स यथा बिभेति चलति वा तद्वदविजे । अकंपे । ओविजी भयचलनयोः । अनुदात्तेत्तादिकः । तस्य लज्युत्तमेरूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this verse Agni gives the cause of his flight. O gods, my elder brothers, born before, three of them, Bhūpati, Bhuvanapati and Bhūtānāṃ pati, took up this task, called the carrying of the oblation, in succession (अन्वावरीवुः (*anvāvarīvuḥ*)). The illustration of the taking up: as a charioteer takes up (follows) the road, so those brothers, doing thus, were slain. Out of fear of that death, O Varuṇa, I have come to a distant place. Further, as a wild animal (गौरो न (*gauro na*)) trembles or flees at the bowstring of an archer, the shooter of arrows, so I too अविजे (*avije*), in trembling.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O gods) रथी (*rathī*)—the driver of a chariot
- अध्वानं इव (*adhvānaṃ iva*)—as one grows thin by going round and round the road
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—my
- पूर्वे भ्रातरः (*pūrve bhrātaraḥ*)—elder brothers
- एतं अर्थं (*etaṃ arthaṃ*)—this very task of carrying the oblation
- अन्वावरीवुः (*anvāvarīvuḥ*)—having performed it, one after another were slain
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- गौरः (*gauraḥ*)—the animal called gaura
- क्षॆप्पोः (*kṣèppoḥ*)—of the bowman who looses the arrow
- ज्यायाः न अविजे (*jyāyāḥ na avije*)—as it flees in fear of the bowstring
- तस्माद्भिया (*tasmādbhiyā*)—from that same fear
- दूरं आयं (*dūraṃ āyaṃ*)—I have come to a distant place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni: O Varuṇa, as a charioteer grows thin by going round and round the road, my elder brothers performed this task of carrying the oblation and were slain one after another. O Varuṇa, as the animal called सौर (*saura*) **NOTE**, frightened, runs trembling at the bowstring of the archer who looses the arrow, so I too, trembling with the same fear, have fled to this distant place.

> रिष्या न म्रियसे तथा कुर्मः । अथ वहासि वह सुमनस्यमानः सौमनस्यं कुर्वन्।
> वोढव्यं वहन् । तदेव दर्शयति । हविषो यजमानप्रत्तस्य भागं । केभ्यः ।
> देवेभ्यः । हे सुजात शोभनजन्मन्नग्ने ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the speech of the gods. "O Agni, the life that is अजरं (*ajaraṃ*), free from old age, that we grant to you. Endowed with that life, O Jātavedas, O one of acquired knowledge, we act so that you do not perish (न रिष्याः (*na riṣyāḥ*), you do not die). Then वहासि (*vahāsi*): bear, being सुमनस्यमानः (*sumanasyamānaḥ*), showing good will, bearing what is to be borne." He shows what: the portion of the oblation given by the sacrificer, for whom? For the gods. "O सुजात (*sujāta*), Agni of fair birth."

- यत् आयुः (*yat āyuḥ*)—the life which

- ते (*te*)—to you
- कुर्मः (*kurmaḥ*)—we grant
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who are Jātavedas
- युक्तः (*yuktaḥ*)—you, endowed with that life
- यथा न रिष्याः (*yathā na riṣyāḥ*)—we shall see to it that you do not perish
- अथ (*atha*)—therefore
- सुजात (*sujāta*)—O Agni of excellent birth

- सुमनस्यमानः (*sumanasyamānaḥ*)—desiring to do good

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods: O Agni, we grant you the life that does not decay. O Agni, Jātavedas, endowed with that life, we shall see to it that you do not perish. Therefore, O Agni of excellent birth, desiring to do good, bear the portions of the oblation to the respective gods.

##### English translation
(The gods :) We grant you life, Agni, which (is) exempt from decay, so that thus endowed, Jatavedas, your will not die; so, becoming concili- ated, well-born Agni, bear their portion of the oblation to the gods.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this verse Agni, having spoken of the bearing of the oblation, makes the request "give". "O gods, give me the oblations named Prayājas, to be offered at the head of the principal offering, and likewise the Anuyājas, to be offered after the principal offering, exclusively, for me alone. Also give the portion of the whole oblation, rice-cake and cooked grain and the rest, that is ऊर्जस्वंतं (*ūrjasvaṃtaṃ*), full of sap through the repeated pouring of ghee,

> स्विष्टकृदाख्यं भागं दत्त । आथवोर्जस्वंतं हविषो भागं प्रयाजानुयाजाख्यं
> दत्तेति योज्यं । किंचापां सारभूतं ताभ्य उत्पन्नं ना धृतमाज्यभागादिसाधनमोषधीनामोषधीभ्य उत्पन्नं पुरुषं च भागं दत्त । किंचाग्नेर्मम दीर्घमायुश्चास्तु । वषट्कारकृतवधभयं मा भूदित्यर्थः। अमुमितिहासं प्रस्तुत्य कौषीतकिब्राह्मणं । तस्मादाहुराग्नेयाः प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा आग्नेयमाज्यमाग्नेयः पुरोडाश इति । शरीरदाया ह ना अग्नयो भवंतीति च ब्राह्मणं
> पुरुषाहुतिर्यस्य प्रियतमेति च ॥

the portion called Sviṣṭakṛt. Or else the construction is: give the portion of the oblation, called Prayāja and Anuyāja, as full of sap. And further give the ghee, the essence of the waters, produced from them, the means of the Ājyabhāgas and the rest, and the पुरुषं (*puruṣaṃ*) portion, produced from the plants. And let there be long life for me, Agni; the meaning is, let there be no fear of death through the vaṣaṭ-call." Having introduced this story, the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa says: तस्मादाहुराग्नेयाः प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा आग्नेयमाज्यमाग्नेयः पुरोडाश इति । (*tasmādāhurāgneyāḥ prayājā āgneyā anuyājā āgneyamājyamāgneyaḥ puroḍāśa iti |*). And a Brāhmaṇa says: शरीरदाया ह ना अग्नयो भवंतीति (*śarīradāyā ha nā agnayo bhavaṃtīti*) and पुरुषाहुतिर्यस्य प्रियतमेति (*puruṣāhutiryasya priyatameti*).

Agni: O gods, offer the oblations named Prayāja and those named Anuyāja so that they reach me alone. Give me the sap-full portion of the oblation. Give the ghee, the essence of the waters, and the Puruṣa portion (food), the essence of the plants. Let me have the power of living long.

##### English translation
(Agni :) Only grant to me, deities, the concentrated portion of the oblation, the Prayajas and the Anuyajas exclusively : (give me) the butter (the essence) of the waters and man (the essence) of the plants; and let the life of Agni be long.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the present Ṛk and in the next, the words प्रयाजाः (*prayājāḥ*) and अनुयाजाः (*anuyājāḥ*) are used. On the meaning of these words Yāska has given the etymological explanation as follows.

### Printed p. 269
अथ किं देवताः प्रयाजानुयाजाः । अग्नेया इत्येके । प्रयाजान्मे अनुयाजांश्च केवलानूर्जस्वंतं हविषो दत्तभागं । धृतं चापां पुरुषं चौषधीनामग्नेश्च दीर्घमायुरस्तु देवाः । तव प्रयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल ऊर्जस्वंतो हविषः संतु भागाः । तवाग्ने यज्ञो ३ यमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमंतां प्रदिशश्चतसः ॥ आग्नेया वै प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*atha kiṃ devatāḥ prayājānuyājāḥ | agneyā ityeke | prayājānme anuyājāṃśca kevalānūrjasvaṃtaṃ haviṣo dattabhāgaṃ | dhṛtaṃ cāpāṃ puruṣaṃ cauṣadhīnāmagneśca dīrghamāyurastu devāḥ | tava prayājā anuyājāśca kevala ūrjasvaṃto haviṣaḥ saṃtu bhāgāḥ | tavāgne yajño 3 yamastu sarvastubhyaṃ namaṃtāṃ pradiśaścatasaḥ ‖ āgneyā vai prayājā āgneyā anuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 8-22)
Having asked "Which deities are the Prayājas and Anuyājas?", he says in answer: आग्नेया इत्येके (*āgneyā ityeke*), "Agni is the deity of those mantras", this being the view of some. A little explanation is necessary here. In sacrifices and other rites one makes offerings in Agni, addressing gods who are not visible. The offerings made to the gods designated and invoked are called principal offerings (mukhyāhuti). It is customary to perform some subsidiary offerings both before and after these principal offerings. Therefore the subsidiary offerings made before the principal offerings are called Prayājas, and those made after the principal offering Anuyājas. In the two Ṛks quoted above, Agni asked the gods for the boon that these offerings, Prayājas and Anuyājas, be made addressed to himself, and that he himself be the deity of those offerings; the gods granted the boon, saying "So be it." Therefore Yāska explains here that, in the view of some, Agni is the deity of these Prayāja-Anuyāja mantras and of the offerings. On this point he also cites the Brāhmaṇa sentence आग्नेया वै प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा (*āgneyā vai prayājā āgneyā anuyājā*). In the same way he states the opinions of other schools:
छंदोदेवता इत्यपरं । छंदांसि वै प्रयाजाश्चंदांस्यनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*chaṃdodevatā ityaparaṃ | chaṃdāṃsi vai prayājāścaṃdāṃsyanuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*)
ऋतुदेवता इत्यपरं । ऋतवो वै प्रयाजा ऋतवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*ṛtudevatā ityaparaṃ | ṛtavo vai prayājā ṛtavo 'nuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*)
पशुदेवता इत्यपरं । पशवो वै प्रयाजा पशवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं॥ (*paśudevatā ityaparaṃ | paśavo vai prayājā paśavo 'nuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ‖*)
प्राणदेवता इत्यपरं । प्राणा वै प्रयाजाः प्राणा वा अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*prāṇadevatā ityaparaṃ | prāṇā vai prayājāḥ prāṇā vā anuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*)
आत्मदेवता इत्यपरं। आत्मा वै प्रयाजा आत्मा वा अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं॥ (*ātmadevatā ityaparaṃ| ātmā vai prayājā ātmā vā anuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ‖*)
Some say that metre is the deity of the Prayāja-Anuyāja mantras. On this there is the Brāhmaṇa sentence छंदांसि वै प्रयाजाश्चंदांस्यनुयाजा (*chaṃdāṃsi vai prayājāścaṃdāṃsyanuyājā*). Others say of these mantras that

### Printed p. 270
the seasons (spring and the rest) are the deities. The Brāhmaṇa sentence ऋतवो वै प्रयाजा ऋतवोऽनुयाजा (*ṛtavo vai prayājā ṛtavo 'nuyājā*) supports this. Others say that animals, cows and the rest, are the deity; the Brāhmaṇa sentence पशवो वै प्रयाजा पशवोऽनुयाजा (*paśavo vai prayājā paśavo 'nuyājā*) is the basis for this. Others say that breath is the deity of these mantras and show as basis the Brāhmaṇa sentence प्राणा वा प्रयाजाः प्राणा वा अनुयाजा (*prāṇā vā prayājāḥ prāṇā vā anuyājā*). Others say that the Self is the deity, and maintain that the Brāhmaṇa sentence आत्मा वै प्रयाजा आत्मा वा अनुयाजा (*ātmā vai prayājā ātmā vā anuyājā*) is the proof for it.
आग्नेया इति तु स्थितिः । भक्तिमात्रमितरत्। किमर्थं पुनरिदमुच्यते । यस्यै देवताय्कॆ हविर्गृहीतं स्यात्तां मनसा ध्यायेद्वषट् करिष्यन्निति ह विज्ञायते ॥ (*āgneyā iti tu sthitiḥ | bhaktimātramitarat| kimarthaṃ punaridamucyate | yasyai devatāykè havirgṛhītaṃ syāttāṃ manasā dhyāyedvaṣaṭ kariṣyanniti ha vijñāyate ‖*) (Ni. 8-22)
Despite all these differences of view and opinion, it is settled that the view that Agni is the deity of these mantras is the one worthy of authority. If so, why are the various differing views stated? What is the use of this? Because there is an injunction and a tradition that, when offering the Prayāja-Anuyāja mantras in Agni with the vaṣaṭ-call, one should offer while meditating in the mind on the deities of the respective mantras, all this had to be set out here in detail.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Thus entreated by Agni, the gods reply: "O Agni, let the Prayājas and Anuyājas be yours alone, exclusive; let the portions of the oblation, ऊर्जस्वंतः (*ūrjasvaṃtaḥ*), strong, be yours. O Agni, let this whole sacrifice be yours. And let the four प्रदिशः (*pradiśaḥ*), the principal quarters, bow to you." The remainder to be supplied: therefore come, bear the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- प्रयाजाः (*prayājāḥ*)—the oblations in the form of Prayāja
- अनुयाजाश्च (*anuyājāśca*)—and the oblations named Anuyāja
- केवले तव (*kevale tava*)—for you alone
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—are designated, let them be
- हविषः (*haviṣaḥ*)—of the oblations
- ऊर्जस्वंतः (*ūrjasvaṃtaḥ*)—sap-full
- भागाः (*bhāgāḥ*)—portions, are for you alone
- अयं सर्वः यज्ञः (*ayaṃ sarvaḥ yajñaḥ*)—this whole sacrifice
- तव (*tava*)—addressed to you alone
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be offered
- चतस्रः प्रदिशः (*catasraḥ pradiśaḥ*)—the four principal quarters
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- नमंतां (*namaṃtāṃ*)—let them bow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods: O Agni, the oblations in the form of Prayāja and those named Anuyāja are designated for you alone. The sap-full portions of the oblations are for you alone. Let the whole sacrifice be offered addressed to you alone. Let the four principal quarters bow to you.

##### English translation
(The gods :) yours, Agni, be the Prayajas and Anuyajas exclusively ; yours be the concentrated portions of the oblations : let this sacrifice, Agni, be all yours and let the four quarters of space bow down before you.

## Sūkta 52 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Pīṭhikā**
Since the Viśvedevas are the deities praised in this sūkta, we explain the matter of these deities here briefly. Their name is read among the thirty-one names that indicate special deities such as the Aśvins. The commentator says that they are separate, special deities. Some say they are all the gods. But from the matter in other sūktas it can be said clearly that the seers worshipped separate deities called Viśvedevas. On this question Yāska has written an explanation of the Ṛk ओमासः (*omāsaḥ*).

### Printed p. 272
आवितारो वावनीया वा मनुष्यधृतः सर्वे देवा इहा गच्छत हत्तवंतो दत्तवतः सुतमिति. तदेतदेकमेव वैश्वदेवं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते यत्तु किंचिद्दहुदैवतं तद्वैश्वदेवानां स्थाने युज्यते यदेव विश्वलिंगमिति शाकपूणिः (*āvitāro vāvanīyā vā manuṣyadhṛtaḥ sarve devā ihā gacchata hattavaṃto dattavataḥ sutamiti. tadetadekameva vaiśvadevaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate yattu kiṃciddahudaivataṃ tadvaiśvadevānāṃ sthāne yujyate yadeva viśvaliṃgamiti śākapūṇiḥ*) (Ni. 12-40). As to the meaning of this Ṛk, there is no difference between the sense we have given and Yāska's sense. But according to Yāska's own account, विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*) means "all the gods", while the view of Śākapūṇi is that the Viśvedevas are a particular set of gods called by that name. It can therefore be said with certainty that there was already a difference of opinion on this point in Yāska's time. If we speak as the usage now stands in domestic (gṛhya) and other rites, it is understood that these Viśvedevas do not belong to the group of ordinary gods; they are a special group of thirteen persons of their own. However that may be, it seems reasonable to say that the Viśvedevas described in the Ṛgveda belong to a separate group of gods.

In the Ṛgveda there are 63 sūktas in praise of the Viśvedevas alone. Besides these, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164 the first 41 Ṛks are addressed to the Viśvedevas. In all of these, except the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-155, many gods are praised, that is, as in other sūktas, gods such as Agni and Indra, and besides them trees, rivers, mountains, cows, horses and the like are also spoken of. Besides these, in sūktas of other deities, in many places, a total of 17 Ṛks have the Viśvedevas as their deity. In all these places the Viśvedevas themselves are named as the deities of these Ṛks; and in the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-125-1 the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are included together with the Viśvedevas.

In the mantra 2-22 of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) Indra is prayed to join with the Ādityas, Vasus, Maruts and Viśvedevas. In the mantras 33-45 to 47 of the same Saṃhitā Indra, Vāyu and other gods are praised together with the Viśvedevas. In the mantra 20-62-6 of the Atharvaveda the Viśvedevas are referred to in the singular, and the Atharvaveda has many sūtras addressed to the Viśvedevas.

### Printed p. 273
In the Brāhmaṇas too the name of the Viśvedevas is mentioned here and there. In the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 4-14 and the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa 1-20 all the gods are addressed by the very name Viśvedevas. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3-9-2-6 the Viśvedevas are called the rays of the sun, in Śa. Brā. 14-2-2-37 the vital airs (prāṇa and the rest), in Śa. Brā. 7-1-1-42 the sacrificial acts, and in Śa. Brā. 2-4-4-13 Indra and Agni. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 5-1-6) Indra and Agni are praised together with the Viśvedevas.

In the Purāṇas, in some places, these Viśvedevas are said to be the lords of the directions. In the Nirukta (Ni. 12-39) it is said that the Viśvedevas are all the gods. Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, has explained the Viśvedevas as the rays of the sun. Yāska, the author of the Nirukta, has stated his own view that the Viśvedevas are all the gods, and has also indicated the view of Śākapūṇi. Śaunaka, speaking of the Viśvedevas in his work Bṛhaddevatā (Bṛ. De. 2-148 to 134, verses), says that Yāska and Śāṇḍilya hold that विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*) means all the gods. Śaunaka's own view is the same.

Sāyaṇācārya, in commenting on this Ṛk, has expressed his view that the Viśvedevas are the thirty-one gods beginning with the Aśvins, who together are called Viśvedevas.

Among Western scholars, Langlois, Kaegi and Hopkins hold that the Viśvedevas are all the gods; Wilson, Griffith and Macdonell accept both meanings: either all the gods, or a separate company of gods called the Viśvedevas.

The main point is this: it may be said that in former times, that is, in very ancient times, the meaning "all the gods" was current for the Viśvedevas, and that in course of time it came into use to think of the Viśvedevas as a company of separate gods of that name. In many Brāhmaṇas and Purāṇas the Viśvedevas are indicated as a separate group of gods. But it is known from Yāska's Nirukta itself that even in Yāska's time there was a difference of opinion on this matter.

In the Ṛgveda, besides the Ṛks addressed to the Viśvedevas that occur here and there, there are 58 separate sūktas that have the Viśvedevas as their deity. In the first maṇḍala of the Ṛ. Saṃ.: sūktas 14, 89, 90, 105, 106, 107, 121, 122; in the second maṇḍala: sūktas 29-31; in the third maṇḍala: sūkta 54; in the fourth maṇḍala: sūkta 55; in the fifth maṇḍala: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51; in the sixth maṇḍala: 49, 50, 51, 52; in the seventh maṇḍala: 35, 36, 37, 39, 40, 42, 43; in the eighth maṇḍala: 27, 28, 29, 30, 58, 83; in the tenth maṇḍala: the sūktas 31, 32, 35, 36, 51, 64, 65, 66, 92, 93, 100, 101, 109, 114, 126, 128, 137, 141, 157, 181 are addressed to the Viśvedevas.

It is necessary to examine here who the Viśvedevas are, what their nature is, and similar questions.

को नु नां वैश्वदेवानि एकादश पराण्यतः । (*ko nu nāṃ vaiśvadevāni ekādaśa parāṇyataḥ |*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-36)

### Printed p. 274
The statement of the Bṛhaddevatā is that, beginning with the sūkta that starts with the mantra को नु वां मित्रावरुण् (*ko nu vāṃ mitrāvaruṇ*), eleven sūktas in all are sūktas of praise addressed to the Viśvedevas; it indicates the details praised in the eleven sūktas of the fifth maṇḍala of the Ṛksaṃhitā, from sūkta 41 to sūkta 51. This is what the Sarvānukramaṇikā states as वैश्वदेवं वै तत् (*vaiśvadevaṃ vai tat*).
(Macdonell's Brihad Dewata, English Translation P. 175)

It is not easy to give a precise opinion on the question "What are the Viśvedevas?" There are differences of view whether the meaning is the assemblage of all the gods, or a separate group (gaṇa) of gods denoting a fixed number. But in the Ṛksaṃhitā there is also a passage that clearly designates all the gods as Viśvedeva groups:

अमी ये देवा स्थन त्रिष्वा रोचने दिवः । (*amī ye devā sthana triṣvā rocane divaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-5)

The gods of the three worlds who are all designated in this mantra are the very gods of whom the Bṛhaddevatā speaks, saying:

बृहस्पतिप्रचोदिता विश्वेदेवगणास्त्रयः । जग्मुस्त्रितस्य तं यज्ञं भागांश्च जगृहुः सह ॥ (*bṛhaspatipracoditā viśvedevagaṇāstrayaḥ | jagmustritasya taṃ yajñaṃ bhāgāṃśca jagṛhuḥ saha ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 1-136)

All the gods, divided into three groups in the three worlds beginning with the earth, impelled by Bṛhaspati, came to Trita's sacrifice and took part in it; thus the word विश्वदेव (*viśvadeva*) is explained as meaning all the gods. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also explains this same view:

वैश्वदेवश्चतुर्थमहर्भवति । विश्वे वै सर्वॆ देवाः सर्वेषां देवानामाप्लै वैश्वदेवा ग्रहा भवंति वैश्वदेव्यः परोरुचः सर्वं वैश्वदेवमसदिति ॥ (*vaiśvadevaścaturthamaharbhavati | viśve vai sarvè devāḥ sarveṣāṃ devānāmāplai vaiśvadevā grahā bhavaṃti vaiśvadevyaḥ parorucaḥ sarvaṃ vaiśvadevamasaditi ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-7-1-6)

The fourth day is Vaiśvadeva. Viśvedevas means all the gods. The aim is that on the fourth day their full favour should be obtained. The Soma cups are Vaiśvadeva cups. The groups of rites called Parorukh also aim at winning the favour of all the gods. Therefore these cups must satisfy all the gods. And likewise:

इति ह स्माह सत्यकामो जाबालो विश्वे वै सर्वॆ देवास्तदेनान्यथा देवतं प्रीणातीति ॥ (*iti ha smāha satyakāmo jābālo viśve vai sarvè devāstadenānyathā devataṃ prīṇātīti ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-5-2-1)

### Printed p. 275
Viśvedevas means all the gods; therefore, the Śatapatha states clearly, Satyakāma Jābāla declared that by this rite, which has the Viśvedevas as its deity, individual satisfaction is obtained by all the gods. Although the view that the word applies to all the gods is found in Vedic passages themselves, in some other places room is left for an alternative meaning. For example:

स नैव व्यभवत्स विशमसृजत यान्येतानि देवजातानि गणश अख्यायंते वसवो रुद्रा आदित्या विश्वे देवा मरुत इति ॥ (*sa naiva vyabhavatsa viśamasṛjata yānyetāni devajātāni gaṇaśa akhyāyaṃte vasavo rudrā ādityā viśve devā maruta iti ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 1-4-12)

Prajāpati, engaged in the work of creation, had not yet attained the fullness of creation. Then he created the creatures and the gods who are designated in the form of groups (gaṇa). They are the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas and Viśvedevas; and then the Maruts are also mentioned. Śaṅkarācārya, in his commentary, explains that among these groups the Vasus show a group of eight, the Rudras a group of eleven (11), the Ādityas a group of twelve (12), and the Maruts a group of seven; and he gives the meaning of the word विश्वेदेव (*viśvedeva*) as follows:

विश्वेदेवास्त्रयोदश विश्वाया अपत्यानि । सर्वे वा देवाः । (*viśvedevāstrayodaśa viśvāyā apatyāni | sarve vā devāḥ |*)
(Bṛ. U. Śaṃ. Bhā. 1-4-12) **NOTE**

He says that there are alternative meanings: one, a company of thirteen gods who are the sons of Viśvā; the other, all the gods. Who this Viśvā is, and how the status of her sons came to the gods, is not easy to say. In the Saṃhitās and the like she is not a very famous person. Only in the Bṛhaddevatā is her name given, in one place:

अदितिर्दितीर्दनुः काला दनायुः सिंहिका मुनिः । क्रोधा विश्वा वरिष्ठा च सुरभिर्विनता तथा । कद्रूश्चैवेति दुहित्याः कश्यपाय ददौ स च ॥ (*aditirditīrdanuḥ kālā danāyuḥ siṃhikā muniḥ | krodhā viśvā variṣṭhā ca surabhirvinatā tathā | kadrūścaiveti duhityāḥ kaśyapāya dadau sa ca ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-14)

Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, had thirteen divine wives. They are: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālā, Danāyu, Siṃhikā, Muni, Krodhā, Viśvā, Variṣṭhā, Surabhi, Vinatā and Kadrū; these were the daughters of Dakṣa. Dakṣa gave these thirteen maidens to Kaśyapa in marriage.

तासु देवासुराश्चैव गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । (*tāsu devāsurāścaiva gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ |*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-145)

From these daughters of Dakṣa arose gods, asuras, gandharvas, serpents, rākṣasas and the rest.

### Printed p. 276
Giving the details that twelve sons were born to Aditi and so on, the text explains the order of birth of Agastya and Vasiṣṭha. In that context:

सर्वत्र पुष्करं तत्र विश्वे देवा आधारयन् । (*sarvatra puṣkaraṃ tatra viśve devā ādhārayan |*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-155)

It says that the Viśvedevas held Vasiṣṭha, who was placed in the pukṣkara (lotus flower). Although Viśvā is said to be Kaśyapa's wife, it is not stated that the Viśvedevas were her sons. But the holding of Vasiṣṭha, who was in the lotus, is also described in the Ṛksaṃhitā:

उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या ब्रह्मन्मनसोऽधि जातः । द्रप्सं स्कन्नं ब्रह्मणा दैन्यन विश्वे देवाः पुष्करे त्वाददंत ॥ (*utāsi maitrāvaruṇo vasiṣṭhorvaśyā brahmanmanaso 'dhi jātaḥ | drapsaṃ skannaṃ brahmaṇā dainyana viśve devāḥ puṣkare tvādadaṃta ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-33-11)

"O Vasiṣṭha, you are the one born of Mitra and Varuṇa from Urvaśī. The Viśvedevas held you, who were in the lotus." Here Sāyaṇa has not said who विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) are. The author of the Nirukta, when giving the purport of this same sentence, says:

सर्वे देवाः त्वाधारयंत । (*sarve devāḥ tvādhārayaṃta |*)
(Ni. 5-14)

Thus he has explained विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) as meaning all the gods.

Only in the Matsya Purāṇa, in one place, is it stated that the Viśvedevas are sons of Viśvā, and that they are ten: Kratu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kālakāma, Muni, Kuraja, Manuja, Vīja and Rocamāna. They are praised as worthy of worship in offerings to gods and ancestors (Matsya 203). The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa states that they received a curse from Viśvāmitra (Mārkaṇḍeya 7). But for now we cannot settle the meaning of Vedic passages on the basis of the Purāṇas.

In Vedic passages the praise of the Viśvedevas is of three kinds. The Bṛhaddevatā states this thus:

वैश्वदेवानि सूक्तानि त्रिविधानि भवंति तु । सूर्यसंस्तवसंयुक्तं विश्वलिंगं पृथक् स्तुति ॥ (*vaiśvadevāni sūktāni trividhāni bhavaṃti tu | sūryasaṃstavasaṃyuktaṃ viśvaliṃgaṃ pṛthak stuti ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-42)

The sūktas that praise and pray to the Viśvedevas are of three kinds. Sūktas that are combined with praises of the Sun belong to the first group. Sūktas that praise all the gods by indicating their common qualities belong to the second group. And, besides, the praising of an individual deity and the extolling of that deity's individual qualities (pṛthak stuti)

### Printed p. 277
belong to the third group.

पृथक् स्तुतीति यत्पोक्तं तद्विद्याद्बहुदैवतं । विश्वलिंगं तु तद्यत्र विश्वैःस्वैः कर्मजैर्गुणैः ॥ (*pṛthak stutīti yatpoktaṃ tadvidyādbahudaivataṃ | viśvaliṃgaṃ tu tadyatra viśvaiḥsvaiḥ karmajairguṇaiḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-43)

Among the three kinds of praise explained in the verse above, (1) combined with praise of the Sun, (2) viśvaliṅga, (3) pṛthak stuti, the pṛthak stuti is the individual praise of many deities. The viśvaliṅga is that which states the common qualities of the gods. Stating the same point in another place, the text explains what viśvaliṅga is:

ऋषिर्देवताः सर्वा विश्वाभिः स्तुतिभिः स्तुताः । संज्ञा तु विश्वमित्येषा सर्वानाप्ता निपातिता ॥ (*ṛṣirdevatāḥ sarvā viśvābhiḥ stutibhiḥ stutāḥ | saṃjñā tu viśvamityeṣā sarvānāptā nipātitā ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 2-139

All the gods have been praised by the seers through praises that are joined together and that describe the qualities of the whole (viśva). The term विश्व (*viśva*) is used in the sense of सर्वानाप्ति (*sarvānāpti*). सर्वानाप्ति (*sarvānāpti*) means comprising everything. According to this term, विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*) means comprising all the gods. This same thing was described above by the term विश्वलिंग (*viśvaliṃga*). The author of the Nirukta, explaining the term विश्वलिंग (*viśvaliṃga*), has also given the view of Śākapūṇi, who says that only the sūktas praising deities, indicated by the word विश्व (*viśva*), are Vaiśvadeva sūktas (Ni. 12-40).

विश्वैः स्वैः कर्मजैर्गुणैः (*viśvaiḥ svaiḥ karmajairguṇaiḥ*) (3-43): it is also stated that the qualities common to the whole are born of the individual acts of the respective gods. In this sense there is no great difference between the two groups of sūktas, viśvaliṅga and pṛthak stuti. How? Explaining what "born of one's own acts" means, the text indicates what the universal qualities born of one's own acts are:

स्तूयंते देवता ह्यासु कर्मभिः स्वैः पृथक् पृथक् । स्तुताः कर्मगुणैः स्वैः स्वैर्देवता यत्र तत्र तु ॥ पृथक्कर्मस्तुतिर्नाम वैश्वदेवं तदेव तु ! (*stūyaṃte devatā hyāsu karmabhiḥ svaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak | stutāḥ karmaguṇaiḥ svaiḥ svairdevatā yatra tatra tu ‖ pṛthakkarmastutirnāma vaiśvadevaṃ tadeva tu !*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-69, 70)

Wherever the gods are praised through the description of their respective individual qualities and through the individual deeds of each deity, there is room for pṛthakkarma-stuti (praise of individual acts). Such praise is Vaiśvadevika.

### Printed p. 278

Third, if we examine what the Vaiśvadeva praise described by the phrase सूरसंस्तवसंयुक्तं (*sūrasaṃstavasaṃyuktaṃ*) actually is, its nature is given as follows.

विश्वानुद्दिश्य यद्देवान् स्तौति सूर्यमनेकधा । देवानेवाभिसंस्तौति तं प्राहुः सूर्यसंस्तवं ॥ (*viśvānuddiśya yaddevān stauti sūryamanekadhā | devānevābhisaṃstauti taṃ prāhuḥ sūryasaṃstavaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-44)

A mantra that, addressed to the Viśvedevas, praises Sūrya at length, and is also chiefly in praise of the deities, is called by the name Sūryasaṃstava. But this rule fails to apply in one or two places. For example:

न तु भागस्य सूक्तादौ सूक्तेष्वेनौषसेषु ना । न सावित्रे ह्वयामीति न सूरायां क्रतौ मखे ॥ (*na tu bhāgasya sūktādau sūkteṣvenauṣaseṣu nā | na sāvitre hvayāmīti na sūrāyāṃ kratau makhe ‖*) (Bṛ. Ve. 3-45) **NOTE**

In the whole Ṛksaṃhitā, in Sūkta 7-41, the only sūkta addressed to Bhaga, many deities are mentioned. But it cannot be a Vaiśvadeva sūkta. In the very first mantra of this sūkta, Indra, Agni and various other deities are praised and prayed to along with Savitṛ. Yet that too is not Vaiśvadeva. The same rule applies to Ṛ. Saṃ. Sūkta 10-85; it is reckoned simply a Sūryā-sūkta. Although it has many deities, all these mantras are not counted as Vaiśvadeva mantras that are useful in sacrificial rites. Similarly,

ह्वयाम्यग्निं प्रथमं स्वस्तये ह्वयामि मित्रावरुणा विहावसे । ह्वयामि रात्रीं जगतो निवेशनीं ह्वयामि देवं सवितारमूतये ॥ (*hvayāmyagniṃ prathamaṃ svastaye hvayāmi mitrāvaruṇā vihāvase | hvayāmi rātrīṃ jagato niveśanīṃ hvayāmi devaṃ savitāramūtaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-1)

In places such as this there are mantras that could be put into the group called Vaiśvadeva, joined with Sūra-saṃstava, and there is praise of other deities along with Savitṛ. But this also is not Vaiśvadeva. Thus many sūktas that seem as if they could belong to the third group do not come under this rule.

In examining such injunctions and prohibitions, one must also know who the deities are that are mentioned incidentally in the Vaiśvadeva sūktas.

देवताविदनेक्षेत प्रयोगे सर्वकर्मणां (*devatāvidanekṣeta prayoge sarvakarmaṇāṃ*) (Bṛ. De. 8-124)

For all rites to attain skill in performance, one must fully know these deities, individual and collective. Who are those deities?

### Printed p. 279

सप्तर्षयो वसवश्चापि देवा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोमसूर्याः । पथ्यास्वस्ती रोदसी चोक्तमंत्रे कुहूर्गुंजूरदितिर्धेनुरघ्न्या ॥ (*saptarṣayo vasavaścāpi devā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somasūryāḥ | pathyāsvastī rodasī coktamaṃtre kuhūrguṃjūraditirdhenuraghnyā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 8-125)

The seven sages, the Vasus, the gods, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, Soma, Sūrya, Pathyā-svasti, the heaven and earth who are subsidiary mantra-deities, Kuhū, Guṃgū, Dhenu and Aghnyā.

असुनितीरिळा चाप्त्या विधातानुमतिर्ह या । अंगिरोभिः सहैताः स्युरुक्तमंत्राश्च देवताः ॥ ( (*asunitīriḷā cāptyā vidhātānumatirha yā | aṃgirobhiḥ sahaitāḥ syuruktamaṃtrāśca devatāḥ ‖ (*) (Bṛ. De. 8-126)

Asunīti, Iḷā, the Āptyas, Vidhātṛ, Anumati together with the Aṅgirases: all these are reckoned as deities of the subsidiary mantras. (The deities mentioned here are praised only rarely. All of them are praised in Vaiśvadeva sūktas.)

वैश्वानरो हि सुपर्णो विवस्वान् प्रजापति दौर्यः सुधन्वा नगोह्यः । अपांनपादर‍्यमा वातजूतिरिळस्पतिश्चापि रथस्पतिष्ण ॥ (*vaiśvānaro hi suparṇo vivasvān prajāpati dauryaḥ sudhanvā nagohyaḥ | apāṃnapādaryamā vātajūtiriḷaspatiścāpi rathaspatiṣṇa ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 8-12)

Vaiśvānara, Suparṇa, Vivasvān, Prajāpati, Dyauḥ, Sudhanvā, Nagohya, Apāṃnapāt, Aryaman, Vātajūti, Iḷaspati and Rathaspati.

ऋभवः पर्जन्यः पर्वता ग्नाश्च दक्षो भगो देवपत्नीर्दिशश्च । आदित्याः रुद्राः पितरोऽथ साध्या निपातिनो वैश्वदेवेषु सर्वॆ ॥ (*ṛbhavaḥ parjanyaḥ parvatā gnāśca dakṣo bhago devapatnīrdiśaśca | ādityāḥ rudrāḥ pitaro 'tha sādhyā nipātino vaiśvadeveṣu sarvè ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 8-128)

The Ṛbhus, Parjanya, the mountains, the female deities, Dakṣa, Bhaga, the wives of the gods, the deities of the quarters, the Ādityas, Rudras, Pitṛs and Sādhyas: all these are deities mentioned incidentally and prayed to in a Vaiśvadeva sūkta.

In answer to the question what Vaiśvadeva sūktas are, the following sentence showing their general characteristic is cited:

अस्तु श्रौषड्वैश्वदेवं तृतीय वैश्वदेवं स्याद्बहुदेवतेषु । (*astu śrauṣaḍvaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīya vaiśvadevaṃ syādbahudevateṣu |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-7)

The general rule is that wherever there is praise addressed to many deities, as seen in sūktas such as अस्यवामस्य पलितस्य (*asyavāmasya palitasya*) (1-164), they are to be determined as Vaiśvadeva sūktas. (The over-extension and non-extension of the rule are explained in the sentences above.)

1-3-7 to 9; 1-14; 123-10 to 12; 1-89; 1-90; 1-105 to 107; 1-122; 1-139-1, 11; 1-164-1 to 41; 1-186; 2-29; 2-31; 2-41-13 to 15; 3-20-1 to 5; 3-54 to 57; 4-55; 5-26-9; 4-41; 5-42-1 to 10, 12 to 18; 5-43 to 45; 5-46-1 to 6; 5-47 to 51; 6-21-9, 11; 6-49 to 52; 7-34-1 to 15, 18 to 25; 7-35 to 37; 7-39; 7-40; 7-42; 7-43; 7-50-3; 8-25-10 to 12; 8-27 to 30; 8-54-3, 4; 8-58-2, 3; 8-69-11; 8-83; 10-31; 10-32; 10-33-1; 10-35; 10-36; 10-56; 10-57; 10-61; 10-62-7; 10-63-1 to 14, 17; 10-64-66; 10-92; 10-93; 10-100; 10-109; 10-114; 10-126; 10-128; 10-137; 10-141; 10-155-5; 10-157; 10-165; 10-181.

Viśvedevas or Agni—9-67-27;
Viśvedevas or Aṅgirases—10-62-1 to 6;
Viśvedevas or Indra—1-121;
Viśvedevas or Ṛtvijas—8-58-1; 10-101;
Viśvedevas or Yūpas—3-8-8.

The names of the seers who, having received the vision of these sūktas, praised and prayed to the Viśvedevas are given in the following sentences:

मेधातिथिरगस्यस्तु बृहदुक्को मनुर्गयः । ऋजिश्वा वसुकर्णश्च शार्यातो गोतमो लुशः ॥ स्वस्तात्रेयः परुच्छेपः कक्षीवान् गाथिनौर्वशौ । नाभाकश्चैव निर्दिष्टो दुवस्युर्ममतासुतः ॥ विहव्यः कश्यप ऋषिरवत्सारश्च नाम यः । वामदेवो मधुच्छंदाः पार्थो दक्षसुतादितिः ॥ जुहूर्ग्नत्समदश्चर्षिर्देवाः सप्तर्षयश्च ये । यनोऽग्निस्तापसः कुत्सः कुसीदी चित्र एव च ॥ बंधुप्रभृतयश्चैव चत्वारो भ्रातरः पृथक् । विष्णुश्च नेजमेषश्च नाम्ना संवननश्च यः । एते तु सर्व एवास्य विश्वैः स्वैः कर्मजैर्गुणैः । समस्तॆरथ च व्यस्थैः पृथक्कूक्तेषु तुष्टुवुः ॥ (*medhātithiragasyastu bṛhadukko manurgayaḥ | ṛjiśvā vasukarṇaśca śāryāto gotamo luśaḥ ‖ svastātreyaḥ parucchepaḥ kakṣīvān gāthinaurvaśau | nābhākaścaiva nirdiṣṭo duvasyurmamatāsutaḥ ‖ vihavyaḥ kaśyapa ṛṣiravatsāraśca nāma yaḥ | vāmadevo madhucchaṃdāḥ pārtho dakṣasutāditiḥ ‖ juhūrgnatsamadaścarṣirdevāḥ saptarṣayaśca ye | yano 'gnistāpasaḥ kutsaḥ kusīdī citra eva ca ‖ baṃdhuprabhṛtayaścaiva catvāro bhrātaraḥ pṛthak | viṣṇuśca nejameṣaśca nāmnā saṃvananaśca yaḥ | ete tu sarva evāsya viśvaiḥ svaiḥ karmajairguṇaiḥ | samastèratha ca vyasthaiḥ pṛthakkūkteṣu tuṣṭuvuḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-55 to 60)

### Printed p. 281

Medhātithi, Agastya, Bṛhaduktha, Manu, Gaya, Ṛjiśvan, Vasukarṇa, Śāryāta, Gotama, Luśa, Svasti Ātreya, Paruchepa, Kakṣīvān, Viśvāmitra the son of Gādhi, Vasiṣṭha the son of Urvaśī, Nābhāka, Duvasya, Dīrghatamas the son of Mamatā, Vihavya, Kaśyapa, Avatsāra, Vāmadeva, Madhuchandas, Pārtha, Aditi the daughter of Dakṣa, Juhū, Gṛtsamada, the seven sages, Yama, Agni, Tāpasa, Kutsa, Kusīdī, Trita, Bandhu and his brothers, Viṣṇu, Nejameṣa and Saṃvanana.

All these seers mentioned above have praised Agni in various ways in separate sūktas.

समस्मैरथ च व्यस्मैः पृथक्कूक्तेषु तुष्टुवुः (*samasmairatha ca vyasmaiḥ pṛthakkūkteṣu tuṣṭuvuḥ*) (Bṛ. De. 3-60)

The description of all the qualities of the god Agni, arising from his manifold actions, is the description of the Viśvedevas. That is, since the various deities are all transformations of Agni, the praise of many deities is the praise of the many qualities of Agni. The meaning is that all the seers named above, in their own individual sūktas, have fully praised only the universal qualities of the god Agni, who has the form of the Viśvedevas. The same idea is stated clearly in some other places too. For example:

आग्नेयं सूक्तमैभिर्यद्वैश्वदेवमिहोच्यते । तद्विश्वलिंगं गायत्रं वैश्वदेवेषु शस्यते ॥ (*āgneyaṃ sūktamaibhiryadvaiśvadevamihocyate | tadviśvaliṃgaṃ gāyatraṃ vaiśvadeveṣu śasyate ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-33)

Although the mantra ऐभिरग्ने (*aibhiragne*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14) is addressed to Agni, it is Viśvedeva-deitied. Because it is composed in the Gāyatrī metre, the mantras of this sūkta have the Viśva characteristic and also praise the universal qualities. Therefore,

यद्वैभिरिति चैतस्मिन् वैश्वदेवेऽग्निमर्चति (*yadvaibhiriti caitasmin vaiśvadeve 'gnimarcati*) (Bṛ. De. 3-51)

the same idea is stated again and again. Moreover, explaining the relation between the Agnihotra and the Viśvedevas, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says:

यो ना अग्निहोत्रं वैश्वदेवं षोळशकलं पशुषु प्रतिष्ठितं वेद वैश्वदेवेनाग्निहोत्रेण षोळशकलेन पशुषु प्रतिष्ठितेन राध्योति ॥ (*yo nā agnihotraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ṣoḷaśakalaṃ paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda vaiśvadevenāgnihotreṇa ṣoḷaśakalena paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitena rādhyoti ‖*) (I. Bo. 5-26) **NOTE**

It praises thus: he who knows that the Agnihotra, having sixteen heads and established in cattle, is Vaiśvadeva, and who performs this Agnihotra whose deities are the Viśvedevas, becomes endowed with wealth such as cattle. Therefore,

### Printed p. 282

यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमासमचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितंच । अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुतमासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान् हिनस्ति ॥ ( (*yasyāgnihotramadarśamapaurṇamāsamacāturmāsyamanāgrayaṇamatithivarjitaṃca | ahutamavaiśvadevamavidhinā hutamāsaptamāṃstasya lokān hinasti ‖ (*) (Maṇḍaka 1-2-3)

If the Agnihotra is without rites such as the Darśa, Paurṇamāsa, Cāturmāsya, Āgrayaṇa and Vaiśvadeva, it damages the man's future even in the seven worlds: thus the excellence of the Vaiśvadeva rite is praised. All the Viśvedevas are contained in Agni, or the forms of all the other deities are transformations of Agni. Therefore the Agnihotra and the Vaiśvadeva rite are related by identity; this can be known from the Vaiśvadeva nivid mantra. Likewise in some other mantras too it is stated clearly that the Viśvedevas are contained in Agni. For example:

त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः । तै विश्वे सहसस्पुत्र देवास्त मिंद्रो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥ (*tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ | tai viśve sahasasputra devāsta miṃdro dāśuṣe martyāya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1)

O Agni, you are Varuṇa, you are Mitra, and in you all the Viśvedevas are contained. They all live by the offering made in you. The offering made to you is to reach them as well, and what is offered to them all is to reach you; such is the praise. But who are they? How many are they? This is told in the Vaiśvadeva nivid mantra.

त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् । औक्षन् घृतैरस्तृणन्बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्दोतारं न्यसादयंत ॥ (*trīṇi śatā trī sahasrāṇyagniṃ triṃśacca devā nava cāsaparyan | aukṣan ghṛtairastṛṇanbarhirasmā ādiddotāraṃ nyasādayaṃta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-9)

This is reckoned to be the Vaiśvadeva nivid mantra. In it the number of the deities is stated. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka gives its explanation as the number of the Viśvedevas. Explaining the number of all these deities contained in Agni, it says:

अथ हैनं विदग्धः शाकल्यः पप्रच्छ कति देवा याज्ञवल्क्येति स हैतय्येव निविदा प्रतिपेदे यावंतो वैश्वदेवस्य निविदुच्यंते त्रयश्च त्री च शता त्रयश्च त्री च सहस्रेत्योमिति ॥ (*atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha kati devā yājñavalkyeti sa haitayyeva nividā pratipede yāvaṃto vaiśvadevasya nividucyaṃte trayaśca trī ca śatā trayaśca trī ca sahasretyomiti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-1)

In the commentary on the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-9 quoted above, Sāyaṇa has cited and explained this Upaniṣad sentence. Here there is the conversation between Vidagdha Śākalya and Yājñavalkya on the numbers of the deities.

### Printed p. 283

Vidagdha Śākalya: O Yājñavalkya, what is the total number of the gods? Yājñavalkya: The number stated in the Viśvedeva nivid mantra is the number of the Viśvedevas, namely three hundred and three, and three thousand and three. In all, three thousand three hundred and six. But this number differs slightly from the number stated elsewhere. According to that, 11 × 3 = 33 must be added; that is, a total of three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine. This is the number of the Viśvedevas contained in Agni. The worship of these Viśvedevas is the worship of Agni, and the worship of Agni is the worship of the Viśvedevas.

If saying that the Viśvedevas are contained in Agni is one manner in such descriptions, there are also some passages in which the Viśvedevas are described as consisting of the five peoples. In such contexts the five peoples are the gods, humans, Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Pitṛs; this is explained in the Vaiśvadeva śastra section thus:

पांचजन्यं वा एतदुक्थं यद्वैश्वदेवं सर्वॆषां वा एतत्पंचजनानामुक्थं देवमनुष्याणां गंधर्वाप्सरसां सर्पाणां च पितृणां चैतेषां वा एतत्पंचजनानामुक्थं सर्व एनं पंचजना विदुः ॥ (*pāṃcajanyaṃ vā etadukthaṃ yadvaiśvadevaṃ sarvèṣāṃ vā etatpaṃcajanānāmukthaṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ sarpāṇāṃ ca pitṛṇāṃ caiteṣāṃ vā etatpaṃcajanānāmukthaṃ sarva enaṃ paṃcajanā viduḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 3-31)

The Vaiśvadeva rite is Pāñcajanya, that is, it concerns the five groups of people: gods, humans, Gandharvas, Apsarases and Pitṛs. One who knows this principle is skilled in this rite; thus there is praise of the Vaiśvadeva rite and a description of the Viśvedevas. Other contexts that praise the greatness of this rite will be given later.

Thus it is one setting that the Viśvedevas are contained in Agni, who is made of all the deities; it is another setting that all beings, gods, humans and the rest, are contained in the Viśvedevas. Besides these, a third kind of description is also well known in Vedic sentences: that the Viśvedevas are a power-designation showing the distinction of the varṇas in the order of creation. According to this description Agni, Indra and the Viśvedevas are three special deities reflecting three varṇas. The arrangement of sūktas in the Ṛksaṃhitā also suggests this. Except in the eighth and ninth maṇḍalas, in all the other maṇḍalas there are, at the beginning, sūktas in praise of Agni, then in praise of Indra; after that, sūktas generally in praise of the Viśvedevas follow. Later, in the Brāhmaṇas and the like, Agni, Indra and the Viśvedevas are shown to be identical respectively with the three varṇas, Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya and Vaiśya. Some examples make this clear.

### Printed p. 284

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रजापतिर्वाव ज्येष्ठस्स ह्येतेनाग्रेऽयजत प्रजापतिरकामयत प्र जायेयेति स मुखतस्त्रिवृतं निरमिमीत तमग्निर्देवतान्नसृजत गायत्रीच्छंदो रथतरग्‌ंसाम ब्राह्मणो मनुष्याणामजः पशूनां ॥ (*prajāpatirvāva jyeṣṭhassa hyetenāgre 'yajata prajāpatirakāmayata pra jāyeyeti sa mukhatastrivṛtaṃ niramimīta tamagnirdevatānnasṛjata gāyatrīcchaṃdo rathataragṃsāma brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇāmajaḥ paśūnāṃ ‖*) (Śai. Saṃ. 7-1-1-4) **NOTE**

Because he was the first of all to perform the sacrificial rite, Prajāpati himself is the foremost. Then he wished: "May I obtain offspring." Then he brought forth the Trivṛt from his mouth. From it arose the deity Agni, the Gāyatrī metre, the Rathantara Sāman, the Brāhmaṇas among men, and the goat among animals. Since they arose from the mouth, all of them obtained pre-eminence.

उरसो बाहुभ्यां पंचदशं निरमिमीत तमिंद्रो देवतान्नसृज्यत त्रिष्टुप्छंदो बृहत् साम राजन्यो मनुष्याणामविः पशूनां तस्मात्ते वीर्यावंतो वीर्याद्ध्यसृज्यंत ॥ (*uraso bāhubhyāṃ paṃcadaśaṃ niramimīta tamiṃdro devatānnasṛjyata triṣṭupchaṃdo bṛhat sāma rājanyo manuṣyāṇāmaviḥ paśūnāṃ tasmātte vīryāvaṃto vīryāddhyasṛjyaṃta ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-1-4, 5)

From the chest and the arms he brought forth the Pañcadaśa. From it arose the deity Indra, the Triṣṭup metre, the Bṛhat Sāman, the Kṣatriyas among men, and the sheep among animals. Since they were born of the valour of the arm, all of them became indicative of valour.

मध्यतस्सप्तदशं निरमिमीत तं विश्वेदेवा देवता अन्वसृज्यंत जगती छंदो वैरूपग्‌ंसाम वैश्यो मनुष्याणां गावः पशूनां तस्मात्त आद्या अन्नधानाद्दस्यृज्यंत तस्माद्भूयाग्‌ंसोऽन्येभ्यो भूयिष्ठा हि देवता अन्वसृज्यंत ॥ (*madhyatassaptadaśaṃ niramimīta taṃ viśvedevā devatā anvasṛjyaṃta jagatī chaṃdo vairūpagṃsāma vaiśyo manuṣyāṇāṃ gāvaḥ paśūnāṃ tasmātta ādyā annadhānāddasyṛjyaṃta tasmādbhūyāgṃso 'nyebhyo bhūyiṣṭhā hi devatā anvasṛjyaṃta ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-1-5)

Then from his middle part he brought forth the Saptadaśa Stoma. From it the Viśvedevas arose. Among metres the Jagatī, among Sāmans the Vairūpa, among the people the Vaiśyas, and among animals the cows arose. Since all these arose from the store of food, they became endowed with abundance of food and fit for enjoyment. Since they are related to the Viśvedevas, their numbers too became exceedingly great. Thus, beginning thus, the order of origin of Agni, Indra and the Viśvedevas, and the varieties of their powers, are set forth. The same matter is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as stated below.

क्षत्रं वा इंद्राग्नी । विशो विश्वेदेवा यत्र वै क्षत्रमुज्जयत्यन्वाभक्ता वै तत्र विड्वद्विश्वान्देवानन्वाभजतां तस्मादेष वैश्वदेवश्चरुर्भवति ॥ (*kṣatraṃ vā iṃdrāgnī | viśo viśvedevā yatra vai kṣatramujjayatyanvābhaktā vai tatra viḍvadviśvāndevānanvābhajatāṃ tasmādeṣa vaiśvadevaścarurbhavati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-4-3-6)

### Printed p. 285
Indra and Agni are of the nature of the warrior class; the Viśvedevas are of the nature of the Vaiśyas. Wherever the Kṣatriyas win victory, there the Vaiśyas too obtain a share. Therefore it is said that the Viśvedevas also take part in the victory of Indra and Agni. This division of the classes may be said in one way to exist naturally. For Agni, in the form of the sacrificial fire, in the role of priest, invites the gods to the sacrifice, carries the oblation to the gods, and fosters the relation between gods and men. Sharp radiance and brilliance are likewise marks of the Brāhmaṇa. Indra, who always fights the Asuras and others and gains victory, has the natural warrior power. Just as, apart from these, the remaining people are called Vaiśyas, so the other deities apart from Indra and Agni belong to the Vaiśya group. In this division it is understood that the Viśvedevas are different from Indra and Agni, and that their radiance or valour is not as great as theirs. According to this division the shares are also apportioned in the three Savanas. This order of division can be seen in the Saṃhitā and Brāhmaṇa passages.

प्रजापतिर्वै यज्ञं छंदासि देवेभ्यो भागधेयानि व्यभजत्स गायत्रीमेवाग्नये वसुभ्यः प्रातःसवनेऽभजत्रिष्टुभमिंद्राय रुद्रेभ्यो मध्यंदिने जगतीं विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्य आदित्येभ्यस्तृतीयसवने ॥ (*prajāpatirvai yajñaṃ chaṃdāsi devebhyo bhāgadheyāni vyabhajatsa gāyatrīmevāgnaye vasubhyaḥ prātaḥsavane 'bhajatriṣṭubhamiṃdrāya rudrebhyo madhyaṃdine jagatīṃ viśvebhyo devebhya ādityebhyastṛtīyasavane ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 3-13)

Prajāpati distributed the sacrificial portions and the metres among the gods: in the morning Savana the Gāyatrī to Agni and the Vasus; in the midday Savana the Triṣṭup to Indra and the Rudras; in the third Savana the Jagatī to the Viśvedevas and the Ādityas. The same topic is somewhat different in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, as follows.

अथ प्रातः । आग्नेयः पुरोडाशो भवत्यैंद्रग्ं सांनाय्यं प्रातःसवनमेवास्याग्नेयः पुरोडाश आग्नेयग्ं हि प्रातःसवनमध्यैंद्रग्ं सांनाय्यं माध्यंदिनमेवास्य तत्वनमैंद्रग्ं हि माध्यंदिनग्ं सवनं ॥ (*atha prātaḥ | āgneyaḥ puroḍāśo bhavatyaiṃdragṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ prātaḥsavanamevāsyāgneyaḥ puroḍāśa āgneyagṃ hi prātaḥsavanamadhyaiṃdragṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ mādhyaṃdinamevāsya tatvanamaiṃdragṃ hi mādhyaṃdinagṃ savanaṃ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-4-12)

In the morning the Āgneya Puroḍāśa and the Sāṃnāyya for Indra are offered. The morning Savana is dear to Agni; likewise the midday Savana is dear to Indra.

अथ यत्पूर्वेद्युः । ऐंद्राग्नेन यजतेऽमावास्यायां तृतीयसवनमेवास्य तद्वैश्वदेवं वै तृतीयसवनमिंद्राग्नी वै विश्वेदेवाः ॥ (*atha yatpūrvedyuḥ | aiṃdrāgnena yajate 'māvāsyāyāṃ tṛtīyasavanamevāsya tadvaiśvadevaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanamiṃdrāgnī vai viśvedevāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-4-4-13)

### Printed p. 286
The Puroḍāśa connected with Indra and Agni, offered on the new-moon day, is the third Savana, directed to the Viśvedevas. In this passage, where Indra and Agni are described as the Viśvedevas, the identity of Indra and Agni with the Viśvedevas is shown.

Besides this, a historical occasion showing that the Viśvedevas have pre-eminence in the third Savana is described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows.

देवा वै यज्ञमतन्वत तांस्तन्वानानसुरा अभ्यायन् यज्ञवेशसमेषां करिष्याम इति..................ते वै पुरस्तादपहता असुराः पश्चात्परीत्य प्राविशंस्ते देवाः प्रतिबुद्ध्य विश्वान्नेवानात्मानं पश्चात्तृतीयसवने पत्याहंस्ते विश्वैरेव देवैरात्मभिः पश्चात्तृतीयसवनेऽसुररक्षांस्यपाघ्नत तथैवैतद्यजमाना विश्वैरेव देवैरात्मभिः पश्चात्तृतीयसवनेऽसुररक्षांस्यपाघ्नते तस्माद्वैश्वदेवं तृतीयसवनं ॥ (*devā vai yajñamatanvata tāṃstanvānānasurā abhyāyan yajñaveśasameṣāṃ kariṣyāma iti..................te vai purastādapahatā asurāḥ paścātparītya prāviśaṃste devāḥ pratibuddhya viśvānnevānātmānaṃ paścāttṛtīyasavane patyāhaṃste viśvaireva devairātmabhiḥ paścāttṛtīyasavane 'surarakṣāṃsyapāghnata tathaivaitadyajamānā viśvaireva devairātmabhiḥ paścāttṛtīyasavane 'surarakṣāṃsyapāghnate tasmādvaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 6-4)

When the gods strove to perform the sacrifice, the Asuras entered, striving "We shall cause obstruction to it." Then in the morning Savana, with the help of Mitra and Varuṇa, they drove away the Asuras who had entered from the south. Indra became the guardian of the middle part, and Indra and Agni together became the guardians of the northern quarter. Agni became the guardian of the front. The Asuras, who had no opening for entry at the front, began to enter from behind. Then the gods appointed the Viśvedevas in the third Savana as protectors there, and with their help drove away the Asuras entering from behind. Therefore the Viśvedevas have pre-eminence in the third Savana. One who knows this principle becomes able to drive away the Asuras.

Thus, while in the Brāhmaṇas and the like the order is Agni, Indra, Viśvedevas, in the Upaniṣads the order is Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas and Viśvedevas. As follows—

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति यद्वसूनां प्रातःसवनं रुद्राणां माध्यंदिनं सवनमादित्यानां च विश्वेषां च देवानां तृतीयसवनं ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti yadvasūnāṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ rudrāṇāṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ ‖*) (Chā. U. 2-24-1)

The knowers of Brahman have declared that the morning Savana is prescribed for the Vasus, the midday Savana for the Rudras, and the third Savana for the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas.

अथ जुहोति नम आदित्येभ्यश्च विश्वेभ्यश्च देवेभ्यो दिविक्षिद्भ्यो लोकक्षिद्भ्यो लोकं मे यजमानाय विंदत ॥ (*atha juhoti nama ādityebhyaśca viśvebhyaśca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyo lokaṃ me yajamānāya viṃdata ‖*) (Bhā. U. 2-24-15) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 287
तस्मा आदित्याश्च विश्वे च देवास्त्रीयसवनं संप्रयच्छंत्येष ह वै यज्ञस्य मात्रां वेद य एवं वेद (*tasmā ādityāśca viśve ca devāstrīyasavanaṃ saṃprayacchaṃtyeṣa ha vai yajñasya mātrāṃ veda ya evaṃ veda*) (Bhā. U. 2-24-16)

Then: salutation to the Ādityas; salutation to the Viśvedevas; salutation to the gods who dwell in the atmosphere and on the earth. When he prays, "Prepare a world for me, the sacrificer, to dwell in," the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas favour him with the third Savana.

In the sacrificial periods of the Pṛṣṭha Ṣaḍaha as well, in the same order, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes Agni, Indra and the Viśvedevas as having pre-eminence on the first, second and third days.

(1) अग्निर्वै देवता प्रथममहर्वहति त्रिवृत्स्तोमो रथंतरं साम गायत्रीच्छंदः ॥ (*agnirvai devatā prathamamaharvahati trivṛtstomo rathaṃtaraṃ sāma gāyatrīcchaṃdaḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 4-29)

(2) इंद्रो वै देवता द्वितीयमहर्वहति पंचदशस्तोमो बृहत्साम त्रिष्टुप्छंदः ॥ (*iṃdro vai devatā dvitīyamaharvahati paṃcadaśastomo bṛhatsāma triṣṭupchaṃdaḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 4-31)

(3) विश्वे वै देवा देवतास्त्रीयमहर्वहंति सप्तदशः स्तोमो वैरूपं साम जगतीच्छंदः ॥ (*viśve vai devā devatāstrīyamaharvahaṃti saptadaśaḥ stomo vairūpaṃ sāma jagatīcchaṃdaḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 5-1)

In the Pṛṣṭha Ṣaḍahas, on the first day the deity Agni is joined with the Trivṛt Stoma, the Rathantara Sāman and the Gāyatrī metre. On the second day the deity Indra is joined with the Pañcadaśa Stoma, the Bṛhat Sāman and the Triṣṭup metre. On the third day the Viśvedevas are joined with the Saptadaśa Stoma, the Vairūpa Sāman and the Jagatī metre; thus the third place is assigned to the Viśvedevas. In this way the views expressed on the position and rank of the Viśvedevas are given. But since these same Viśvedevas reflect various principles, they are described in many ways in many places. Only some of them may be taken here as examples.

इमे वै प्राणाः । मनोज्ञाता मनोयुजो दक्षक्रतवो नागेवाग्निः प्राणोदान् मित्रावरुणौ चक्षुरादित्यः श्रोत्रं विश्वेदेवाः ॥ (*ime vai prāṇāḥ | manojñātā manoyujo dakṣakratavo nāgevāgniḥ prāṇodān mitrāvaruṇau cakṣurādityaḥ śrotraṃ viśvedevāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-13)

These vital breaths, endowed with life, are born of the mind. Agni is speech; Mitra and Varuṇa are the in-breath and out-breath. Āditya is the principle of the eye. The Viśvedevas are the principle of the organ of hearing.

### Printed p. 288
वैश्वदेवं ना अंतरिक्षं तद्यदेनेनेमाः प्रजाः प्राणत्यश्चोदानत्यश्चांशरिक्ष मनुचरंति तेन वैश्वदेवं वषट्कृते जुहोति ॥ (*vaiśvadevaṃ nā aṃtarikṣaṃ tadyadenenemāḥ prajāḥ prāṇatyaścodānatyaścāṃśarikṣa manucaraṃti tena vaiśvadevaṃ vaṣaṭkṛte juhoti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-8-2-32)

Because they are the means of the travelling of sound connected with the organ of hearing, and because all beings act in the atmosphere itself by means of in-breath and out-breath, the Viśvedevas, who are the presiding deities of all these, are the reflectors of the principle of the atmosphere.

एतस्मै वै गृह्णाति य एष तपति विश्वेभ्यो ह्येना देवेभ्यो गृह्णाति रश्मयो ह्यस्य विश्वे देवास्तस्मादाह हविष्ठा अस्तु सूर‍्य इति ॥ (*etasmai vai gṛhṇāti ya eṣa tapati viśvebhyo hyenā devebhyo gṛhṇāti raśmayo hyasya viśve devāstasmādāha haviṣṭhā astu sūrya iti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-9-2-12)

All oblations offered to Sūrya are as if offered to the Viśvedevas. For all the rays of the sun are forms of the principle of the Viśvedevas. Therefore the sun's rays, the objects of movement, and the atmosphere, the means of movement, are the very symbols of the Viśvedevas. For this reason they are also said to be the makers of the quarters.

विश्वेदेवाः वैश्वानरा दिशः कृत्वा तास्वेतामाशिषमाशासत । (*viśvedevāḥ vaiśvānarā diśaḥ kṛtvā tāsvetāmāśiṣamāśāsata |*) (Śa. Brā. 6-5-2-6)

The Viśvedevas created all the quarters and blessed them. Since they are the presiding deities of the quarters and of the atmosphere pervading them, they are described as the regulators of the seasons and the like, and accordingly as the producers of rain.

ऋतवो वै विश्वेदेवास्तदेनां विश्वैर्देवैर्युतुभिः संविदानः । (*ṛtavo vai viśvedevāstadenāṃ viśvairdevairyutubhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 7-1-1-43)

विश्वेच वै देवा मरुतश्च वर्षस्येशत ऊर्जस्वती । (*viśveca vai devā marutaśca varṣasyeśata ūrjasvatī |*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-2-10)

By such sentences their all-pervasiveness and exceeding power are praised. Because of such exceeding power, praise of them is found:

विश्वे वै देवा देवानां यशस्वितमा यश एवास्मिन्धधाति (*viśve vai devā devānāṃ yaśasvitamā yaśa evāsmindhadhāti*) (Śa. Brā. 13-1-2-8)

Among all the gods the Viśvedevas are the most renowned, and similar laudatory sentences. Thus, in some places showing their identity with Indra and Agni, and in others describing their individual nature, they are praised in many ways. If all these descriptions are examined,

### Printed p. 289
one may say on the whole that the Viśvedevas are deities who reflect all the powers in the universe; or that the Brahman-nature itself, which contains all principles, is what is meant by the Viśvedeva deity. As follows—

तद्वै तत्पश्यन्नृषिरभ्यनूनाद । भूतं भविष्यत्प्रस्तौमि महद्ब्रह्मैकमक्षरं बहु ब्रह्मैकमक्षरमित्येतद्ध्येवाक्षरग्ं सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतान्यभिसंपद्यंते तदेतद्ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं चाग्निरेव ब्रह्मेंद्रः क्षत्रमिंद्राग्नी वै विश्वेदेवा विडु विश्वेदेवास्तदेतद्ब्रह्म क्षत्रं विट् ॥ (*tadvai tatpaśyannṛṣirabhyanūnāda | bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyatprastaumi mahadbrahmaikamakṣaraṃ bahu brahmaikamakṣaramityetaddhyevākṣaragṃ sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhisaṃpadyaṃte tadetadbrahma ca kṣatraṃ cāgnireva brahmeṃdraḥ kṣatramiṃdrāgnī vai viśvedevā viḍu viśvedevāstadetadbrahma kṣatraṃ viṭ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-9)

This is a saying of a seer who obtained the vision of the great principle: "I praise that which was in past times and will be in future, the great, the imperishable, the manifold Brahman." All the gods and all beings are absorbed in this principle. This is the form of Brahman, this is the form of Kṣatra: Agni is the exponent of the power of Brahman, Indra the exponent of the power of Kṣatra; the Viśvedevas are Indra and Agni. But the Viśvedevas are also the exponents of the power of the Vaiśya; therefore this principle, which contains everything, is the source of all these powers: Brahman, Kṣatra and Viś.

**Deities to be praised occasionally in the Vaiśvadeva hymns**

**Hymns 41–46 of the fifth Maṇḍala**

Who are the Viśvedevas? Whether this is a single group, or the complete assembly of all deities, has been discussed in the preliminary introduction to Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41. Even if one accepts the view that the company of deities named in the Vaiśvadeva hymns is a separate one, other deities too who are praised incidentally are included in those hymns besides the deities of that group. Concerning who these occasional deities are, the Bṛhaddevatā has a whole section. This subject will be explained in detail later. For the present, however, it is stated who these deities praised occasionally are. In the Bṛhaddevatā, enumerating these occasional deities beginning with सप्तर्षयो वसवश्चापि देवाः (*saptarṣayo vasavaścāpi devāḥ*) (Bṛ. De. 8-125), it concludes with निपातिनो वैश्वदेवेषु सर्वॆ (*nipātino vaiśvadeveṣu sarvè*) (8-128). They are:

The seven seers, the Vasus, the Atharvans who are of divine nature, the Bhṛgus, Soma, Sūra, Pathyā Svasti, Heaven and Earth, Kuhū, Gungū, Aditi, Dhenu, Aghnyā, Asunīti, Iḷā, the Āptyas, Vidhātṛ, Anumati, the assembled Aṅgirases, Vaiśvānara, Suparṇa, Vivasvat, Prajāpati, Dyaus, Sudhanvan, Nagohya, Apāṃ Napāt, Aramyan, Vātajūti, Iḷaspati, Rathaspati, the Ṛbhus, Parjanya, the mountains,

### Printed p. 290
Gnā, Dakṣa, Bhaga, the wives of the gods, the deities of the directions, the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Pitṛs and the Sādhyas. (Bṛ. De. 8-125 to 128)

If all the deities in this group are occasional (naimittika) deities, then to settle who the constant (nitya) deities are also becomes laborious. Deities such as Agni, Soma and Bṛhaspati are regularly praised in all the Vaiśvadeva sūktas. In speaking of the deities included in this section, that is, in the sūktas (5-41 to 46), the Bṛhaddevatā names only some of the deities. So one question is whether all the deities named there may be taken as occasional deities in these sūktas. Secondly, Yāska and others have shown a variety of opinion even about which deity is precisely praised in some mantras. It is like this.

प्र सुष्टुतिः स्तनयंतं रुवंतमिळस्वंतं जरितर्नूनमश्याः । यो अब्बिमा उदनिमा इयर्ति प्र विद्युता रोदसी उक्षमाणः ॥ (*pra suṣṭutiḥ stanayaṃtaṃ ruvaṃtamiḷasvaṃtaṃ jaritarnūnamaśyāḥ | yo abbimā udanimā iyarti pra vidyutā rodasī ukṣamāṇaḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-14)

In this mantra there is praise of Iḷaspati. There is no settled opinion at all about who this Iḷaspati is. Sāyaṇa has explained इळः अन्नस्य उदकस्य ना पतिं स्वामिनं (*iḷaḥ annasya udakasya nā patiṃ svāminaṃ*) as "Parjanya, the lord of food or water". This is one view. The view of Yāska and others is given in the Bṛhaddevatā as follows:

तमुष्टुहीति रौद्री तु प्र सुष्टुतिरिति त्वृचि । शौनकादिभिराचार्यैर्देवता बहुधेरिता । (*tamuṣṭuhīti raudrī tu pra suṣṭutiriti tvṛci | śaunakādibhirācāryairdevatā bahudheritā |*)

इळस्पतिं शाकपूणिः पर्जन्याग्नी तु गालवः ॥ यास्कस्तु पूषणं मेने स्तुतमिंद्रं तु शौनकः । वैश्वानरं भागुरिस्तु मारुत्येष समाश्विनौ ॥ (*iḷaspatiṃ śākapūṇiḥ parjanyāgnī tu gālavaḥ ‖ yāskastu pūṣaṇaṃ mene stutamiṃdraṃ tu śaunakaḥ | vaiśvānaraṃ bhāguristu mārutyeṣa samāśvinau ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 5-38 to 40)

As to who the deity named in the mantra quoted above is, Śaunaka and others have shown a variety of opinions. Śākapūṇi called it Iḷaspati; Gālava said Parjanya-Agni; Yāska said the god Pūṣan; Śaunaka held it to be Indra; Bhāguri said Vaiśvānara. Such is the variety of opinion. Likewise,

तं प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा ज्येष्ठतातिं बर्हिषदं स्वर्विदं । प्रतीचीनं वृजनं दोहसे गिराशुं जयंतमनु यासु वर्धसे ॥ (*taṃ pratnathā pūrvathā viśvathemathā jyeṣṭhatātiṃ barhiṣadaṃ svarvidaṃ | pratīcīnaṃ vṛjanaṃ dohase girāśuṃ jayaṃtamanu yāsu vardhase ‖*)

(Bṛ. Saṃ. 5-44-1) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 291
In this mantra Sāyaṇa has said that तं (*taṃ*) means Indra, i.e. that there is praise of Indra. But the author of the Bṛhaddevatā, without stating precisely who the deity praised in this mantra is, has shown many alternatives.

तं प्रत्नथेति सौमी ना दैन्यैंद्री ना प्रजापतेः । परोक्षवैश्वदेवं तदाह कौषीतकिः स्वयं ॥ (*taṃ pratnatheti saumī nā dainyaiṃdrī nā prajāpateḥ | parokṣavaiśvadevaṃ tadāha kauṣītakiḥ svayaṃ ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 5-44)

The deity indicated in the mantra तं प्रत्नथा (*taṃ pratnathā*) may be Soma, or some other particular deity, or Indra; or if not that, Prajāpati may be the one indicated: thus the first half gives alternative meanings. In the second half, stating the opinion of the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, it cites the sentence spoken by Kauṣītaki, "In this mantra the Viśvedevas themselves are indicated indirectly" (Kau. Brā. 24-9). **NOTE**

Thus, when there is no settled opinion even about the deity indicated in many mantras, it becomes laborious to determine in the present section (5-41-46) who are the constant deities and who the occasional deities that belong to the Vaiśvadeva group.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रनेति षडृचं दशमं सूक्तं सौचीकस्याग्नेरार्षं वैश्वदेवं॥
> गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ सुग्रादापनात्पूर्वभाविनि जपे विनियुक्ता । सूत्रितं च । विश्वे
> देवाः शास्त्रन मा यथेहाराधि होता निषदा यजीयान् । आ. १-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth sūkta, विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रन (*viśve devāḥ śāstrana*), of six ṛks, has as its seer Agni, called Saucīka; its deity is the Viśvedevas (Vaiśvadeva). The use of the sūkta has been stated already. It is employed in the japa that precedes taking up the ladle (sruk). It is also laid down in the sūtra beginning विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रन (*viśve devāḥ śāstrana*) (Ā. Sū. 1-4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, विश्वेदेवाः शास्त्रन (*viśvedevāḥ śāstrana*), is the tenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Its seer is Agni, named Saucīka; its deity is the Viśvedevas. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier. The use of this sūkta is in the japa performed before taking up the wooden ladle called sruk for the ājya-homa; it is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रन मा यथेहाराधि होता निषदा यजीयान् (*viśve devāḥ śāstrana mā yathehārādhi hotā niṣadā yajīyān*) (Ā. 1-4).

Sūkta 52
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 52.
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 1; Varga 12.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6.
Ṛṣi: Agni Sācīka. **NOTE**
Devatā: the Gods.
Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The whole sūkta is addressed to Agni. "O Viśvedevas, you, मा (*mā*), to me, शास्त्रन (*śāstrana*), give permission. Declare my share (भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*)), declare it as you have fixed the share, and the path by which I may carry the oblation to you; I perform the carrying."

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजीयान् यष्टृतमोऽहं होता सन्न सीदं । निषण्णोऽस्मि । निषदने
> तं निषण्णं विश्वे व्याप्ता मरुतो देवा जुनंति । प्रेरयंति हविर्वहनाय । हे

> भवद्भ्यामनुज्ञातव्यमित्यर्थः । ब्रह्मा भवति भवतु । कः समित् समिद्धश्चंद्रमाः।
> चंद्रमा ब्रह्मा भवतु । किंच सा । स इत्यर्थः । स च समित् समिद्धश्चंद्रमा वां युवयोर्होमार्थं वां युवाभ्यां क्रियमाणायाध्वरवकर्मण आहुतिर्भवत्त्वर्थः । सोमात्मको हि चंद्रमा हूयते । एष वै सोमो
> राजेत्युपक्रम्य तदेवोभयं भवतीति हि च्छंदोगब्राह्मणं । अथवैवं योजना।
> याहुतिराध्वर्यवमनुष्ठितवद्भ्यां होतव्या सा वां युवयोर्युवाभ्यां भवति।
> भवतु। अध्वर्यवं नामित्यस्यैव विवरणमेतत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I, यजीयान् (*yajīyān*), the one most fit to sacrifice, have sat down as hotṛ. To me thus seated, all, i.e. pervading, Maruts, the gods, give impulse (जुनंति (*junaṃti*)), urge me to carry the oblation. O Aśvins, your adhvaryu-office is to be performed day by day" ("is to be performed" is to be supplied): that is, the adhvaryu-office is to be permitted by you. "Let there be a Brahmā. Who? समित् (*samit*), the kindled moon; let the moon be Brahmā. And सा (*sā*), that is, he: that kindled moon is to be your oblation for the adhvara rite performed by you." For the moon, being of Soma's nature, is offered; the Chāndogya Brāhmaṇa says, beginning एष वै सोमो राजेत्युपक्रम्य तदेवोभयं भवतीति (*eṣa vai somo rājetyupakramya tadevobhayaṃ bhavatīti*). Or else the construction is this: the oblation that is to be offered by the two who have performed the adhvaryu-office, let that be yours. This is only an explanation of अध्वर्यवं (*adhvaryavaṃ*) नां (*nāṃ*). **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, worthy of sacrifice, am seated as hotṛ. All the Maruts and gods, or all the Maruts who are divine in nature, urge me to carry the oblation. O Aśvin deities, the work of the adhvaryu is to be performed by you every day. Let Soma be in the place of Brahmā. Let that same Soma be the oblation for you.

##### English translation
Best entitled to the sacrifice, I have sat down as the Hotri : all the divine Maruts urge me (to bear the oblation) : the office of the Adhwaryu is to be discharged daily, Ashwins, by you : let the moon be the Brahman, and let it be also your oblation.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"This one who is the hotṛ, स किः (*sa kiḥ*): who is he, of what sort is he, what is his function?" The answer is given: afraid of Yama, that is of death (this is to be supplied), he carries some offering.

### Printed p. 295

> मूहे । वहति । यद्वा । सर्वमृत्विग्जातं नियमयतीति यमो यजमानः । तस्य
> कमपि हुतमूहे। वहति देवान्प्रति । यत्समंजंति यद्धविः प्राप्नुवंति देवाः ।
> किंचाग्निरहरहः प्रतिदिनमग्निहोत्रार्थं जायते । प्रादुर्भवति । तथा मासिमासि
> प्रतिमासं जायते पितृयज्ञार्थं । एतत्कालद्वयमुपलक्षणं पक्षचतुर्मासषण्माससंवत्सरादीनां । अपरे पुनरेवमाहुः । अहरहः सूर्यात्मना जायते मासि मासि
> चंद्रात्मनेति । अथ तमिममग्निं देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहं । हविषां वोढारं । एवमग्निरात्मानं स्वयमेवोक्तवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऊहे (*ūhe*) means "bears". Or else: Yama is the sacrificer, who controls the whole group of ṛtviks; he carries some offering of his to the gods, which the gods receive (यत्समंजंति (*yatsamaṃjaṃti*)). Moreover Agni is born each day for the agnihotra, appears; so too he is born every month for the pitṛyajña. These two times are indicative of the fortnight, the four-month period, the six-month period, the year and so on. Others say: he is born day by day as the sun, month by month as the moon. Then the gods held this Agni, the bearer of oblations, the carrier of the offerings. Thus Agni has spoken of himself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः अयं होता (*yaḥ ayaṃ hotā*)—he who is this hotṛ
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- किः (*kiḥ*)—who? what is his nature?
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of the sacrificer who keeps the ṛtviks under control
- यत् (*yat*)—which oblation
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- समंजंति (*samaṃjaṃti*)—receive; such
- कमपि (*kamapi*)—all oblations
- ऊहे (*ūhe*)—he carries
- (Agni)
- अहरहः (*aharahaḥ*)—every day
- जायते (*jāyate*)—is born
- मासिमासि (*māsimāsi*)—every month is born
- अथ (*atha*)—therefore
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—the messenger who carries the oblation
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—hold (honour) and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

What is the nature of this Agni who is the hotṛ? Agni carries all those oblations of the sacrificer which the gods receive. This same Agni is born every day. Therefore the gods hold (honour) and worship the messenger who is the bearer of oblations.

##### English translation
Who is this, who is the Hotri ? (Afraid) of Yama, what offering does he bear that the gods accept ? Agni is born day by day; and month by month, and so the gods have made for themselves a bearer of oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अहरहः (*aharahaḥ*)—every day; the rite called agnihotra has to be performed every day. Because Agni is produced or worshipped every day for it, it is said here that Agni is born every day. Likewise मासिमासि (*māsimāsi*)—every month: since the sacrifices such as the darśapūrṇamāsa are performed in every month, and for them it is prescribed that Agni be produced by churning in the araṇis at every sacrifice, it is explained here that Agni is born in every month.
