> स्तुतिभिर्विस्कृतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods have made me, Agni, हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*), the bearer of oblations. Sāyaṇa describes me as one who went away and came back (अपम्लुक्तं (*apamluktaṃ*)), and who moves through many difficult places (बहु कृच्छा (*bahu kṛcchā*)). He adds that the gods did this with a certain intent, which is now stated: this Agni, knowing everything, will accomplish for us the sacrifice. That sacrifice is पंचयामं (*paṃcayāmaṃ*), "of five-fold movement", since the sacrifice is पांक्तो (*pāṃkto*) (five-fold). It is त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*), threefold through the division into the three pressings (savana). It is सप्ततंतुं (*saptataṃtuṃ*), extended by seven metrical hymns of praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपम्लुक्तं (*apamluktaṃ*)—one who went away from here and came back
- बहु कृच्छा (*bahu kṛcchā*)—many hardships
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—one who has endured
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—as the bearer of oblations
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—have obtained
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—one who knows everything
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- पंचयामं (*paṃcayāmaṃ*)—having five-fold movement
- तिवृतं (*tivṛtaṃ*)—having three pressings
- सप्ततंतुं (*saptataṃtuṃ*)—having seven metres
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- कल्पयाति (*kalpayāti*)—will construct

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods have taken me, who went away from here and came back and who endured many hardships, as the bearer of oblations. Agni, who knows everything, will construct for us the sacrifice that has five-fold movement, three pressings and seven metres.

##### English translation

> सुपुत्रं च । हे देवाः वो युष्माकं वरिवः परिचर्यां हवीरूपं धनं वा यथा
> कराणि करवाणि तदर्थमित्यर्थः । किंचेंद्रस्य बाह्वोर्वज्रमा धेयां । ग्राहयामीत्यर्थः । अग्नेर्होतृत्वाभाव इंद्रस्य सोमाद्यभानाद्दुर्बलत्वेन वज्रधारणं
> नोपपद्यते । आतस्तत्कृत्वा वज्रं ग्राहयामीत्यर्थः । अथैवं सतीमा विश्वाः सर्वाः
> पृतनाः शत्रुसेनाः जयाति । जयति । जयतु ना ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, I ask (यक्षि (*yakṣi*), I request) of you": what? Immortality, that is, indestructibility, and excellent sons. वरिवः (*varivaḥ*) is service of you, or wealth in the form of oblations; so that I may perform it, that is, for that purpose. Further: "may I place (धेयां (*dheyāṃ*)) the thunderbolt in the arms of Indra", that is, I make him grasp it. Since Agni is not the hotṛ, and Indra, lacking the Soma and the like, is weak and cannot bear the thunderbolt, I therefore, having done so (made him strong), make him grasp the thunderbolt. Then, this being so, may he conquer (जयाति (*jayāti*)) all these hostile armies.

- कराणि (*karāṇi*)—I may offer; for that (purpose)
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—deathlessness
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—an excellent son, (I ask) that you grant
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- आ यक्षि (*ā yakṣi*)—I request
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)—in the arms
- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—the thunderbolt
- आ धेयां (*ā dheyāṃ*)—I make him hold

- इमाः विश्वाः पृतनाः (*imāḥ viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ*)—all these hostile armies
- जयाति (*jayāti*)—he defeats

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Gods numbering three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine worshipped me. They spread a seat of darbha grass for me to sit on. They sprinkled it with flowing ghee. Immediately after that they seated me for the hotṛ's work.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the present Ṛk the number of the gods is stated: त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राणि त्रिंशच्च देवाः (*trīṇi śatā trī sahasrāṇi triṃśacca devāḥ*), "three thousand three hundred and thirty-three gods". Who are these gods, and what is the limit of their number? This can be examined closely here.

This Ṛk states the limit of the number of the gods. In the Ṛk beginning ये देवासो दिव्येकादशस्थ (*ye devāso divyekādaśastha*) it is stated that there are thirty-three gods in earth, atmosphere and heaven. The total number of the gods is given as thirty-three: दिवि एकादश, पृथिव्यां एकादश, अप्पुक्षितः एकादश (*divi ekādaśa, pṛthivyāṃ ekādaśa, appukṣitaḥ ekādaśa*). Sāyaṇa quotes the Nirukta statement यद्यपि तिस्र एव देवताः (*yadyapi tisra eva devatāḥ*) (Ni. 7-5) and explains: क्षित्याद्यभिमानिन्नो देवतास्त्रिस्र एव तथापि स्वस्वविभूत्या त्रयस्त्रिंशत्संख्याता भवंति । तत्तत्स्थाना अन्यास्तद्विभूतय इत्युक्तत्वात् (*kṣityādyabhimāninno devatāstrisra eva tathāpi svasvavibhūtyā trayastriṃśatsaṃkhyātā bhavaṃti | tattatsthānā anyāstadvibhūtaya ityuktatvāt*). That is: although the deities presiding over earth, atmosphere and heaven are only three, by their own greatness they appear as thirty-three in number; the other deities in the several worlds are their manifestations (vibhūti). The Nirukta-kāra also says:

तिस्र एव देवताः (नि. ७-५) ऎंब निरुक्तवचनवन्नु दाहरिसि क्षित्याद्यभिमानिन्नो देवतास्त्रिस्र एव तथापि स्वस्वविभूत्या त्रयस्त्रिंशत्संख्याता भवंति । तत्तत्स्थाना अन्यास्तद्विभूतय इत्युक्तत्वात् । पृथिवी, अंतरिक्ष मत्तु द्युलोकाभिमानिगळ संख्यॆयु मूरे आदरू सह अवरु अवरवर महिमॆयिंद ३३ संख्यॆयुळ्ळवरागि काणुत्तारॆ. आया लोकगळल्लिरुव उळिद देवतॆगळॆल्ला इवर विभूतिगळु ऎंदु विवरिसिद्दारॆ. निरुक्तकाररू सह— तिस्र एव देवता इति नैरुक्ताः । अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानः । वायुर्वा इंद्रो ना अंतरिक्षस्थानः । सूर्यो द्युस्थानः । तासां महाभाग्यात् एकैकस्या अपि बहूनि नामधेयानि भवंति । अपि वा कर्मपृथक्त्वात् ॥ (*tisra eva devatāḥ (ni. 7-5) èṃba niruktavacanavannu dāharisi kṣityādyabhimāninno devatāstrisra eva tathāpi svasvavibhūtyā trayastriṃśatsaṃkhyātā bhavaṃti | tattatsthānā anyāstadvibhūtaya ityuktatvāt | pṛthivī, aṃtarikṣa mattu dyulokābhimānigaḷa saṃkhyèyu mūre ādarū saha avaru avaravara mahimèyiṃda 33 saṃkhyèyuḷḷavarāgi kāṇuttārè. āyā lokagaḷalliruva uḷida devatègaḷèllā ivara vibhūtigaḷu èṃdu vivarisiddārè. niruktakārarū saha— tisra eva devatā iti nairuktāḥ | agniḥ pṛthivīsthānaḥ | vāyurvā iṃdro nā aṃtarikṣasthānaḥ | sūryo dyusthānaḥ | tāsāṃ mahābhāgyāt ekaikasyā api bahūni nāmadheyāni bhavaṃti | api vā karmapṛthaktvāt ‖*)
(Ni. 7-5)

According to the Nirukta school, the three deities Agni, Vāyu or Indra, and Sūrya are likewise the presiding deities of the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven. These deities have many names according to their greatness or because of the variety of their actions. Those names are said to be the many deities.

### Printed p. 300
Having said so, the Nirukta begins: अथातोऽनुक्रमिष्यामः अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानः तं प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यामः (*athāto 'nukramiṣyāmaḥ agniḥ pṛthivīsthānaḥ taṃ prathamaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ*), and in the sections Ni. 7-14 to 9-43 it describes the nature of the earth-dwelling deities. With अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवताः । तासां वायुः प्रथमगामि भवति (*athāto madhyasthānā devatāḥ | tāsāṃ vāyuḥ prathamagāmi bhavati*), in Ni. 10-1 to 11-50 it describes the deities of the middle region, the atmosphere. With अथातो दुस्थाना देवताः (*athāto dusthānā devatāḥ*), from Ni. 12-1 to the end of the chapter, it describes the deities of the heavenly world. Although there are differences of opinion on how many deities there are in this division, one and the same view is found in many places in the Ṛg-saṃhitā.

आ नासत्या त्रिभिरेकादशैरिह देवेभिर्यातं मधुपेयमश्विना । प्रायस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ॥ (*ā nāsatyā tribhirekādaśairiha devebhiryātaṃ madhupeyamaśvinā | prāyastāriṣṭaṃ nī rapāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sedhataṃ dveṣo bhavataṃ sacābhuvā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-11)

In this Ṛk the Aśvin deities are praised: "Come to this place of sacrifice with the thirty-three gods and drink Soma."

श्रुष्टीवानो (*śruṣṭīvāno*) … *ā vaha* **NOTE**
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-2)

In this Ṛk Agni is entreated to bring the thirty-three gods.

ऐभिरग्ने सरथं याह्यर्वाज् नानारथं वा विभवो ह्यश्वाः । पत्नीवतस्त्रिंशतं त्रींश्च देवाननुष्टधमा वह मादयस्व ॥ (*aibhiragne sarathaṃ yāhyarvāj nānārathaṃ vā vibhavo hyaśvāḥ | patnīvatastriṃśataṃ trīṃśca devānanuṣṭadhamā vaha mādayasva ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-6-9)

इति स्तुतासो असथा रिशादसो ये स्थ त्रयश्च त्रिंशच्च । मनोर्देना यज्ञियासः ॥ (*iti stutāso asathā riśādaso ye stha trayaśca triṃśacca | manordenā yajñiyāsaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-30-2)

विश्वैर्देवैस्त्रिभिरेकादशैरिहाद्भिर्मरुद्भिर्भृगुभिः सचाभुवा (*viśvairdevaistribhirekādaśairihādbhirmarudbhirbhṛgubhiḥ sacābhuvā*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-35-3)

तव त्ये सोम पवमान निण्ये विश्वे देवास्त्रय एकादशासः । दश स्वधाभिरधि सानो अव्ये मृजंति त्वा नद्यः सप्त यह्वीः ॥ (*tava tye soma pavamāna niṇye viśve devāstraya ekādaśāsaḥ | daśa svadhābhiradhi sāno avye mṛjaṃti tvā nadyaḥ sapta yahvīḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-92-4)

In these Ṛks and others it is clear that the number of the gods is thirty-three. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too

### Printed p. 301
अष्टौ वसवः । एकादश रुद्राः । द्वादशादित्या इमे एव द्यावापृथिनी त्रयस्त्रींशः देवाः प्रजापतिश्चतुस्त्रींशः ॥ (*aṣṭau vasavaḥ | ekādaśa rudrāḥ | dvādaśādityā ime eva dyāvāpṛthinī trayastrīṃśaḥ devāḥ prajāpatiścatustrīṃśaḥ ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 4-5-7-2)

Eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, together with heaven and earth, make thirty-three gods; besides these, Prajāpati is the thirty-fourth. So it is said in one place. But in another place, although the number is the same thirty-three, Indra and Prajāpati are included in place of heaven and earth.

ते त्रयस्त्रिंशदित्यष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्यास्त एकत्रिंशदिंद्रश्चैव प्रजापतिश्च त्रयस्त्रिंशाविति ॥ (*te trayastriṃśadityaṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāsta ekatriṃśadiṃdraścaiva prajāpatiśca trayastriṃśāviti ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 11-6-3-5)

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too:

त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वै देवाः सोमपास्त्रयस्त्रिंशदसोमपा अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्याः प्रजापतिश्च वषट्कारश्चैते देवाः सोमपाः ॥ (*trayastriṃśadvai devāḥ somapāstrayastriṃśadasomapā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiśca vaṣaṭkāraścaite devāḥ somapāḥ ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 2-18)

The Soma-drinkers are thirty-three gods: the eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, Prajāpati and Vaṣaṭkāra. Thus both in the Saṃhitā and in the Brāhmaṇas there is one view on this number. But

त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् । औक्षन् धृतैरस्त्रृणन्बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्दोतारं न्यसादयंत ॥ (*trīṇi śatā trī sahasrāṇyagniṃ triṃśacca devā nava cāsaparyan | aukṣan dhṛtairastrṛṇanbarhirasmā ādiddotāraṃ nyasādayaṃta ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-9)

what is recited in this Ṛk is recited again in the present Ṛk. Here it is said that three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine gods worshipped Agni. The same occurs in the Vājasaneya Saṃhitā (33-7).

नमो महद्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यो नमो युवभ्यो नम आशिनेभ्यः ॥ यजाम देवान्यदि शक्ननाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवाः ॥ (*namo mahadyo namo arbhakebhyo namo yuvabhyo nama āśinebhyaḥ ‖ yajāma devānyadi śaknanāma mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsamā vṛkṣi devāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-13)

Where homage is said to all kinds of gods, great and small, young and old, it is understood that there is variety of form among the gods. This Ṛk is recited also in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 7-16), in the Śunaḥśepa story, in the context of the prayer to the Viśvedevas. But

In न हि वो अस्त्यर्भको देवासो न कुमारकः । विश्वे सतोमहांत इत् ॥ (*na hi vo astyarbhako devāso na kumārakaḥ | viśve satomahāṃta it ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-30-1), there is no distinction between great and small among the gods. The praise is that all the gods are great souls.

## Sūkta 53 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमैच्छामेत्येकादशर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं । देवानां वाक्यत्वाद्देवा
> ऋषयः । तदद्येति तृचस्य सौचीकोऽग्निर्ऋषिः । तंतुं तन्नन्नित्याद्या अष्टमीवर्जिता जगत्यः । अष्टमी शिष्टाश्च त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । तंतुमाद्या
> जगत्योऽष्टमीवर्जमिति । शिष्टमुक्तं ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यमैच्छाम (*yamaicchāma*) has eleven Ṛks and is the eleventh sūkta. Because it records the speech of the gods, the gods are the seers. For the triplet beginning तदद्य (*tadadya*) the seer is Agni Saucīka. The Ṛks beginning तंतुं तन्वन् (*taṃtuṃ tanvan*), with the eighth excepted, are Jagatī; the eighth and the remaining Ṛks are Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: तंतुमाद्या जगत्योऽष्टमीवर्जमिति (*taṃtumādyā jagatyo 'ṣṭamīvarjamiti*). The rest has been stated; the viniyoga of the sūkta is finished.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning यमैच्छाम (*yamaicchāma*) is the eleventh sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Since it contains the words of the gods, the gods themselves are the seers of this sūkta. For the two Ṛks beginning तदद्य (*tadadya*) only (Ṛks 4-5), Agni Saucīka is the seer; for the remaining Ṛks the gods are the seers. Agni is the deity. The first five Ṛks, up to the Ṛk तंतुं तन्वन् (*taṃtuṃ tanvan*), and the Ṛks other than the eighth are in the Jagatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The Anukramaṇī says: तंतुमाद्या जगत्योऽष्टमीवर्ज० (*taṃtumādyā jagatyo 'ṣṭamīvarja0*). The viniyoga has already been stated earlier.

Sūkta 53. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 53. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 1; Vargas 13, 14. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11.
Seer: 1-3, 6-11, the gods; 4-5, Agni Saucīka.
Deity: 1-3, 6-11, Agni Saucīka; 4-5, the gods.
Metre: 1-5, 8, Triṣṭubh; 6, 7, 9-11, Jagatī.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमग्निमैच्छाम अनिष्टवंतो वयं मनसा हविष्प्रापणबुद्धा । मह्यं
> हविः प्रापयत्त्विति बुद्धेत्यर्थः । सोऽयमग्निरागात् । आजगाम । कीदृशोऽग्निः ।
> यज्ञस्य यज्ञं विद्वान् तथा परुषः परूंषि संधातव्यान्यंगानि चिकित्वानभिगच्छन् ।
> सोऽग्निर्यजीयान्यष्टृतमो नोऽस्मान्देवताता देवतात् यज्ञे यक्षत् ।
> यजतु । नि हि षत्सत् । न्यसीदत्पलु वेद्यामिति शेषः । कीदृशः सन् । अंतर ऋत्विजां
> यष्टव्यानां देवानां च मध्यॆ संचरन् अस्मत्पूर्वोऽस्मत्तो देवेभ्यः
> पूर्वभावी सन् । अग्निं समिध्य पश्चाद्धि देवा आह्वयंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, whom we sought, wishing the oblation to reach us, with the thought "let him convey the oblation to me", has come. He knows the sacrifice and knows the joints, the parts of the sacrifice that are to be joined. That Agni, the best sacrificer, is to sacrifice for us at the worship of the gods; नि हि षत्सत् (*ni hi ṣatsat*) means he has sat down on the altar. Moving among the priests and the gods to be worshipped, he comes before us, before the gods; for the gods are called only after Agni has been kindled.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the meditative mind
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- ऐच्छाम (*aicchāma*)—we were seeking
- सः (*saḥ*)—such
- यज्ञस्य विद्वान् (*yajñasya vidvān*)—one who knows the nature of the sacrifice
- परुषः (*paruṣaḥ*)—to join the separate parts of the sacrifice
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—one who knows
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Agni
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—has come
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—the worshipful one
- निषत्सद्धि (*niṣatsaddhi*)—seated on the sacrificial altar
- अस्मत् पूर्वः (*asmat pūrvaḥ*)—coming even before us
- अंतरः (*aṃtaraḥ*)—one who has joined in among the priests
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- देवताता (*devatātā*)—at the sacrifice
- यक्षत् (*yakṣat*)—may he worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, whom we were seeking with the meditative mind, who knows the nature of the sacrifice and knows how to join the separate parts of the sacrifice, has come. May Agni, the worshipful, seated on the sacrificial altar, who has joined in among the priests even before us, worship for us at the sacrifice.

> देवान् स्तुत्येळामहा इति बुद्धैति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices this Ṛk beginning *purārādhi* is to be muttered (japya); the sūtra has been quoted. This Agni, the hotṛ who accomplishes the offering and the best sacrificer, has been made ready by sitting on the altar; that is, he has become fit for the oblations. Such as he is, he looks all around at the well-placed offerings, the cooked grain, cakes and other foods; हि (*hi*) only fills out the verse-quarter. With what thought? "Let us quickly worship with ghee the gods who are worthy of sacrifice and receive the oblations; let us praise with hymns the gods who are worthy of praise": the words "with this thought" are to be supplied.

- सुधितानि (*sudhitāni*)—well offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the accomplisher of the offering and the worshipful one, is fit for worship because he is seated on the sacrificial altar. He looks all around at the well-offered cooked grain, cakes and the like. Let us quickly worship with the offering of ghee the gods who are worthy of sacrifice. Let us praise the gods who are worthy of praise.

##### English translation
The hotri, most skilled in worship, has been sanctified by his seat (at the altar); he contemplated the sacred offerings reverently placed (before him) : let us speedily worship with ghi the gods to whom worship is due ; let us praise those who are entitled to praise.

> देवहूतिं देवानामाह्वानवंतं यज्ञं भद्रामकः । कल्याणं कृतवान् । आद्येदानीं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the word "dead" is heard about a sacrificer who is still alive, the Surabhimatī iṣṭi is to be performed for him; the Ṛk साद्वीमकः (*sādvīmakaḥ*) is the yājyā there. It is so stated in the sūtra: अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयान् साद्वीमकर्देवनीतिं नो अद्य (*agnirhotā nyasīdadyajīyān sādvīmakardevanītiṃ no adya*) (Ā. 3-13). This Agni today has made our sacrifice efficacious, that is, one to which the gods come, or one accompanied by the gods' eating of the oblation. We have found the sacrifice's tongue, the most hidden one: Agni is the tongue of the sacrifice, since through him the gods drink, hence the figurative use of "tongue". Such an Agni, fragrant, clothing himself in the life given by the gods, comes; and having come, he has made for us auspicious the sacrifice in which the gods are invoked. आद्य (*ādya*) means "now".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—by us
- देवनीतिं (*devanītiṃ*)—the oblation offered for the gods
- साध्वीं (*sādhvīṃ*)—as fit to be eaten
- अकः (*akaḥ*)—has made
- (वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we)
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- गुह्यां (*guhyāṃ*)—the mysterious
- जिह्वां (*jihvāṃ*)—tongue
- अविदाम (*avidāma*)—we have obtained
- सः (*saḥ*)—Agni
- सुरभिः (*surabhiḥ*)—fragrant
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life favoured by the gods
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—possessing
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—comes
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- देवहूतिं (*devahūtiṃ*)—the sacrifice that attracts the gods
- भद्रां (*bhadrāṃ*)—as auspicious
- अकः (*akaḥ*)—has made

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni has made the oblation offered by us to the gods fit to be eaten. We have obtained the mysterious tongue of the sacrifice. Agni comes fragrant and possessing the life favoured by the gods. Today he has made auspicious for us the sacrifice that attracts the gods.

##### English translation
He has to-day made our banquet to the gods efficacious : we have obtained the mysterious tongue of sacrifices : he has come, fragrant, clothed with life : he makes our oblation to the gods to-day auspicious.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

If, while a sacrificer who performs a sacrifice is still alive, the word that he is dead is heard about him for some other reason, then as expiation for it the iṣṭi called Surabhimatī is to be performed. In that iṣṭi the Ṛk साद्वीमकः (*sādvīmakaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयान् साद्वीमकर्देवनीतिं नो अद्य (*agnirhotā nyasīdadyajīyān sādvīmakardevanītiṃ no adya*) (Ā. 3-13).

> ऊर्जS अदः । उत । यज्ञियासः । पंच । जनाः । मम । होत्रं । जुषध्वं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दर्शपूर्णमासयोः सामिधेन्यर्थं प्रेषितेन होत्रा तदद्य वाच इत्येषा
> जप्या । स्रुगादापनात्पूर्वमपि जप्या । सूत्रितं च। तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयेति
> समाप्य । आ. १-२ । इति ॥
> इदमुत्तरं चाग्निर्वाक्यमित्युक्तं। अद्येदानीं प्रथमं । मुख्यनामैतत् ।
> वाचां मुख्यं तद्वाचो वचो वचनं मसीय । मंसीय । उच्चारयामि ।
> येन वचसाहं देवाश्च वयमसुरानभ्यसाम । अभिभवेम । किं तत्प्रथमं वचनमिति उच्यते । ऊर्जादो हे अन्नाद उतापि च यज्जियासो यज्ञार्हा हे
> पंच जना देवमनुष्यादयः यूयं मम होत्रं जुषध्वं । सेवध्वमिति । एवं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, when the hotṛ has been sent out for the sāmidhenī verses, this Ṛk तदद्य वाचः (*tadadya vācaḥ*) is to be muttered; it is also to be muttered before the taking up of the ladle. The sūtra says: तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयेति समाप्य (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīyeti samāpya*) (Ā. 1-2). This and the following Ṛk are said to be Agni's words. अद्य (*adya*) means "now"; प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*) is a word meaning "chief": I utter today that chief utterance of speech, by which we gods overcome the asuras. What is that first utterance? It is said: O eaters of food, and O you worthy of sacrifice, five peoples, gods, men and the rest, take delight in my offering; "serve it" is the meaning. Thus

### Printed p. 308

> बहूच्यमानेऽग्निमनूद्यंति सर्वॆ देवा इत्यभिप्रायः । अत्र तदद्य वाच इत्यादि
> निरुक्तं द्रष्टव्यं । नि-३-८ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that when many (gods) speak in this way, all the gods follow Agni; this is the intention. Here the Nirukta passage beginning तदद्य वाच इत्यादि (*tadadya vāca ityādi*) is to be consulted (Ni. 3-8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—by which instruction in the form of speech
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- असुरान् (*asurān*)—the Asuras
- अभ्यसाम (*abhyasāma*)—(by which) they are able to defeat, such
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—the foremost
- तद्वचः (*tadvacaḥ*)—that same instruction in speech
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- मसीय (*masīya*)—I utter
- ऊर्जादः (*ūrjādaḥ*)—you who eat the oblation
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यज्ञियासः (*yajñiyāsaḥ*)—who are entitled to the sacrifice
- पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*)—O five orders of people, you who are divided into five groups, gods, men and the rest
- मम (*mama*)—my
- होत्रं (*hotraṃ*)—the office of the hotṛ
- जुषध्वं (*juṣadhvaṃ*)—be pleased with (it)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Today I utter that same best instruction in speech by which all the gods are able to defeat the Asuras. O five orders of people, gods, men and the rest, you who eat the oblation and are entitled to the sacrifice, be pleased with my office of hotṛ.

##### English translation
(Agni speaks :) I communicate to-day the best advice by which we gods may overcome the Asuras : do you who are the eaters of sacrificial food, who are entitled to worship, and you five orders of men, be pleased by my (discharge of ) the office of hotri.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This ṛk, तदद्य वाचः (*tadadya vācaḥ*), is to be muttered by the hotṛ as a prompting (praiṣa) at the choosing of the sāmidhenī verses in the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयेति समाप्य (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīyeti samāpya*) (Ā. 1-2).

Pañca janāḥ: in the Ṛgveda the words पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*) and पंच क्षितयः (*paṃca kṣitayaḥ*) are found used here and there. Both expressions have one meaning. As to who these "five peoples" (pañca janāḥ, pañca kṣitayaḥ) are, Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning. First: देवा मनुष्याः पितरः पशवः पक्षिणश्चेति पंच जनाः (*devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraḥ paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaśceti paṃca janāḥ*), that is, the five kinds: gods, men, fathers, beasts and birds. Second:

### Printed p. 309
चत्वारो वर्णाः निषादपंचमाः पंच जना इत्यन्ये (*catvāro varṇāḥ niṣādapaṃcamāḥ paṃca janā ityanye*); that is, he has explained in another way that they are the people of the four classes together with the Niṣādas. For both these meanings authorities from Śruti texts can be shown. First the derivation of the word kṣiti may be examined; afterwards it may be considered what meaning of "five kṣitis" can be stated in the present case.

Kṣitīnām: क्षियंति निवसंति गच्छंति वाक्षितयो मनुष्याः (*kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃti gacchaṃti vākṣitayo manuṣyāḥ*); they dwell or they move about. Therefore Sāyaṇa explains that this epithet belongs to men. The author of the Nirukta read the word kṣiti among the twenty-five names of man beginning with नरः (*naraḥ*) (Ni. 3-7).

अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋताना । स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद्विश्वाति दुरिता गृणंतं ॥ (*agnirnetā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtānā | sa vṛtrahā sanayo viśvavedāḥ parṣadviśvāti duritā gṛṇaṃtaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-4).
In ṛks of this kind, where the difference between men and the people belonging to the gods is shown, the word kṣiti indicates men, the people of the earth. But in the present ṛk one cannot say definitely that only earthly men are meant. For Indra's lordship pervades earth and atmosphere alike.

न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अंतमापुः । स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥ ( (*na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaścana śavaso aṃtamāpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaśca marutvānno bhavatviṃdra ūtī ‖ (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-15).
In ṛks of this kind Indra, divine in nature through his qualities such as generosity, is described as having a power greater than every other power in the world, whose end neither gods nor men could reach, and as one who, with his destructive and majestic power, makes earth and heaven shine together. Since in the present ṛk also Indra's lordship is described as all-pervading, पंचक्षितीनां (*paṃcakṣitīnāṃ*) cannot be said to mean only the four classes together with the Niṣādas as fifth. On this point the author of the Nirukta does not state his own view but only reports the opinions of others.

जुषद्वं” गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः ॥ (*juṣadvaṃ” gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-8).
He has only reported the opinions of others: some hold that the five peoples are Gandharvas, fathers, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; Upamanyu and others hold that the four classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with a fifth group, the Niṣādas, are the five peoples.

### Printed p. 310
Formerly all the gods asked Agni to receive the oblation offered in the sacrifice for them and distribute it to all; Agni agreed and spoke the present ṛk. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā quotes this passage, in which the answer is given that the five peoples together should enjoy this oblation, and shows and discusses the differences of opinion about the five peoples.

प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मया ॥ (*pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mayā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-66).
In this verse the answer Agni gave to the gods is stated, and afterwards the word pañcajana is explained.

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖*) (Jṛ. De. 7-67).**NOTE**
That is: the fire at the entrance part of the sacrificial hall, the Āhavanīya fire that has been led forward, the Gārhapatya fire that is the son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires; these five fires are traditionally called the five peoples. Besides this view:

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गंधर्वा पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gaṃdharvā pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68).
According to the first opinion, one group is men and the others together with serpents and Rākṣasas; according to the second opinion, one group is formed by Yakṣas and Rākṣasas together.

यास्येहमन्यनावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णा मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (*yāsyehamanyanāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇā manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-69).
In this verse the author of the Bṛhaddevatā says that Yāska's view is the first. But in the Nirukta Yāska has only stated the views of others; he has not stated his own view definitely.

### Printed p. 311
ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते (*ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate*) (Bṛ. De. 7-20).
Śākapūṇi holds that the four priests beginning with the hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make the five groups.

चक्षुःशोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः । गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा । सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके ॥ (*cakṣuḥśotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ | gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā | sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-71, 72).
The view of those who speak of the self is that eye, ear, mind, speech and breath are the five peoples. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it is explained that they are the Gandharvas and the rest (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5). In the exposition of the Bṛhaddevatā also these differences of opinion are shown: Agni answered the gods that such five peoples should enjoy the oblation.

To explain who the five peoples are, Yāska has stated the derivation for this ṛk as follows:

तदद्य वाचः परमं मंसीय येनासुरानभिभवेम देवाः । असुरा असुरताः स्थानेष्टस्ता स्थानेभ्य इति वा । अपि वासुरिति प्राणनामास्तः शरीरे भवति तेन तद्वंतः । सोर्धेवानसृजत तत्सुराणां सुरत्वं, असोरसुरानसृजत तदसुराणामसुरत्वमिति विज्ञायते । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः । अन्नादाश्च यज्ञियाश्च । ऊर्गित्यन्ननामोर्जयतीति सतः । पक्वं सुप्रवृक्षमिति वा । पंचजना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं । गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । निषादः कस्मान्निषदनो भवति निषण्णमस्मिन् पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः । यत् पांचजन्यया विशा । पंचजनीनया विशा । पंचपृक्ता संख्या स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकेष्टविशिष्टा ॥ (*tadadya vācaḥ paramaṃ maṃsīya yenāsurānabhibhavema devāḥ | asurā asuratāḥ sthāneṣṭastā sthānebhya iti vā | api vāsuriti prāṇanāmāstaḥ śarīre bhavati tena tadvaṃtaḥ | sordhevānasṛjata tatsurāṇāṃ suratvaṃ, asorasurānasṛjata tadasurāṇāmasuratvamiti vijñāyate | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ | annādāśca yajñiyāśca | ūrgityannanāmorjayatīti sataḥ | pakvaṃ supravṛkṣamiti vā | paṃcajanā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ | gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ | niṣādaḥ kasmānniṣadano bhavati niṣaṇṇamasmin pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ | yat pāṃcajanyayā viśā | paṃcajanīnayā viśā | paṃcapṛktā saṃkhyā strīpuṃnapuṃsakeṣṭaviśiṣṭā ‖*) (Sa. 5-8).**NOTE**

The sense of the first half of this ṛk is: "I shall think upon and know in my mind that most excellent speech by which we shall be able to defeat the Asuras." असुराः (*asurāḥ*) means those who delight in living in bad places, or न सुष्टु स्थानेषु रताः चपला इत्यर्थः (*na suṣṭu sthāneṣu ratāḥ capalā ityarthaḥ*): those who do not like to be in good places; or *sthāneṣu

### Printed p. 312
astāḥ*, those driven out of their own places (having been defeated by the gods and others); or asu is a name for breath, that is, the vital air; it may be said that they are the creatures that live in the body in which such vital air is present. Further, su means an excellent place. According to the Brāhmaṇa sentence सोर्दॆवानसृजत (*sordèvānasṛjata*), Prajāpati created the gods from his own excellent place, that is, from his best limb; therefore the gods are called Surās. In the same way Prajāpati created the Asuras from his own inferior limb, one not excellent; therefore they are called Asuras. Ūrk is a name for food. ऊर्जयतीति सतः (*ūrjayatīti sataḥ*): strength arises in the body from food; or पक्वं सुप्रवृक्षमिति (*pakvaṃ supravṛkṣamiti*): when food is cooked it can be easily broken up or separated and eaten. The five peoples are: Gandharvas, hosts of fathers, gods and Asuras, a five-fold class; or, according to the opinion of the teacher Aupamanyava, the people of the four classes, Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya and Śūdra, together with the people of the Niṣāda caste, the hunters, make five groups and are named the five peoples. As to how the name Niṣāda came to the hunters: the hunter lives by killing animals, or the sin that arises from violence such as killing animals dwells in him, therefore he has come to be called Niṣāda; this is the view of the Nirukta authors. In पंचजन्यया विशा (*paṃcajanyayā viśā*) the meaning is "by the community of five kinds of people", and in this community there are all kinds of people, women, men, eunuchs and the rest.

> य॒ज्ञिया॑सः ।

> पृथिवी । नः । पार्थिवात् । पातु । अंहसः । अंतरिक्षं । दिव्यात् । पातु । अस्मान् ॥ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पंच जना देवादयो मम होत्रं हवमाह्वानं जुषंतां । सेवंतां ।
> अपि च गोजाता भूम्यामुत्पन्नाः । यद्वा । गोशब्देन तज्जं पयआदिकमुच्यते ।

> हविरर्थं प्रादुर्भूता इत्यर्थः । तादृशे ये संति । उतापि च ये यज्ञियासो
> यज्ञार्हाः संति ते मम होत्रं जुषंतां । किंच पृथिवी पृथिवीदेवता पार्थिवात्पृथिवीसंबंधान्नोऽस्मानंहसः पापात्पातु । रक्षतु । तथांतरिक्षमंतरिक्षदेवता
> दिव्यादांतरिक्षादंहसः पापसकाशादस्मान्पातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The five peoples, gods and the rest, are to enjoy my होत्रं (*hotraṃ*), that is, my invocation (हवमाह्वानं (*havamāhvānaṃ*)). Also those who are गोजाता (*gojātā*), born on earth; or else the word गो (*go*) here denotes what is produced from the cow, milk and the like, and the meaning is that they have appeared for the sake of the oblation. Those who are such, and those who are fit for the sacrifice, are to enjoy my hotṛ-office. Further, Earth, the deity of the earth, is to protect us from sin connected with the earth; likewise Antarikṣa, the deity of the atmosphere, is to protect us from the heavenly, that is, atmospheric, sin.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*)—the five peoples, gods, men and the rest
- गोजाताः (*gojātāḥ*)—those born to eat ghee and the like
- उत (*uta*)—and
- ये (*ye*)—those who
- यज्ञियासः (*yajñiyāsaḥ*)—are entitled to the sacrifice
- मम (*mama*)—my
- होत्रं (*hotraṃ*)—office of the hotṛ
- जुषंतां (*juṣaṃtāṃ*)—let them enjoy
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—Earth
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पार्थिवात् (*pārthivāt*)—connected with the earth
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- पातु (*pātu*)—let her protect
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the atmosphere
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- दिव्यात् (*divyāt*)—from the sin connected with the atmosphere
- पातु (*pātu*)—let it protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the five peoples, gods, men and the rest, who are entitled to the sacrifice and are born to eat ghee and the like, enjoy my office of hotṛ. May Earth protect us from sin connected with the earth, and the atmosphere from sin connected with the atmosphere.

##### English translation
May the five orders of men, may those who were born for the sake of ghi, may those who are entitled to worship be pleased by my (discharge of ) the office of hotri : may earth preserve us from all earthly sin : may the firmament preserve us from heavenly.

> स्रावणीया । सूत्रितं च । गार्हपत्यादविच्छिन्नामुदकधारां हॆरेत्तंतुं तन्नृजसो
> भानुमन्विहि । आ-२-२ । इति । अग्न्यंतराले श्वातिक्रमणेऽनया गार्हपत्याहवनीययोर्मध्य उदकेन भस्मना चापूरयेत् । सूत्रितं च । गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरंतरं भस्मराज्योदकराज्या च संतनुयात् । आ.३-१० । इति ॥ अग्निमारुतेऽ
> प्येषा धाय्या । सूत्रितं च । तंतुं तन्नृजसो भानुमन्विहैवान इंद्रो मघवा
> विरष्यी । आ.५-२० । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने तंतुं यज्ञं तन्नन्विस्तारयन्नजसो रंजनात्मकस्य लोकस्य
> भानुं भासकमादित्यमन्विहि । अनुगच्छ । रश्मिद्वारा सूर्यमंडलं प्रविशेत्यर्थः ।
> किंच ज्योतिष्मतः । प्रकाशवतो यज्ञस्य पथो गमनमार्गान् अथवा ज्योतिष्मतो
> दीप्तिमतः स्वर्गस्य पथो मार्गान्देवयानान् रक्ष । पालय । कीदृशान्मार्गान् ।
> धिया कर्मणा कृतान् संपादितान् । किंच सोऽग्निर्जोगुवां स्तोत्कृणामपः ।
> कर्मनामैतत् । क्रियया व्याप्यं कर्मानुल्बणमनतिरिक्तं वयत । करोतु ।
> यदेव यज्ञ उल्बणं क्रियते तस्यॆवैषा शांतिः। तै. सं. ३-४-३-७॥ इति हि ब्राह्मणं।

> जनय । उत्पा-दय । यज्ञाभिगमनवंतं कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk the sacrificer spreads darbha grass (vedatṛṇa) on the altar from the Gārhapatya to the Āhavanīya. Sāyaṇa cites the sūtra: अविधून्वन् संततं स्त्रणन् सव्येन गार्हपत्यादाहवनीयमेति तंतुं तन्नृजसो भानुमन्विहि । आ.११-१ । इति ॥ (*avidhūnvan saṃtataṃ straṇan savyena gārhapatyādāhavanīyameti taṃtuṃ tannṛjaso bhānumanvihi | ā.11-1 | iti ‖*) (Ā. 1-11). In the Agnihotra offering this Ṛk accompanies the pouring of an unbroken stream of water; the sūtra cited is गार्हपत्यादविच्छिन्नामुदकधारां हॆरेत्तंतुं तन्नृजसो भानुमन्विहि । आ-२-२ । इति । (*gārhapatyādavicchinnāmudakadhārāṃ hèrettaṃtuṃ tannṛjaso bhānumanvihi | ā-2-2 | iti |*) (Ā. 2-2). When a dog passes between the fires, the space between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya is filled with water and ashes with this Ṛk (Ā. 3-10). In the Agnimāruta śastra it is the dhāyyā verse (Ā. 5-20).
"O Agni, spreading the sacrifice (tantu), follow the sun, the illuminator of the world (rajas), the radiant one." That is, enter the orb of the sun by means of rays. Protect the luminous paths of the sacrifice, the ways of going; or else the paths of the shining heaven, the paths of the gods, made by action (dhiyā). May Agni make the works (apaḥ, a name for action) of the praisers free from excess (anulbaṇa), neither deficient nor surplus. The Brāhmaṇa says: यदेव यज्ञ उल्बणं क्रियते तस्यॆवैषा शांतिः (*yadeva yajña ulbaṇaṃ kriyate tasyèvaiṣā śāṃtiḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-3-7). "Be Manu", that is, be worthy of thought and praise. "Generate the divine people", that is, the host of gods; make them come to the sacrifice.

- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by excellent action

- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—paths

- दैव्यं जनं (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*)—the divine people
- जनय (*janaya*)—generate

### Printed p. 315

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, spreading the sacrifice, follow the sun, the illuminator of the whole world. Protect the paths that are luminous, belong to the sacrifice and are obtained by excellent action. May Agni make the works of the praisers free from deficiency and excess. O Agni, be a revered producer; generate the divine people.

##### English translation
(The gods :) Spreading out the sacrifice, follow the illuminator of the world (the sun); protect the luminous paths (of the gods) constructed by sacred acts : may Agni render the pious works of the worshipper free from defect : become Manu, generate the people of heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

While darbha grass is spread over the sacrificial altar from the Gārhapatya fire-pit to the Āhavanīya fire-pit, this Ṛk तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*) is to be recited, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: धून्वन् संततं स्तृणन् सव्येन गार्हपत्यादाहवनीयमेति तंतुं तन्न्रजसो भानुमन्विहि (*dhūnvan saṃtataṃ stṛṇan savyena gārhapatyādāhavanīyameti taṃtuṃ tannrajaso bhānumanvihi*) (Ā. 1 11). In the Agnihotra offering too this Ṛk is recited while sprinkling with a stream of water, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: गार्हपत्यादविच्छिन्नामुदकधारां हरेत्तंतु तन्नस्रजसो भानुमन्विहि (*gārhapatyādavicchinnāmudakadhārāṃ harettaṃtu tannasrajaso bhānumanvihi*) (Ā. 2-2). If a dog enters between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires, this Ṛk is recited while purifying that place with water and ashes, as explained by the sūtra गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरंतरं भस्मराज्योदकराज्या च संतनुयात् (*gārhapatyāhavanīyayoraṃtaraṃ bhasmarājyodakarājyā ca saṃtanuyāt*) (Ā. 3-10). In the Agni-Māruta śastra mantras this Ṛk is recited as a dhāyyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra तंतुं तन्न्रजसो भानुमन्विहैवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरष्टी (*taṃtuṃ tannrajaso bhānumanvihaivā na iṃdro maghavā viraṣṭī*) (Ā. 5-20).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, wishing to go to the sacrifice, speak to one another. "O soma-worthy gods, yoke to the chariot the horses that are to be bound to the pole; prepare the reins, the bridles of the horses, properly; adorn the horses." Vandhura is the seat of the charioteer. "Draw on all sides the chariot of the sun with eight seats", that is, make your chariots go to the sacrifice together with the sun's chariot. The connection is: bring from all sides that chariot by which the gods bring us the dear (wealth). Or else it is to be construed: carry it to that sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम्याः (*somyāḥ*)—O gods who drink soma
- अक्षानहः (*akṣānahaḥ*)—the horses to be fastened to the poles
- नह्यतन (*nahyatana*)—bind them to the chariot
- रशनाः (*raśanāḥ*)—the bridles
- इष्टृणुद्वं (*iṣṭṛṇudvaṃ*)—prepare
- आ पिंशत (*ā piṃśata*)—adorn the horses
- येन (*yena*)—by which chariot
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—wealth dear to us
- अभ्यनयन् (*abhyanayan*)—bring to us
- अष्टावंधुरं (*aṣṭāvaṃdhuraṃ*)—having eight seats
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—mounting the chariot
- अभितः (*abhitaḥ*)—gathering all around
- वहत (*vahata*)—bring to the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O soma-drinking gods, yoke to the chariot the horses that are to be fastened to the poles. Prepare the bridles. Adorn the horses. Mount and sit in the chariot with eight seats, by which the gods bring us the wealth dear to us, and gathering around (from various directions) bring (the gods) to the sacrifice.

##### English translation
(The gods to one another :) Drinkers of the soma, bind (the horses) that are to be fastened to the pole; prepare reins; caparison (the steeds); accompany everywhere (in your cars) the chariot which has eight seats with which the gods bring us acceptable (wealth).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On a wedding journey, if a river must be crossed by boat, the bride is placed in the boat with the first half-verse and the river is crossed with the second. Sūtra: अश्मन्वती रीयते सं रभध्वमुत्तिष्ठत प्र तरता सखायः । अत्रा जहाम ये असन्नशेवाः शिवान्वयमुत्तरेमाभि वाजान् ॥ ८ ॥ अश्मन् 5वती । रीयते । सं । रभध्वं । उत् । तिष्ठत । प्र । तरत । सखायः । अत्र । जहाम । ये । आसन् । अशेवाः । शिवान् । वयं । उत् । तरेम । अभि । वाजान् ॥ ८ ॥ वैवाहिके प्रयाणे यदि नाना तार्या नदी स्यात् तदानीमश्मन्वतीत्यर्धर्चेन वधूं नावमारोहयेत् उत्तरेणार्धर्चेन नदीमुत्क्रमयेत् । सूत्रितं च । अश्मन्वती रीयते सं रभध्वमित्यर्धर्चेन नावमारोहयेदुत्तरेणोत्क्रमयेत् । आ. गृ. १-८-२, ३ । इति ॥ (*aśmanvatī rīyate saṃ rabhadhvamuttiṣṭhata pra taratā sakhāyaḥ | atrā jahāma ye asannaśevāḥ śivānvayamuttaremābhi vājān ‖ 8 ‖ aśman 5vatī | rīyate | saṃ | rabhadhvaṃ | ut | tiṣṭhata | pra | tarata | sakhāyaḥ | atra | jahāma | ye | āsan | aśevāḥ | śivān | vayaṃ | ut | tarema | abhi | vājān ‖ 8 ‖ vaivāhike prayāṇe yadi nānā tāryā nadī syāt tadānīmaśmanvatītyardharcena vadhūṃ nāvamārohayet uttareṇārdharcena nadīmutkramayet | sūtritaṃ ca | aśmanvatī rīyate saṃ rabhadhvamityardharcena nāvamārohayeduttareṇotkramayet | ā. gṛ. 1-8-2, 3 | iti ‖*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-2, 3). With this Ṛk too the gods, wishing to go to the sacrifice, speak to one another. The river named Aśmanvatī flows (root री (*rī*), going). "Rise to cross it for going to the sacrifice. Having done so, cross over that river. O friends", that is, friends of the sacrificer, the gods being addressed. "Here, in this river, let us leave those who are aśevāḥ": śeva means happiness, so those who are unhappy and cling to us we leave. Having done so, we cross to the auspicious, pleasant foods, the oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत्तिष्ठत (*uttiṣṭhata*)—rise (O gods)
- अश्मन्वती (*aśmanvatī*)—the river Aśmanvatī
- रीयते (*rīyate*)—flows here
- सं रभध्वं (*saṃ rabhadhvaṃ*)—prepare to go to the sacrifice
- प्र तरत (*pra tarata*)—cross this river
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O friends
- ये (*ye*)—whatever things
- अशेवाः असन् (*aśevāḥ asan*)—are causes of sorrow to us, those
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this river
- जहाम (*jahāma*)—let us leave
- शिवान् (*śivān*)—auspicious
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—foods
- अभि (*abhi*)—to obtain
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- उत्तरेम (*uttarema*)—let us cross the river

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, rise; the river Aśmanvatī flows here. Prepare to go to the sacrifice. Cross this river. O friends, let us leave here all things that cause us sorrow. Let us cross this river to obtain auspicious foods.

### Printed p. 318

##### English translation
The Ashmanvati flows along : be alert ; rise up, cross over, my friends; here let us leave those who are unhappy, so that we may cross over to auspicious sacrificial viands.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When one travels for a wedding and must cross a river on the way by boat, the bride is made to board the boat with the first half of this Ṛk and the river is crossed with the second half, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra: अश्मन्वतीरीयते संरभध्वमित्यर्धर्चेन नावमारोहयेदुत्तरेणोत्क्रमयेत् (*aśmanvatīrīyate saṃrabhadhvamityardharcena nāvamārohayeduttareṇotkramayet*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-2; 3).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वष्टा॑ मा॒या वे॑द॒पसा॑म॒पस्त॑मो॒ बिभ्र॒त्पात्रा॑ देव॒पाना॑नि॒  ॑
> शंतमा ।  
> शिशी॑ते नू॒नं प॑र॒शुं स्वा॑य॒सं येन॑ वृ॒श्चादेत॑शो॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं त्वष्टा देवशिल्पी मायाः । कर्मनामैतत् । कर्माणि पात्रनिर्माणविषयाणि वेत् । वेत्ति । जानाति । स च त्वष्टापसां शोभनकर्मवतां मध्येऽपस्तमोऽतिशयेन शोभनकर्मा देवपानानि । देवाः पिबंति येषु तानि पात्रा
> सोमपात्राणि बिभ्रद्दारयन्वर्तत इति शेषः । स च त्वष्टा नूनमिदानीमग्नौ हविर्वहनायांगीकृते सति स्वायसं शोभनायःसारभूतं परशुं शिशिते । तीक्ष्णयति ।
> त्वष्टा पात्रसंपादनार्थं येन परशुनैतश एतशवर्णो ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणो
> मंत्रस्य पाता पात्रादिसंपादनरूपस्य कर्मणः स्वामी ना वृश्चात् वृश्चति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, knows the works (māyāḥ, a name for action) concerned with making vessels. Among skilled workers he is the most skilful (apastama). He goes about bearing the soma vessels, devapānāni, in which the gods drink. Now, once he has agreed to carry the oblation to the fire, he sharpens the axe of good iron (svāyasa) with which, to make vessels, Brahmaṇaspati, the white-coloured (etaśa), protector of the mantra and master of the work of making vessels and the like, cuts.

Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, knows the methods of making vessels. Tvaṣṭṛ, the doer of the best work among works, has soma-drinking vessels fit for the gods to drink from and auspicious. For making the vessels which the white-coloured Bṛhaspati uses for carrying the oblation, Tvaṣṭṛ makes his axe sharp.**NOTE**

##### English translation

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O kavayaḥ, wise ones, my (Tvaṣṭṛ's) pupils the Ṛbhus, being good (satah, that is, excellent), now sharpen (the tools) exceedingly".

### Printed p. 320

> शीभिः पात्राण्यमृताय सोमाय । तत्पानायेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । युष्माकममृतत्वाय तदर्थं तक्षत । संपादयथ । हे कवयो विद्वांसः यूयं गुह्यानि
> गोपनीयानि पदा पदानि निवासस्थानानि कर्तन । कुरुत। येन स्थानकरणेन देवासो
> देवाः यूयममृतत्वमानशुः प्राप्ता यूयं । एवं स्वशिष्यानाह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues: the vessels are sharpened with the adzes (वाशीभिः (*vāśībhiḥ*)) with which the Ṛbhus fashion cups for the immortal Soma, that is, for its drinking. Or else: "fashion" (तक्षत (*takṣata*)) means "bring about" for the sake of your own immortality. O sages, learned ones, make the secret, to-be-guarded abodes (पदा (*padā*), dwelling-places), by which kind of making you, O gods, have attained immortality. Thus he addresses his own pupils.

- सतः (*sataḥ*)—you who are good men
- याभिः वाशीभिः (*yābhiḥ vāśībhiḥ*)—the vessels which
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—for the drinking of nectar
- तक्षथ (*takṣatha*)—you fashion; those vessels
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- सं शिशीत (*saṃ śiśīta*)—prepare well

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—you who are venerable
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—freedom from death
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—you attained; such
- गुह्यानि (*guhyāni*)—secret

- विद्वांसः (*vidvāṃsaḥ*)—you who are learned

> मेधाविगळाद ऎलै ऋभुगळे, सत्पुरुषराद नीवु याव पात्रॆगळन्नु अमृतपानक्कागि  
> संपादिसुविरो आ पात्रॆगळन्नु ईग संस्करिसिरि. याव निर्माणक्रियॆयिंद पूज्यराद नीवु मरण  
> राहित्यवन्नु हॊंदिदिरो आ रहस्यात्मकवाद निवासस्थानगळन्नु प्राज्ञराद नीवु निर्मिसि.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Ṛbhus, you who are good men, now prepare well the vessels that you fashion for the drinking of nectar. You who are learned, make those secret dwelling-places by whose fashioning you, the venerable, attained freedom from death.

##### English translation
Verily being sages, (Ribhus) sharpen the instruments with which you fabricate the cups for the nectar. Do you, who are wise, prepare the mysterious paths whereby gods have attained to immortality.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते मरुतो गर्भे मृताया गोर्मध्यॆ ग्राहके चर्मणि मृताया गोः
> संबंधिनि योषां कांचिद्दामदधुः । धारितवंतः । निश्चर्मणो गामरिणीत धीतिभिः ।
> ऋ. १-१६१-७ । इत्युक्तं । तथासनि मृताया आस्यॆ वत्समदधुः । केन
> साधनेन । अपीच्येन मनसा देवत्वमाकांक्षतोतापि च जिह्वया । सादृश्यप्रधानोऽयं निर्देशः । जिह्वावदायतया वाश्येत्यर्थः । यद्वा जिह्वया युक्तां
> योषामिति संबंधः । सिषासनिः संभजनशीलः स ऋभुसंघो विश्वाहा सर्वॆष्वहःसु
> सर्वदा योग्याः स्वोचिताः सुमनाः स्तुतीरभिवनते । स च संघो जितिं शत्रुजयं
> कामं कार इत् कर्तृव । शत्रुजयकर्तृव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts placed some female (योषां (*yoṣāṃ*)) in the womb (गर्भे (*garbhe*)), the enveloping hide, of a dead cow. This is said in ऋ. १-१६१-७ (*ṛ. 1-161-7*) ("they fashioned the cow with their thoughts from the hide"). So too in its mouth (आसनि (*āsani*)) they placed a calf. By what means? With a mind (अपीच्येन (*apīcyena*)) that aspires to godhood, and also with a tongue; this is a statement based on likeness, meaning that she is long-tongued, as it were. Or else the connection is "the female endowed with a tongue". The fraternity of the Ṛbhus, inclined to share (सिषासनिः (*siṣāsaniḥ*)), daily and always offers fitting praises, and that company achieves victory over enemies, the desired object; it is the doer of victory over foes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपीच्येन मनसा (*apīcyena manasā*)—with a mind desirous of obtaining godhood
- (the Maruts)—in the womb, in the middle of a dead cow
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—endowed with an excellent tongue
- योषां (*yoṣāṃ*)—another cow
- आदधुः (*ādadhuḥ*)—they placed
- आसनि (*āsani*)—in its mouth
- वत्सं (*vatsaṃ*)—a calf they placed
- सिषासनिः (*siṣāsaniḥ*)—endowed with generosity
- सः (*saḥ*)—that company of Ṛbhus
- विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)—on all days
- योग्य्याः (*yogyyāḥ*)—fit to be offered to the gods
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—excellent praises
- अभि वनते (*abhi vanate*)—offers
- जितिं (*jitiṃ*)—victory over enemies
- कार इत् (*kāra it*)—will surely obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, with a mind desirous of obtaining godhood, placed in the middle of a dead cow another cow endowed with an excellent tongue. In its mouth they placed a calf. That generous company of Ṛbhus offers on all days excellent praises fit to be offered to the gods, and will surely obtain victory over enemies.

##### English translation
(The Maruts) placed a female in the enveloping hide (of a dead cow) and a calf in the mouth (of a dead cow), with mind and tongue, aiming (at deification) : daily the generous (fraternity of the Ribhus) offers suitable praises (to the gods), granting victory over our foes.

## Sūkta 54 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तां सु त इति षडृचं द्वादशं सूक्तं नामदेवगोत्रस्य बृहदुक्थस्यार्षं
> त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । तां सु षड् बृहदुक्थो नामदेव्य इति ॥
> 41

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The twelfth sūkta, तां सु त (*tāṃ su ta*), of six Ṛks, has as seer Bṛhaduktha of the Nāmadeva (Vāmadeva) gotra; its metre is Triṣṭubh and its deity Indra. The Anukramaṇī says: तां सु षड् बृहदुक्थो नामदेव्य इति (*tāṃ su ṣaḍ bṛhaduktho nāmadevya iti*).

### Printed p. 322

> समूढस्य दशरात्रस्य द्वितीये छंदोम एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । अपूर्व्या पुरुतमानि तां सु ते कीर्तिं महा इंद्र । आ. ८-७ । इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा भूय इद्द्वावृधे वीर्याय।
> ऐ. आ. ५-१-६ । इति ॥
> आनुवादवु—तां सु ते ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हन्नॆरडनॆय सूक्तवु.
> इदरल्लि आरु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ वामदेवगोत्रद बृहदुक्थनॆंबुवनु ऋषियु, इंद्रनु
> देवतॆयु; त्रिष्टुप्‌छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—तां सु षट् बृहदुक्थो वामदेव्यः
> ऎंदु हेळिरुवुदु. समूळ्ववॆंब दशरात्रयागद द्वितीयछंदोमदल्लि ई सूक्तवन्नु पठिस
> बेकॆंदु आश्वलायनशौतसूत्रद—अपूर्णा पुरुतमानि तां सु ते कीर्तिं त्वं महा
> इंद्र ऎंब सूत्रदिंद विवृतवागिरुवुदु. महाव्रतेष्टियल्लियू निष्केवल्यशस्त्रमंत्रगळल्लि ई
> सूक्तवन्नु पठिसबेकॆंदु ऐतरेयारण्यकद तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा भूय इद्दावृधे वीर्याय ऎंब वाक्यदिंद (ऐ, आ. ५-१-६) निर्दिष्टवागिरुवुदु.
> सूक्त—५४
> मंडल—१० ॥ अनुवाक—४ ॥ सूक्त—५४ ॥
> अष्टक—८ ॥ अध्याय—१ ॥ वर्ग—१५ ॥
> सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—६ ॥
> ऋषिः—बृहदुक्थो वामदेव्यः ॥
> देवता—इंद्रः ॥
> छंदः—त्रिष्टुप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta is used in the second Chandoma day of the Samūḍha Daśarātra. It is prescribed in the sūtra अपूर्व्या पुरुतमानि तां सु ते कीर्तिं महा इंद्र। आ. ८-७ । इति (*apūrvyā purutamāni tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ mahā iṃdra| ā. 8-7 | iti*) (Ā. 8-7). In the Mahāvrata it is used in the Niṣkevalya. It is prescribed in तां सु ते कीर्तिं महा इंद्र । आ. ८-७ । इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा भूय इद्द्वावृधे वीर्याय। (*tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ mahā iṃdra | ā. 8-7 | iti ‖ mahāvrate niṣkevalya etattūktaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ maghavanmahitvā bhūya iddvāvṛdhe vīryāya|*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-6).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta तां सु ते (*tāṃ su te*) is the twelfth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Bṛhaduktha of the Vāmadeva gotra, its deity is Indra, its metre Triṣṭup. The Anukramaṇī says तां सु षट् बृहदुक्थो वामदेव्यः (*tāṃ su ṣaṭ bṛhaduktho vāmadevyaḥ*). The sūkta is to be recited in the second Chandoma of the Daśarātra sacrifice called Samūḷha (Samūḍha), as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अपूर्णा पुरुतमानि तां सु ते कीर्तिं त्वं महा इंद्र (*apūrṇā purutamāni tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ tvaṃ mahā iṃdra*). In the Mahāvrata rite also it is to be recited among the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras, as indicated by the Aitareya Āraṇyaka sentence तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा भूय इद्दावृधे वीर्याय (*tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ maghavanmahitvā bhūya iddāvṛdhe vīryāya*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-6).

##### Particulars

- Sūkta—54
- Maṇḍala—10; Anuvāka—4; Sūkta—54
- Aṣṭaka—8; Adhyāya—1; Varga—15
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—6
- Ṛṣi—Bṛhaduktha Vāmadevya
- Devatā—Indra
- Chandas—Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तां सु ते॑ की॒र्तिं म॑घवन्महि॒त्वा यत्त्वा॑ भी॒ते रोद॑सी॒  ॑
> अह्वयेतां ।  
> प्रावो॑ दे॒वा अति॑रो॒ दास॒मोजः॑ प्र॒जायै॑ त्वस्यै॒ यदशि॑क्ष  
> इंद्र ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तां । सु । ते । कीर्तिं । मघवन् । महित्वा । यत् । त्वा । भीते इति । रोदसी  
> इति । अह्वयेतां ।

### Printed p. 323

> प्र । आवः । देवान् । आ । अतिरः । दासं । ओजः । प्रजायै । त्वस्यै । यत् । अशिक्षः ।  
> इंद्र ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र मघवन् धनवन् ते तव संबंधिनीं महित्वा महत्वेनागतां
> कीर्तिं सु सुष्टु कीर्तयामीति शेषः । किंच यद्यदा त्वा त्वां प्रति भीते असुरैर्भयं प्राप्ते रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावह्वयेतां आनेत्यब्रूतां तदानीं देवानावः । प्रारक्षः । तथा दासं देवानामुपक्षयकर्तारमसुरमातिरः । व्यनाशयः ।
> असुरान् हत्वा देवानां रक्षणेन द्यावापृथिव्योर्भितिं पर्यहर इति यदस्ति
> किंच त्वस्या एकस्यॆ प्रजायै यजमानरूपाय्कॆ यद्बलमशिक्षः प्रायच्छः तां
> कीर्तिं कीर्तयामीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, Maghavan (wealthy one), I well proclaim that glory of yours which came by your greatness (महित्वा (*mahitvā*)); this is the word to be supplied. Moreover, when heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), frightened by the Asuras, called on you, saying "Come", you then protected the gods. And you destroyed the dāsa, the Asura who harmed the gods. By slaying the Asuras and protecting the gods you removed the fear of heaven and earth. Further, the strength that you gave to the one offspring (प्रजायै (*prajāyai*)), in the form of the sacrificer, that glory I proclaim.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—acquired by greatness
- तां कीर्तिं (*tāṃ kīrtiṃ*)—that glory
- सु (*su*)—I recite exceedingly
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- भीते (*bhīte*)—frightened by the Asuras
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- त्वा अह्वयेतां (*tvā ahvayetāṃ*)—prayed to you, then
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- प्रावः (*prāvaḥ*)—you protected
- दासं (*dāsaṃ*)—the Asuras
- अतिरः (*atiraḥ*)—you destroyed
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वस्यॆ प्रजाय्कॆ (*tvasyè prajāykè*)—to one sacrificer
- यत् (*yat*)—with what pride
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- अशिक्षः (*aśikṣaḥ*)—you granted; therefore I praise you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, I exceedingly recite that glory acquired by your greatness. When heaven and earth, frightened by the Asuras, prayed to you, you protected the gods and destroyed the Asuras. O Indra, for the pride with which you granted strength to the sacrificer, for that very reason I praise you.

##### English translation
(I celebrate), Maghavat, the great glory (you have acquired) by your might ; when heaven and earth alarmed called upon you, you defended the gods, and destroyed (their) adversary ; (I celebrate your glory), Indra, in that you gave strength to one person (the worshipper).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदच॑रस्त॒न्वा॑ वावृधा॒नो बला॑नींद्र प्रब्रुवा॒णो जने॑षु ।  
> मा॒येत्सा ते॒ यानि॑ यु॒द्धान्व्या॒हुर्नाद्य शत्रुं॑ न॒नु पु॒रा  ॑
> विवित्से ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अचरः । तन्वा । ववृधानः । बलानि । इंद्र । प्रब्रुवाणः । जनेषु ।  
> माया । इत् । सा । ते । यानि । युद्धानि । आहुः । न । आद्य । तत्रुं । ननु । पुरा ।  
> विवित्सॆ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तन्वा शरीरेण स्तोत्रेण वा वावृधानो वर्धमानो जनेषु
> प्राणिषु बलानि प्रब्रुवाणो वृत्रवधादिरूपाणि सामर्थ्य्यानि प्रकर्षेण कथयन्नचर
> इति यत्संचारं कृतवानिति यदस्ति ते तव सा गतिर्मायेन्माय्कॆव । मृषेत्यर्थः।
> किंच यानि युद्धानि शत्रुविषयाण्याहुः ब्रुवते पुराविद ऋषयः तान्यपि माय्कॆव ।
> कुत इति आह । अद्येदानीं शत्रुं हंतव्यं न विवित्सॆ । न लभसे । अद्य मा भूत्
> पूर्वं हतवानस्मीति यद्भूषे तदपि नेत्याह । नन्निति प्रश्ने । किं पुरा शत्रुमलभथाः । तदपि नेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, growing by body or by praise, proclaiming among creatures your powers of the kind of Vṛtra-slaying, the fact that you "moved about" (अचरः (*acaraḥ*)), that going of yours is mere illusion (माया (*māyā*)), that is, false. Moreover, the battles against enemies that the seers of old tell of are also illusion. Why? He says: you do not now find (न विवित्से (*na vivitse*)) an enemy to be slain. Let it not be today; even if you say "I slew before", he says no to that as well. ननु (*nanu*) is a question: did you find an enemy before? The meaning is: that too, no.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—by praise
- वावृधानः (*vāvṛdhānaḥ*)—having grown
- जनेषु (*janeṣu*)—among all creatures
- बलानि (*balāni*)—your enemies
- प्र ब्रुवाणः (*pra bruvāṇaḥ*)—proclaiming
- अचरः (*acaraḥ*)—the report that you went about
- यत् (*yat*)—which affair there is, such
- ते सा (*te sā*)—that going of yours
- माया इत् (*māyā it*)—surely false
- यानि युद्धानि (*yāni yuddhāni*)—the battles of yours which
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—they praise (those battles also are false)
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- शत्रुं (*śatruṃ*)—any enemy to oppose you
- न विवित्से (*na vivitse*)—you do not have
- ननु पुरा (*nanu purā*)—what enemies did you indeed have before?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you have grown by praise and proclaim your powers among all creatures; that affair of your going about is surely false. The battles of yours which people praise are also false. There is now no enemy to oppose you. Even before, who indeed was an enemy equal to you?

##### English translation
When your proceed, Indra, increasing in form, and proclaiming your powers among mankind, false is that your (wandering), false the combats which they have narrated; you (find) now no enemy (to attack), did you formerly find one ?

> यन्मा॒तरं॑ च पि॒तरं॑ च सा॒कमज॑नयथास्त॒न्व१॒॑गः स्वायाः॑ ॥३॥

> आपुः ।  
> यत् । मातरं । च । पितरं । च । साकं । अजनयथाः । तन्वः । स्वायाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव महिमनो महिम्नः समस्यॆ सर्वस्याप्यंतं पारमस्मदस्मत्तः
> पूर्व ऋषयः क आपुः । प्राप्नु वन् । न कोऽपीत्यर्थः। यद्यपि महत्त्वं प्रख्यापयंति तथापि न कात्स्येनेति । तत्र कारणमाह । यद्यस्मान्मातरं पितरं च । द्यौः
> पिता पृथिवी मातेति हि श्रुतं । अतो द्यावापृथिव्यावित्यर्थः । ते उभे अपि साकं
> सहैव स्वायास्तन्वः स्वकीयाच्छरीरादजनयथाः । उदपादयः । अतो नापुरिति
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, which of the seers before us has reached the end, the farther limit, of the whole of your greatness? None. Although they proclaim your greatness, they do not do so completely. He gives the reason: because you brought forth mother and father together from your own body. For it is heard that heaven is the father and earth the mother; so the meaning is heaven and earth. Both of them you produced at once from your own body. Therefore they did not reach it; this is the connection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—the earth
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the world of heaven
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- स्वायाः तन्वः (*svāyāḥ tanvaḥ*)—from your own body
- अजनयथाः (*ajanayathāḥ*)—you brought forth; therefore
- ते (*te*)—your
- समस्य (*samasya*)—complete
- महिमनः (*mahimanaḥ*)—

### Printed p. 326
Who among the Ṛṣis before us has reached the limit of your entire greatness? (The Kannada word-glosses at the head of this page continue the preceding verse.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by that very greatness of yours you produced heaven and earth, both together, from your own body. For that reason there is no one whose greatness matches yours. Even in our company, among the foremost Ṛṣis, who is there that has fully understood your greatness?

##### English translation
Who among the Rishis before us have obtained the limit of your entire greatness. since from your own person you have generated at oace both mother and father (or earth and heaven) ?

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> च॒त्वारि॑ ते असु॒र्या॑णि॒ नामादा॑भ्यानि महि॒षस्य॑ संति ।  
> त्वमं॒ग तानि॒ विश्वा॑नि वित्से॒ येभिः॒ कर्मा॑णि मघवन्ज॒कर्थ॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चत्वारि । ते । असुर्याणि । नाम । अदाभ्यानि । महिषस्य । संति ।  
> त्वं । अंग । तानि । विश्वानि । वित्से । येभिः । कर्माणि । मघवन् । चकर्थ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र महिषस्य महतः पूज्यस्य ते तव चत्वार्यसुर्याण्यसुरविघातीन्यदाभ्यान्यनैरहिंस्यान्युत्तरसूक्त उपांत्यवर्जिते दूरे तन्नामेत्यादिषु प्रतिपादितानि यानि नाम नामकानि शरीराणि संति अंग सखे त्वं तानि विश्वानि सर्वाणि वित्से ।
> अदाभ्यान्यहिंस्यानि वेत्सि । जानासि । येभिर्यॆनामभिः कर्माणि वृत्रवधादिरूपाणि
> चकर्थ कुरुषे हे मघवन् तानि वेत्सीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are mahiṣa, great and worthy of worship. You have four bodies, called "names", that destroy the Asuras and cannot be harmed by others. They are set forth in the later sūkta, with the exception of the penultimate verse, beginning दूरे तन्नाम (*dūre tannāma*). O friend, you know all of them, the unassailable ones. O Maghavan, you know the bodies by which you performed deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महिषस्य (*mahiṣasya*)—of the great one
- ते (*te*)—to you
- असुर्याणि (*asuryāṇi*)—enemy-destroying
- अदाभ्यानि (*adābhyāni*)—not subject to harm by others
- चत्वारि नाम (*catvāri nāma*)—four bodies

### Printed p. 327
- संति (*saṃti*)—there are
- अंग (*aṃga*)—O friend
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—by which bodies
- कर्माणि (*karmāṇi*)—deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra
- चकर्थ (*cakartha*)—you performed
- विश्वानि तानि (*viśvāni tāni*)—the natures of all those bodies
- वित्से (*vitse*)—you know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, great one, you have four bodies, destroying enemies and not subject to harm by others. O friend Indra, you alone know the natures of all those bodies by which you performed deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra.

##### English translation
Four are the Asura-slaying uninjurable forms of you the mighty one: you know them all where-with, Maghavat you have achieved your exploits.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं विश्वा॑ दधिषे॒ केव॑लानि॒ यान्या॒विया च॒ गुहा॒ वसू॑नि ।  
> काम॒मिन्ने॑ मघव॒न्मा वि ता॑री॒स्वमा॑ज्ञा॒ता त्वमिं॑द्रासि  ॒
> दाता ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । विश्वा । दधिषे । केवलानि । यानि । आविः । या । च । गुहा । वसूनि ।  
> कामं । इत् । मे । मघवन् । मा । वि । तारीः । त्वं । आज्ञाता । त्वं । इंद्र ।  
> असि । दाता ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं विश्वा सर्वाणि केवलान्यन्येषामसाधारणानि वसूनि धनानि दधिषे।
> धारयसि । विश्वानीत्युक्तं कथं विश्वत्वमित्यत आह । यान्याविराविर्भूतानि सर्वैः
> प्रसिद्धानि वसूनि वासयोग्यानि धनानि संति या च गुहा गुहायां निगूढे प्रदेशे
> वर्तमानानि वसूनि संति तानि विश्वानि दधिष इति । यस्मादेवं तस्मान्ने मम कामं
> कांक्षितं हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र मा वि तारीः । मा हिंसीः । इदिति पादपूरणः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you hold all the treasures that are exclusively yours, unshared by others. Asked how they can be "all", he says: whatever treasures, fit to dwell in, are manifest and known to all, and whatever lie in a hidden place, you hold all of them. Since this is so, O wealthy Maghavan, do not thwart my desire; इत् (*it*) is a metrical filler.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who placed light, brilliance, within the luminous bodies such as the sun; that is, whatever brilliance is in the sun, fire and the rest was made by Indra. He also joined sweet things, Soma and other sweet substances, with sweet juice. Or else: here by मधुना (*madhunā*) is meant the sun, served by all, and with it he joined the waters. Now, for that Indra, a pleasing praise, strength-giving because it dries up enemies and worthy of reflection, has been uttered by me, the mantra-maker, from the Ṛṣi of this name, Bṛhaduktha, endowed with abundant praises.

##### English translation

## Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दूरे तदित्यष्टर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । ऋष्या द्याः पूर्ववत् । दूर इत्यनुक्रांतं । गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The thirteenth sūkta, दूरे तत् (*dūre tat*), has eight Ṛks. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says दूर (*dūra*). The sūkta's use has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta दूरे तत् (*dūre tat*) is the thirteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer, deity and metre are the same as in the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated beginning with दूरे (*dūre*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दू॒रे तन्नाम॒ गुह्यं॑ परा॒चैर्यत्वा॑ भी॒ते अह्व॑येतां  ॒
> वयोध्यॆ ।  
> उद॑स्तभ्नाः पृथि॒वीं द्याम॒भीके॒ भ्रातुः॑ पु॒त्रान्म॑घवन्तिषा॒णः ॥ ११

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दूरे । तत् । नाम । गुह्यं । पराचैः । यत् । त्वा । भीते इति । अह्वयेतां ।  
> वयोध्यॆ ।  
> उत् । अस्तभ्नाः । पृथिवीं । द्यां । अभीके । भ्रातुः । पुत्रान् । मघवन् । तित्विषाणः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया चत्वारि ते असुर्याणि नामेत्युक्तस्याद्यं नाम स्तूयते हे इंद्र
> ते तव तद्वक्ष्यमाणं नाम सर्वेषां नामकं शरीरं पराचैः पराङ्मुखैर्मनुष्यैः ।
> मनुष्याणामित्यर्थः । गुह्यं गोपनीयमप्रकाशितं सद्दूर इतो विप्रकृष्टे
> दूरदेशे वर्तत इति शेषः । यद्यदा त्वा त्वां रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ भीते सती
> अह्वयेतां । अवेत्यब्रूतां । किमर्थं । वयोधा अन्नस्य निधानार्थं ! जगतोऽन्नस्य साधनायेत्यर्थः । तदानीं तेन शरीरेणाभीके । अंतिकनामैतत् । तव समीप
> एव पृथिवीं द्यां चोदूर्ध्वं परस्परवियुक्तं यथा भवति तथास्तभ्नाः । स्तंभितवानसि । किं कुर्वन् । हे मघवन्निंद्र भ्रातुः पर्जन्यस्य पुत्रान् पुत्रस्थानीयानुदकसंस्कृत्यांस्तिष्णाणो दीपयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk the first of the four "names" (bodies) spoken of in चत्वारि ते असुर्याणि नाम (*catvāri te asuryāṇi nāma*) is praised. O Indra, that body of yours, to be spoken of, which is the name for all, being hidden from men who turn away, lies far from here. When heaven and earth, frightened, called you to establish food, that is, to provide food for the world, then by that body you propped heaven and earth upward in your very neighbourhood, so that they are separated from each other. O Maghavan, you did this making the sons of the brother, that is, of Parjanya, the waters that are as sons, blaze.

- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—being secret

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, your famous body, more secret than men who turn away unable to know it, is far, farther than from here. When frightened heaven and earth called you for the establishment of food, then in your very neighbourhood, making blaze the masses of water that are the sons of Parjanya, you established earth and heaven upward.

##### English translation

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, that body of yours is hidden, unknown to others, desirable to many who seek rain, of the nature of space, great, exceedingly vast; by that body you formerly produced what was and what will be. For the sake of the connection between past and future, येन (*yena*) is repeated. From the form of the Supreme Lord, of the nature of space and the rest, the past and future.

> स्वनिर्वाहार्थ० भजंत इत्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing Sāyaṇa's explanation of the previous verse.) From that ethereal form the world arises, as the śruti says "from ether, air" and so on. He adds that the ancient, earlier light which shines, called Āditya or *adakākhyaṃ* **NOTE**, has been born as dear to this Indra. Into it the five who delight in it enter; "five persons" is to be supplied. As *Bhīmasena* can be called just "भीम (*bhīma*)", this is a designation by one part of the name. The four castes, with the Niṣāda as fifth, enter it, that is, they resort to it to sustain themselves.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—by which heavenly body (light) of yours, of the nature of ether

- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—as pleasing

- प्रश्नं (*praśnaṃ*)—ancient **NOTE**
- यत् ज्योतिः (*yat jyotiḥ*)—which divine light
- प्रियाः (*priyāḥ*)—dear to you
- पंच (*paṃca*)—the five kinds of persons, gods, men and the rest
- समविशंत (*samaviśaṃta*)—serve
- तत् नाम (*tat nāma*)—that divine light
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—secret
- पुरुस्पृक् (*puruspṛk*)—desired by many
- महत् (*mahat*)—exceedingly grown great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, that divine light of yours, of the nature of ether, by which you produced the earlier principles and those of the future, and the ancient divine light, born as pleasing to you, which the five kinds of persons dear to you, gods, men and the rest, serve: that divine light is secret, desired by many, and exceedingly great.

##### English translation
That mighty mysterious form, desired of many, wherewith you have engendered the past, and (engender) the future, the ancient mani- fested light, the beloved of Indra, into which the five (orders of beings) delighted enter.

> समानरूपेण ज्योतिषा प्रकाशकेन विव्रतेन विविधेन कर्मणा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra, with his own body or radiance, filled रोदसी (*rodasī*), heaven and earth, on all sides. उत (*uta*) also he filled the middle, the atmosphere, which lies between heaven and earth; "filled" is to be understood there too, and he fills it with his body or radiance. Further, he surveys the five kinds of gods, named gods, men, fathers, asuras and rākṣasas, and also the "seven, seven": the doubled seven means that all the groups of seven principles that exist in the world are taken in. Which are they? The seven Marut groups, the seven rays of the sun, the seven senses, the seven worlds, and other sevenfold things. He looks upon them in their seasons, time after time, in many ways together with the group of thirty-four gods. He sees, always looks. The thirty-fourfold number of the gods is: eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, Prajāpati, Vaṣaṭkāra and Virāṭ. By what means? By light of like form, that is, illuminating, and by varied activity.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- आ अपृणात् (*ā apṛṇāt*)—pervades (with his radiance)
- सरूपेण (*sarūpeṇa*)—by light of one kind
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—by brightness
- विव्रतेन (*vivratena*)—and by action of many kinds
- पंच देवान् (*paṃca devān*)—the five kinds of persons, gods, men and the rest
- सप्त सप्त (*sapta sapta*)—all principles of the number seven, rooted in the sun's rays
- ऋतुशः (*ṛtuśaḥ*)—each at its proper time
- चतुस्त्रिंशता (*catustriṃśatā*)—with the groups of gods numbering thirty-four
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—in many ways
- वि चष्टे (*vi caṣṭe*)—looks upon

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra with his radiance fully pervades heaven and earth and the atmosphere. By light of one kind and by actions of many kinds he looks in many ways upon the five kinds of persons, gods, men and the rest, and all the principles of the number seven rooted in the sun's rays, each at its proper time, together with the groups of thirty-four gods.

##### English translation
He has filled heaven and earth (with his ethereal form) as well as the mid-heaven ; he contemplates in various aspects the five orders of beings, the classes of seven in their seasons, with the thirty-four (deities), (endowed) with light of like nature, and with various functions.

> अत्र प्रसंगात्सूर्यात्मकेंद्रसंबंधिन्युषाः स्तूयते । हे उष उषोदेवते विभानां विभासकानां ग्रहनक्षत्रादीनां प्रथमा प्रथमभूता सत्यौच्छः ।
> विभासनमकरोः। अग्रे ह्युषसः प्रादुर्भवंति पश्चादन्यानि तेजांसि । येन च तेजसा
> पुष्टस्य पोषयुक्तस्यापि पदार्थस्य पुष्टमतिशयेन पोषयुक्तमादित्यमजनयः ।
> उदपादयः । यत् यद्वा ते तव जामित्वं बांधवनवरमवाज्मुखं । अस्मवभिमुखमित्यर्थः । कीदृश्यास्तवेत्युच्यते । परस्याः । उपरि स्थिताया इत्यर्थः । तदिदं महत्यास्तव महदतिप्रवृद्धमेकमसाधारणमेकमेव वासुरत्वं प्रकृष्टबलवत्त्वं । तव
> बलेन कृतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, by the way, Uṣas belonging to Indra in his solar form is praised. O Uṣas, goddess of dawn, you, being the first of the luminaries, the planets, stars and the rest, shone forth, brought light; for the dawns appear first and the other lights afterwards. And by the radiance by which you begot the nourished of the nourished, that is, Āditya, exceedingly full of nourishment: or यत् (*yat*) that kinship of yours is turned downward, facing us. Of what sort of you is this said? Of you who are परस्याः (*parasyāḥ*), situated above. Thus this is of you who are great: the one, unique, greatly increased असुरत्वं (*asuratvaṃ*), excellent strength; it is meant that it is wrought by your power.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- विभानां (*vibhānāṃ*)—than the luminous Ādityas and the rest
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—as the first
- औच्छः (*aucchaḥ*)—you shone
- येन (*yena*)—by which majesty of yours
- पुष्टस्य (*puṣṭasya*)—than all things that possess nourishment
- पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*)—him who has the greatest nourishment, Āditya
- अजनयः (*ajanayaḥ*)—you produced (Āditya, the nourisher of them all)
- परस्याः (*parasyāḥ*)—though in a lofty station
- ते (*te*)—your
- जामित्वं (*jāmitvaṃ*)—relationship
- यत् (*yat*)—by which generosity
- अवरं (*avaraṃ*)—is connected with the lower world
- महत्याः (*mahatyāḥ*)—of you who are of great nature
- महत् (*mahat*)—exceeding
- असुरत्वं (*asuratvaṃ*)—power
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—is unique

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Uṣas, by your greatness by which you shone as the first before the luminous Ādityas and the rest, by your majesty by which you produced Āditya, the nourisher of the whole world,
### Printed p. 335
and by your generosity by which, though you are in a lofty station, your relationship is with the lower world: such exceeding power of yours, of great nature, is unique.

##### English translation
Since you, Ushas, shone forth the first of luminaries, whereby you begot the nourishment of nourishment (the sun); unequalled is the mighty greatness of you who are mighty, since your relationship is down- wards (towards us), though you are stationed on high.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये विधुं दद्राणमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । आ याह्यर्वाजुप
> वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणमिति ॥
> अनया कालात्मक इंद्रः स्तूयते । विधुं विधातारं सर्वस्य युद्धादेः
> कर्तारं । विपूर्वो दधातिः करोत्यर्थः । तथा समने अननमनः प्राणनं । सम्यगननोपेते संग्रामे बहूनां शत्रूणां दद्राणं द्रावकं ईदृक्षामर्थ्योपेतं
> युवानं संतं पुरुषं पलितो जरा जगार । निगिरतींद्राज्ञया । एवमुक्तलक्षणं
> वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणं च देवस्य कालात्मकस्येंद्रस्य महित्वा महत्वेनोपेतं काव्यं
> सामर्थ्यं पश्य । पश्यत हे जनाः । तथा जरसा प्राप्तोऽयं ममार । म्रियते । स
> ह्यः परेद्युः समान । सम्यक्क्षेष्टते । पुनर्जन्मांतरे प्रादुर्भवतीत्यर्थः । तदेवं
> चत्वारि नामानि शरीराण्युक्तानि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya, this verse विधुं दद्राणं (*vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) is used. It is also put in sūtra form: आ याह्यर्वाजुप वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणमिति (*ā yāhyarvājupa vaṃdhureṣṭhā vidhuṃ dadrāṇamiti*). By this verse Indra in the form of Time is praised. विधुं (*vidhuṃ*) is the arranger, the doer of everything, of war and the rest; the root दधाति (*dadhāti*) with वि (*vi*) has the meaning "does". समने (*samane*): *ananaṃ* is breathing; in a battle where there is fully breathing, the man who scatters many enemies, endowed with such ability, who is young, grey old age swallows, at Indra's command. Thus, O people, behold the power of the deity Indra, whose form is Time, endowed with greatness, such as has been described and will be described. Then this same man, overcome by old age, dies; and on the next day समान (*samāna*), he breathes again; that is, he appears again in another birth. Thus four names, that is bodies, have been stated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विधुं (*vidhuṃ*)—one who has the ability to carry through many wars
- समने (*samane*)—in battle
- बहूनां (*bahūnāṃ*)—many enemies
- दद्राणं (*dadrāṇaṃ*)—the man who drives them off
- युवानं संतं (*yuvānaṃ saṃtaṃ*)—though young
- पलितः (*palitaḥ*)—old age
- जगार (*jagāra*)—covers him
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—(O men) of Indra, whose form is Time
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—endowed with majesty
- काव्यं (*kāvyaṃ*)—power
- पश्य (*paśya*)—behold
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same man
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- ममार (*mamāra*)—meets death
- ह्यः (*hyaḥ*)—the next day
- समान (*samāna*)—breathes again (obtains rebirth)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

A man who has the ability to carry through many wars and who destroys many enemies in battle, though he is young, old age covers him. O people, behold the majestic power of Indra, whose form is Time. That same man dies today. Again, after a time, he obtains rebirth.

##### English translation
The grey-haired has swallowed the warlike (man), the scatterer of many foes, in battle being young; behold the power of the deity (endowed) with might ; he dies to-day ; he is alive to-morrow.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this verse विधुं दद्राणं (*vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) is to be recited among the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras in the Mahāvrata sacrifice is explained by the sentence of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, आ याह्वर्वाजुप वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणं (*ā yāhvarvājupa vaṃdhureṣṭhā vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1).

> शाक्कना । शक्त्येव शाक्क । शक्कना बलेन शाकः शक्तः ॥ शक्त्यशक्तौ । स्वशक्तैव
> सर्वं कर्तुं शक्त इत्यर्थः। न हींद्रस्य सहायांतरापेक्षास्तींद्रत्वादेव ।
> अरुणोऽरुणवर्णः सुपर्णः कश्चिच्छोभनपर्णः पक्ष्या गच्छतीत्यध्याहारः । उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । यो महो महाञ्चरो विक्रांतः सनात्
> पुराणोऽनीळोऽनीडो नीडस्याकर्ता । न हींद्रोऽग्निवत् कुत्रचिदपि यज्ञे
> निकेतनं करोति । एवं सुपर्णरूपेणेंद्रमाह । स पक्षींद्रो यच्चिकेत कर्तव्यत्वेन जानाति तत्सत्यमित् सत्यमेव न तु मोघं व्यर्थं भवति । स स्पार्हं स्पृहणीयं वसूत जेता जयति शत्रुभ्यः सकाशात् उतापि दाता प्रयच्छति च स्तोतृभ्यः॥
> न लोकाव्ययेत्यादिना षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शाक्कना (*śākkanā*) means by power, by strength; शाकः (*śākaḥ*) is capable. That is, he is able to do everything by his own power alone; for Indra, by his very Indra-hood, needs no other help. अरुणः (*aruṇaḥ*) is red-coloured; सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*) is one with beautiful wings; "goes by flight" is to be supplied, and "comes" is supplied from the preverb आ (*ā*) heard in the verse. He who is महः (*mahaḥ*), great, शूरः (*śūraḥ*), valiant, सनात् (*sanāt*), ancient, अनीळः (*anīḷaḥ*), makes no nest; for Indra, unlike Agni, does not make a dwelling anywhere in the sacrifice. Thus he speaks of Indra in the form of a bird. What that bird Indra knows as to be done, that is truly true, not vain. He is the winner of desirable wealth from enemies, and also the giver of it to the praisers. The rest of the passage cites the rule न लोकाव्ययेत्यादिना (*na lokāvyayetyādinā*) for the prohibition of the genitive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
