##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Asunīti, establish again in us the power of sight and the breath, and provide us with comfort. May we see the rising sun for a long time. O goddess Anumati, of noble conduct, bring us welfare and make us happy.

##### English translation
Restore to us, Asuniti, sight and breath, and enjoyment in this world : long may we behold the rising sun ; make us happy, gracious (goddess), with prosperity.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The goddess Earth is to give us the breath (असुं (*asuṃ*)) again; the goddess Heaven is to give breath; likewise the Firmament, the deity of the atmosphere, is to give breath; likewise Soma is to give back our body. Likewise Pūṣan, the deity presiding over nourishment, is to give पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*). पंथा अंतरिक्षं (*paṃthā aṃtarikṣaṃ*) (Ni. 11-45); what is in that…

> वाचं । वागात्मकः शब्दो ह्याकाशादुत्पद्यते। तां पुनर्ददातु । किंच या स्वस्तिर्या
> लोके वेदे च स्वस्तिरुच्यते तामपि पूषा प्रयच्छतु । यद्वा । पूषा पोषं
> प्रयच्छतु । या स्वस्तिर्वाग्नाम्नी देव्यस्ति सा पथ्यां वाचं प्रयच्छतु । वाग्वै
> पथ्या स्वस्तिः । शत. ३-२-३-८ । इति ब्राह्मणं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…speech: for the sound that is of the nature of speech arises from space (ākāśa). May he give that again. Moreover, may Pūṣan grant also the स्वस्ति (*svasti*) that is called svasti in the world and in the Veda. Or else: may Pūṣan grant nourishment; the goddess named Vāk who is स्वस्ति (*svasti*), may she grant the पथ्या (*pathyā*) speech. वाग्वै पथ्या स्वस्तिः (*vāgvai pathyā svastiḥ*) (Śa. 3-2-3-8), says the Brāhmaṇa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the goddess Earth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- असुं (*asuṃ*)—the breath
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—may she give
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the deity of the heavenly world
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—may she give us breath again
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—may the firmament make us live again
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- गः (*gaḥ*)—our **NOTE**
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—body
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—may he give
- या (*yā*)—which
- स्वस्तिः (*svastiḥ*)—the welfare that is called beneficial
- पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*)—and the power of speech
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—may the god Pūṣan provide to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess Earth give us breath. May the deity of the heavenly world give us breath again. May the firmament make us live again. May the god Soma give our body again. May the goddess Vāk, who bestows welfare, create welfare. May the god Pūṣan produce nourishment for us.

##### English translation
May earth restore the (departed) soul to us : may the divine heaven, may the firmament (restore it) : may Soma restore the body to us : may Pushan restore to us speech, which is prosperity.

> शं सुखं प्रयच्छतां । कीदृश्यौ ते । यह्वी महत्वा ऋतस्य यज्ञस्योदकस्य वा
> मातरा निर्मात्र्यौ । यद्रपः पापं कृच्छ्रमस्ति तदप भरतां । अपहरतां । अपनयतां । हे द्यौः हे पृथिवि हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ क्षमा क्षमायां सत्यां । यद्वा
> क्षमा प्वथगप्युच्यते । क्षमाप्यपहरतु । एवमुक्त्वा सुबंधुं बंध्वादयो ब्रुवते।
> हे सुबंधो ते त्वां मो षु मैव सु सुष्टु किं चन परं रसः कृच्छ्रमाममत् ।
> हिनस्तु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With the three verses beginning with this one there is praise of Heaven and Earth. May रोदसी (*rodasī*), Heaven and Earth, give happiness to Subandhu. What are they like? यह्वी (*yahvī*), great; ऋतस्य मातरा (*ṛtasya mātarā*), the makers of the sacrifice or of water. Whatever रपः (*rapaḥ*), sin or hardship, there is, may they carry it away, remove it. O Heaven, O Earth, O Heaven and Earth, क्षमा (*kṣamā*) is said while क्षमायां (*kṣamāyāṃ*) (the earth) exists. Or else क्षमा (*kṣamā*) is also said of the earth: let the earth too carry it away. Having said this, Subandhu's kinsmen and others speak: O Subandhu, let nothing else, no hardship, afflict you; मो षु (*mo ṣu*) means "by no means, well".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यह्वी (*yahvī*)—those of great nature
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- मातरा (*mātarā*)—and makers
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—Heaven and Earth
- सुबंधवे (*subaṃdhave*)—to Subandhu
- शं (*śaṃ*)—may they provide happiness
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever
- रपः (*rapaḥ*)—sinful act (whatever disease) there is
- अप भरतां (*apa bharatāṃ*)—may they destroy
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—O goddess of the heavenly world
- पृथिवि (*pṛthivi*)—O Earth
- क्षमा रपः (*kṣamā rapaḥ*)—destroy all diseases connected with the earth
- ते (*te*)—(O Subandhu) you
- किं चन (*kiṃ cana*)—no sin (no disease)
- मो षु आममत् (*mo ṣu āmamat*)—may it not afflict

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Heaven and Earth, of great nature and makers of the sacrifice, provide happiness to Subandhu and destroy all sins. By their grace may no sin afflict Subandhu.

##### English translation
May the great heaven and earth, the parents of sacrifice, (grant) happiness to Subandhu : heaven and earth, remove all iniquity ; let heaven (take away) iniquity : may no ill ever approach you.

> क्षमा । चरिष्णु । एककं । भरतां । अप । यत् । रपः । द्यौः । पृथिवि । क्षमा । रपः ।  
> मो इति । सु । ते । किं । चन । आममत् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो द्युलोकाद्वेषजा भेषजानि द्वके द्विकं त्रिका त्रिकं चाव चरंति । अत्राश्विनौ द्विकमवचरतः । इळा सरस्वती भारती त्रिकमवचरंति । क्षमा क्षमायां चरिष्णु
> चरत्येककमेकं भेषजमित्यभिप्रायमाह । तानि सर्वाणि सुबंधोः प्राणं रक्षंत्विति
> शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From the heavenly world, remedies come down in द्वके (*dvake*), the pair, and त्रिका (*trikā*), the triad. Here the two Aśvins descend as the pair; Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī descend as the triad. On earth चरिष्णु (*cariṣṇu*) moves एककं (*ekakaṃ*), a single remedy: this is the purport he states. May all these protect the life of Subandhu—this is the supplied remainder.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- भेषजा (*bheṣajā*)—medicines that destroy disease
- द्वके (*dvake*)—in the two forms of the Aśvin deities
- त्रिका (*trikā*)—in the three forms Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī
- अव चरंति (*ava caraṃti*)—move about (come down to the earth)
- क्षमा (*kṣamā*)—on earth
- एककं (*ekakaṃ*)—in a single form
- चरिष्णु (*cariṣṇu*)—it moves
- यत् रसः (*yat rasaḥ*)—whatever (disease) sins there are
- अप भरतां (*apa bharatāṃ*)—may they destroy
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—O goddess of the heavenly world
- पृथिवि (*pṛthivi*)—O Earth
- क्षमा रसः (*kṣamā rasaḥ*)—destroy all sins (diseases) connected with the earth
- ते (*te*)—(O Subandhu) you
- किं च न (*kiṃ ca na*)—no sin (disease)
- मो षु आममत् (*mo ṣu āmamat*)—may it not afflict

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Medicines that destroy disease come down from the heavenly world to the earth in two forms, as the Aśvin deities, and in three forms, as Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī; on the earth alone it has a single form. O Heaven and Earth, destroy all sins connected with the earth. O Subandhu, may no sin afflict you.

##### English translation
Remedies come down from heaven by tows and by threes : one wanders singly in heaven ; heaven and earth, remove all iniquity : let heaven (takc away) iniquity : may no ill ever approach you.

> समिं॑द्रेरय॒ गाम॑न॒ड्वाहं॒ य आव॑हदुशी॒नरा॑ण्या॒ अनः॑ ।  
> भर॑ता॒मप॒ यद्रपो॒ द्यौः पृ॑थिवि क्ष॒मा रपो॒ मो षु ते॒ किं  ॒॑
> चनाममत् ॥ १० ॥

> भरतां । अप । यत् । रपः । द्यौः । पृथिवि । क्षमा । रपः । मो इति । सु । ते । किं ।  
> चन।आममत् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र समीरय प्रेरय । किं । गां गंतारमनड्वाहमनोवहनसमर्थं।
> योऽनड्वानावहत् आवहत्यस्मान्प्रति । किं । अनः शकटं । कस्य । उशीनराण्या एतन्नामिकाया ओषधेः । ययार्तमनुलिंपंति सोशीनराणी । भरतामित्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, समीरय (*samīraya*), send. What? गां (*gāṃ*), the goer, the ox अनड्वाहं (*anaḍvāhaṃ*) able to draw a cart, which आवहत् (*āvahat*) brings to us. What? अनः (*anaḥ*), a cart. Of what? उशीनराण्याः (*uśīnarāṇyāḥ*), of the plant of this name, ययार्तमनुलिंपंति सोशीनराणी (*yayārtamanuliṃpaṃti sośīnarāṇī*). The words beginning भरतां (*bharatāṃ*) have been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- उशीनराण्याः (*uśīnarāṇyāḥ*)—loaded with the plant called Uśīnarāṇī
- अनः (*anaḥ*)—the cart
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which ox
- आवहत् (*āvahat*)—brings
- गां (*gāṃ*)—that moves comfortably
- अनड्वाहं (*anaḍvāhaṃ*)—the ox
- समीरय (*samīraya*)—send to us
- यत् रपः (*yat rapaḥ*)—whatever sin in the form of disease there is
- अप भरतां (*apa bharatāṃ*)—let it all be destroyed
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—O goddess of the heavenly world
- पृथिवि (*pṛthivi*)—O Earth
- क्षमा रपः (*kṣamā rapaḥ*)—destroy all diseases connected with the earth
- ते (*te*)—(O Subandhu) you
- किं चन (*kiṃ cana*)—no disease
- मो षु आममत् (*mo ṣu āmamat*)—may it not afflict

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, send to us the ox that moves comfortably, the ox that brings the cart loaded with the plant called Uśīnarāṇī. Let all sin in the form of disease be destroyed. O goddess of the heavenly world, O Earth, destroy all diseases connected with the earth. O Subandhu, may no disease afflict you.

##### English translation
Send, Indra, the active ox, who may bring the cart (leaden with) the Ushinarani grass : heaven and earth, remove all iniquity ; let heaven (take away) iniquity ; may no ill ever approach you.

## Sūkta 60 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ जनमिति द्वादशर्चमष्टादशं सूक्तं । गौपायना बंध्वादय ऋषयः ।
> षष्ठ्यास्तगस्त्यस्य स्वसैन्यां मातर्षिका । आदितः पंच गायत्र्यः । अष्टमीनवम्या
> 49

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning *ā janam* has twelve ṛks and is the eighteenth. The seers are Bandhu and others of the Gaupāyana line. Of the sixth, Agastya's sister is the mother-seer **NOTE**. The first five are in Gāyatrī; the eighth and ninth… (the text goes on).

### Printed p. 386

> पंक्ति शिष्टा अनुष्टुभः । आदितश्चतसृणामसमातिनान्नो राज्यः स्सूयमानत्वात् स
> एव देवता । पंचम्या इंद्रः । षष्ठ्या अस्यसमातिः । ततः पंचानां सुबंधोर्जिविताह्वानरूपोऽर्थो देवता । अयं मे हस्त इत्यस्या लब्धसंज्ञस्य सुबंधोः
> स्पर्शनहेतुभूतो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । आ जनमिति द्वादशर्चमानुष्टुभं
> चतसृभिरसमातिमस्तुवन्पंचम्येंद्रं षष्ठ्यागस्त्यस्य स्वसा मातैषां राजानमस्तौत्पराभिः सुबंधोर्जिवमाह्वयंस्तमंत्यया लब्धसंज्ञमस्वशन् पंचम्याद्या
> गायत्रोऽष्टम्याद्ये पंक्ति इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the introduction. The first four Ṛks are in the pañkti-less (Anuṣṭubh) arrangement as he states it: the remaining Ṛks are Anuṣṭubh. The deity of the first four is King असमाति (*asamāti*) himself, because he is the one praised. The fifth has Indra, and the sixth has Asamāti. For the next five (7–11) the deity is the subject matter, the calling back to life of Subandhu. For the twelfth, अयं मे हस्त (*ayaṃ me hasta*), the deity is the hand that touched Subandhu when he regained consciousness. He then cites the Anukramaṇī. It says that the sūkta has twelve Ṛks in Anuṣṭubh; that four praise Asamāti; that the fifth is to Indra; that in the sixth Agastya's sister-in-law, the mother of these (seers), praises the king; that with the remaining Ṛks they called Subandhu's life back; and that with the last one he regained consciousness and the hand touched him. The first five are Gāyatrī and the eighth and the next are Paṅkti.
**NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning आ जनं (*ā janaṃ*) is the eighteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. The seers of this sūkta are Bandhu and the others, sons of Gopāyana. For the sixth Ṛk of the sūkta the seer is a woman, the daughter-in-law of the sage Agastya and the mother of these Bandhu and the others. The first five Ṛks of the sūkta are in the Gāyatrī metre; the eighth and ninth Ṛks are in the Paṅkti metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Because in the first four Ṛks of this sūkta a king named Asamāti is praised, the deity of these four Ṛks is this Asamāti himself; for the fifth Ṛk the deity is Indra; for the sixth Ṛk the deity is Asamāti. In the five Ṛks that follow (Ṛks 7–11) the calling back to life of Subandhu is recited, so that subject is the deity. For the twelfth Ṛk, अयं मे हस्तः (*ayaṃ me hastaḥ*), the deity is the matter of his touching Subandhu after regaining consciousness. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आ जनमिति द्वादशर्चमानुष्टुभं चतसृभिरसमातिमस्तुवन्पंचम्येंद्रं षष्ठ्यागस्तस्य स्वसा मातैषां राजानमसौत्पराभिः सुबंधोर्जिवमाह्वयंस्तमंत्यया लब्धसंज्ञमस्पृशन् पंचाद्या गायत्रोष्टम्याद्ये पंक्ति (*ā janamiti dvādaśarcamānuṣṭubhaṃ catasṛbhirasamātimastuvanpaṃcamyeṃdraṃ ṣaṣṭhyāgastasya svasā mātaiṣāṃ rājānamasautparābhiḥ subaṃdhorjivamāhvayaṃstamaṃtyayā labdhasaṃjñamaspṛśan paṃcādyā gāyatroṣṭamyādye paṃkti*).

Sūkta 60
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 60.
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 1; Varga 24, 25.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.
Ṛṣi: Bandhu, Śrutabandhu, Viprabandhu, the Gaupāyanas; 6: Agastya's sister-in-law, mother of these.
Devatā: 1–4, 6: King Asamāti; 5: Indra; 7–11: the calling back to life of Subandhu; 12: the hand.
Chandas: 1–5: Gāyatrī; 6, 7, 10–12: Anuṣṭubh; 8, 9: Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ जनं॑ त्वे॒षसं॑दृशं॒ माही॑नाना॒मुप॑स्तुतं ।

### Printed p. 387

> अगन्मभिभ्रतो नमः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । जनं । त्वेषसंदृशं । माहीनानां । उपस्तुतं ।  
> अगन्म । भिभ्रतः । नमः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदमादिभिस्तिसृभी राजानं स्तुवंति । वयं बंध्वादयो जनं जनपदमसुनीतिस्वभूतवागन्म । अभिगताः ॥ गमर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेति चेर्लुक् । मोश्चेति
> मकारस्य नकारः ॥ कीदृशं जनं । त्वेषसंदृशं दीप्तदर्शनं माहीनानां महतामुपस्तुतमुपगतस्तुतिं ॥ तादौ चेति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः ॥ कीदृशा वयं । नमो
> नमस्कारं बिभ्रतो धारयंतः । कुर्वंत इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । जनमसमातिमित्यर्थः ।
> शिष्टं समानं । नमो बिभ्रत इति राजकृते नमस्कारं धारयंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk and the next two they praise the king. We, Bandhu and the others, have come to the people, the realm, of Asamāti, who is like our own protector. What kind of people? Of splendid appearance, of shining look; honoured by the mighty, one whose praise has been sung. What kind are we? Bearing, holding, that is, performing homage. Alternatively, जनं (*janaṃ*) means Asamāti. The rest is the same; "bearing homage" means offering homage for the king's sake.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- नमः (*namaḥ*)—homage
- बिभ्रतः (*bibhrataḥ*)—offering
- त्वेषसंदृशं (*tveṣasaṃdṛśaṃ*)—him who has a shining form
- माहीनानां (*māhīnānāṃ*)—by the great
- उपस्तुतं (*upastutaṃ*)—praised
- जनं (*janaṃ*)—to the king named Asamāti
- आ अगन्म (*ā aganma*)—we have come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Offering the homage fit for a king, we have come to the king named Asamāti, who has a shining form and is praised by the great.

##### English translation
We have come to the person of splendid appearance, the honoured of the mighty, bringing him reverential homage.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस॑मातिं नि॒तोष॑नं त्वे॒षं नि॑य॒यिनं॒ रथं॑ ।  
> भ॒जेर॑थस्य॒ सत्प॑तिं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असमातिं । नितोशनं । त्वेषं । निययिनं । रथं ।

### Printed p. 388

> भजेऽरथस्य । सत्पपतिं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> असमातिं राजानं नितोशनं शत्रूणां हंतारं । नितोशतिर्वधकर्मा। त्वेषं
> दीप्तं । निययिनं रथमित्युपमाप्रधानो निर्देशः । रथवत्सर्वाभिमतप्राप्तिसाधनं
> भजेरथस्यॆतन्नामकस्य राज्यो वंशे जातं । यद्वा । एतन्नामा कश्चिदस्य शत्रुः । तस्य
> निययिनं ॥ हलदंतात् । पा. ६-३-९ । इति सप्तम्या अलुक् ॥ सत्पतिं सतां पालकं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Asamāti the king is the slayer of enemies; नितोशति (*nitośati*) is a root of killing. त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*) means radiant. "निययिनं रथं (*niyayinaṃ rathaṃ*)" is a statement in which the simile is primary: like a chariot, a means of obtaining everything desired. भजेरथस्य (*bhajerathasya*): born in the line of the king of that name. Or else some enemy of his bears this name, and Asamāti is his निययिनं (*niyayinaṃ*). सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*) is the protector of the good.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नितोशनं (*nitośanaṃ*)—destroyer of enemies
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—radiant
- निययिनं (*niyayinaṃ*)—moving excellently
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—one who provides what is desired like a chariot
- भजेरथस्य (*bhajerathasya*)—one born in the line of Bhajeratha; or भजेरथस्य निययिनं (*bhajerathasya niyayinaṃ*)—the destroyer of the enemy named Bhajeratha
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—protector of the good
- असमातिं (*asamātiṃ*)—to Asamāti (we have come)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have come to Asamāti, the destroyer of enemies, radiant, who provides what is desired like a well-moving chariot, born in the line of Bhajeratha, the protector of the good.

##### English translation
To Asamati, the destroyer (of foes), radiant, a quick-moving chariot (for the bringing of benefits), the descendant) of Bhajeratha, the protector of the good.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो जना॑न्महि॒षा इ॑वातित॒स्थौ पवी॑रवान् ।  
> उ॒ताप॑वीरवान्यु॒धा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । जनान् । महिषान् इव । अतितस्थौ । पवीरवान् ।  
> उत । अपवीरवान् । युधा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽसमातिर्जनान् स्वविरोधिभूतानतितस्थौ अतिक्रम्य तिष्ठति । पराभावयतीत्यर्थः । क इव । महिषान् सिंह इव । कीदृशः सन् । पवीरवान् । पवीर पविः। खड्ग-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Asamāti who stands over, overcomes, the people who are his opponents; that is, he defeats them. Like what? Like a lion over buffaloes. In what state? पवीरवान् (*pavīravān*): पवीर (*pavīra*) is पविः (*paviḥ*), a sword; so, possessing a sword.

### Printed p. 389

> वान् । उतापि चापवीरवानपगतखड्गः सन् । शस्त्रसाहाय्यमपि कदाचिन्नापेक्षत
> इत्यर्थः । किं कुर्वन् । युधा योधनेन । युद्धैत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*utāpi cāpavīravān*: and also when he is without a sword; that is, he never even needs the help of a weapon. Doing what? युधा (*yudhā*): by fighting, that is, in battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवीरवान् (*pavīravān*)—whether he has a sword
- उत (*uta*)—or
- अपवीरवान् (*apavīravān*)—whether he has no sword
- यः (*yaḥ*)—that Asamāti who
- महिषान् इव (*mahiṣān iva*)—as a lion kills wild buffaloes (easily)
- जनान् (*janān*)—the enemy people
- युधा (*yudhā*)—by fighting
- अतितस्थौ (*atitasthau*)—defeats and destroys (we have come to that Asamāti)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have come to that Asamāti who, whether he has a sword or not, kills enemies in battle as easily as a lion kills wild buffaloes.

##### English translation
Who, whether armed or unarmed with a sword, overcomes adversaries in fight, as (a lion destroys) buffaloes.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पवीरवान् (*pavīravān*): पविः शल्यो भवति । यद्विपुनाति कायं तद्वत्पवीरमायुधं तद्वानिंद्रः पवीरवान् । (*paviḥ śalyo bhavati | yadvipunāti kāyaṃ tadvatpavīramāyudhaṃ tadvāniṃdraḥ pavīravān |*) (Ni. 12-30). पविः (*paviḥ*) means a lance, a spear, because it enters the body and splits it. पवीर (*pavīra*) means a pointed weapon.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ये॑क्ष्वा॒ कुरुप॑ व्र॒ते रे॒वान्म॑रा॒य्येध॑ते ।  
> दि॒वी॑व॒ पंच॑ कृ॒ष्टयः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । इक्ष्वाकुः । उप । व्रते । रेवान् । मरायी । विधते ॥  
> दिविऽइव । पंच । कृष्णयः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्य जनपदस्येक्ष्वाकू राजा व्रते कर्मणि रक्षणरूप उपैधते प्रवर्धते ।
> कीदृशः सन् । रेवान् रयिवान् मरायी शत्रूणां मारकश्च सन् । विशेषणद्वयेन

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In whose realm King Ikṣvāku prospers, grows, in the work, the task of protection. What kind is he? Wealthy, and a slayer of enemies.

### Printed p. 390

> जनानां दानादिरूपेण धनलाभः परराजोपद्रवापत्तिश्चोक्ता भवति । एवा सति
> तद्विषयस्थाः पंच कृष्णयो निषादपंचमाश्चत्वारो वर्णा दिनीव द्युलोकॆः यथा
> संकल्पसिद्धाः संतः सुखिनो भवंति तद्वत्सुखिनो भवंतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By these two epithets the people's gain of wealth through gifts and so on, and freedom from the troubles of other kings, are stated. This being so, the five orders (कृष्णयः (*kṛṣṇayaḥ*)) living in that realm, the four castes with the Niṣādas as fifth, become happy, as people in the heavenly world are happy, their wishes fulfilled. That is the word to be supplied.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—in whose kingdom
- पंच कृष्णयः (*paṃca kṛṣṇayaḥ*)—people of five groups
- दिवीव (*divīva*)—so that they may be happy as in the heavenly world
- रेवान् (*revān*)—wealthy
- मरायी (*marāyī*)—destroyer of enemies
- इक्ष्वाकुः (*ikṣvākuḥ*)—the king named Ikṣvāku
- व्रते (*vrate*)—in the work of protecting the subjects
- उप विधते (*upa vidhate*)—prospers (we have come to such an Asamāti)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have come to that Asamāti in whose kingdom the king named Ikṣvāku, wealthy and a destroyer of enemies, prospers in the work of protecting the subjects, so that the people of the five groups are happy as in the heavenly world.

##### English translation
In the good government of whose (realm) the opulent and victorious Ikshwaku prospers (so that) the five orders of men (are as happy) as if they were in heaven.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ क्ष॒त्रास॑मातिषु॒ रथ॑प्रोष्ठेषु धारय ।  
> दि॒वी॑व॒ सूर्यं॑ दृ॒शे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । क्षत्रा । असमातिषु । रथप्रोष्ठेषु । धारय ।  
> दिविइव । सूर्यं । दृशे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयेंद्रमाह्वयतेऽसमात्यर्थं । हे इंद्र क्षत्रा क्षत्राणि बलानि रथप्रोष्ठेष्वसमातिषु ॥ एकस्मिन्बहुवचनं पूजार्थं ॥ रथप्रोष्ठेऽसमात् धारय ।
> दिवीव सूर्यं दिवि यथा सूर्यं दृशे सर्वेषां संदर्शनाय स्थापितवानसि
> तद्वदत्र बलं धारय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk he calls upon Indra for Asamāti's sake. O Indra, hold, maintain, powers (क्षत्रा (*kṣatrā*), strengths) in the Asamātis of the Rathaproṣṭha line. The plural for a single person is for honour. As in heaven you have set the sun for all to see, so maintain strength here.

### Printed p. 391

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—so as to be visible to all
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—as you have set the sun
- रथप्रोष्ठेषु (*rathaproṣṭheṣu*)—of the line of Rathaproṣṭha
- असमातिषु (*asamātiṣu*)—in the king named Asamāti
- क्षत्रा (*kṣatrā*)—strength
- धारय (*dhāraya*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you have set the sun in the sky so that all may see him, establish strength in the king named Asamāti, who belongs to the line of Rathaproṣṭha.

##### English translation
Maintain, Indra, vigour in the Rathaprostha Asamatis, as (you maintain) the sun in heaven for the sight (of all).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒गस्य॑स्य॒ नद्भ्यः॒ सप्ति॑ युनक्षि॒ रोहि॑ता ।  
> प॒णीन्न्य॑क्रमीर॒भि विश्वा॑न्ना जन्नरा॒धसः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अगस्यस्य । नत्भ्यः । सप्ति इति । युनक्षि । रोहिता ।  
> पणीन् । नि । अक्रमीः । अभि । विश्वान् । राजन् । अराधसः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयागस्य स्वसा बंभ्वादीनां माता राजानं स्तौति । हे राजन्नसमाते
> त्वमगस्त्यस्यर्षेर्नद्भो नंदयितृभ्यो बंध्वादिभ्यो निमित्तभूतेभ्यस्तेषां धनप्राप्तये सप्ति सर्पणस्वभावावश्त् रोहिता रोहितवर्णौ युनक्षि । योजय रथे ।
> तथा कृत्वा विश्वान् सर्वानराधसोऽदात्थनयजमानान्पणीन्वणिजो लुब्धकान्निकृष्णं नितरां वाभ्यक्रमीः ! अभिभव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk Agastya's sister-in-law, the mother of Bandhu and the others, praises the king. O King Asamāti, for the sake of the sage Agastya's नद्भ्यः (*nadbhyaḥ*), Bandhu and the others who gladden him and are the cause, so that they may obtain wealth, yoke to the chariot the two red horses (सप्ति (*sapti*)), which are of a darting nature. Having done so, overcome all the non-giving, non-sacrificing पणीन् (*paṇīn*), traders and misers, trampling them down utterly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O Asamāti
- अगस्त्यस्य (*agastyasya*)—of the sage Agastya
- नद्भ्यः (*nadbhyaḥ*)—to provide wealth to all the kinsmen
- रोहिता (*rohitā*)—golden-coloured
- सप्ति (*sapti*)—horses
- युनक्षि (*yunakṣi*)—yoke to the chariot

### Printed p. 392
Of the red horses: "non-sacrificers" (अराधसः (*arādhasaḥ*)) means those who are not performers of sacrifice. "All the Paṇis" (विश्वान् पणीन् (*viśvān paṇīn*)) means all the greedy ones. "Overcome" (नि अभि अक्रमीः (*ni abhi akramīḥ*)) means defeat and destroy.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Raja (the one without equal), yoke the golden-coloured horses to your chariot, to supply wealth to all the kinsmen of the sage Agastya. Defeat and destroy all the greedy ones who are not sacrificers.

##### English translation
Yoke the two red horses to your chariot, for the nephews of Agastya,
and overcome, Raja, all the niggard withholders of oblations.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं मा॒तायं पि॒तायं जी॒वातु॒राग॑मत् ।  
> इ॒दं तव॑ प्र॒सर्प॑णं॒ सुबं॑ध॒वेहि॒ निरि॑हि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । माता । अयं । पिता । अयं । जीवातुः । आ । अगमत् ।  
> इदं । तव । प्रसर्पणं । सुबंधो इति सुबंधो । आ । इहि । निः । इहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र शेषे शाट्यायनकं । अथाग्निं द्वैपदेन सूक्तेनास्तुवन् अग्निः स्तुत
> आजगाम। अगत्य चाह किंकामा मागच्छतेति। सुबंधोरेवासुं पुनर्वनुयामेत्यब्रुवन् । एषांतःपरिधीत्यब्रवीत्तमादध्वमिति । तन्निराह । अयं मातायं पितेति ।
> शौनकश्च ।
> स्तुतः स राजा सुप्रीतस्तस्थौ गौपायनानभि ।
> सूक्तेन तेऽस्तुवन्नग्निं द्वैपदेन यथात्रिषु ॥
> अथाग्निरब्रवीदेतानयमंत्रः परिध्यसुः ।
> सुबंधोरस्य चेक्ष्वाकोर्मया गुप्तो हितार्थिना ॥
> सुबंधवे प्रदायासुं जीवेत्युक्त्वा च पावकः ।
> स्तुतो गौपायनैः प्रीतो जगाम त्रिदिवं प्रति ॥
> आयं मातेति हृष्टास्ते सुबंधोरुसुमाह्वयन् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa cites the Śāṭyāyanaka for the remainder of the sūkta. The kinsmen praised Agni with a two-footed hymn, and Agni, praised, came. He asked them, "What do you desire? Why have you summoned me?" They said, "We wish to bring back the breath of Subandhu." Agni said that it was within the inner enclosure (परिधी (*paridhī*)), and told them to "fetch it". The words अयं मातायं पितेति (*ayaṃ mātāyaṃ piteti*) were that request. Śaunaka also says (in verses) that the king (Agni), praised and well pleased, stood before the Gaupāyanas. They had praised him with a sūkta of two-footed verses, as with the Atris. Agni said that this mantra was the enclosure of the breath, guarded by him for the good of Subandhu, the Ikṣvāku. Having given the breath to Subandhu with the words "live", Agni, pleased, went to heaven. The Gaupāyanas, glad, called out "अयं माता (*ayaṃ mātā*)" to Subandhu's breath.

### Printed p. 393

> शरीरमभिनिर्दिश्य सुबंधोः पतितं भुवि ।
> सूक्तशेषं जगुश्चास्य चेतसो धारणायत इति ॥
> (बृ.. ७-१०२२ रिंद १०७६)
> अयमग्निर्माता । अयमेव पिता । अयं जीवातुर्जीवयितागमत् ।
> आजगाम । अतो हे सुबंधो जीवपरिधौ वर्तमान इदं तव शरीरं तव प्रसर्पणं।
> प्रकर्षेण सर्पणसाधनं। आत इदं प्रत्येहि । आगच्छ। निरिहि। निर्गच्छ परिधेः सकाशात् ।
> अन्य एवं व्याचक्षते । हे निर्गतप्राण सुबंधो अयं ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ इयं
> मातायं पितायं जीवातुर्जीवनफलभूतः पुत्रश्चागमदिति संबध्यते । सर्वे
> त्वामागता दुःखिताः संतः । शिष्टं समानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(The Bṛhaddevatā quotation continues:) Pointing to Subandhu's body fallen on the ground, they sang the rest of the sūkta, "for the holding of his mind" (Bṛ. 7-1022 to 1076). Sāyaṇa then explains: this Agni is the mother, this same is the father, this is the giver of life, the reviver, who has come. So, O Subandhu, who stand in the enclosure of life, this body of yours is your means of moving forth; come to it, and go out from the enclosure. Others explain differently: O Subandhu, whose breath has departed, there is a change of case विभक्तिव्यत्ययः (*vibhaktivyatyayaḥ*); the sense is that this mother, this father and this son, the fruit of living, have come to you, all of them grieving. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुबंधो (*subaṃdho*)—O Subandhu
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Agni
- माता (*mātā*)—your mother
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Agni
- पिता (*pitā*)—your father
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Agni
- जीवातुः (*jīvātuḥ*)—the one who gives you life
- अगमत् (*agamat*)—has come here
- प्रसर्पणं (*prasarpaṇaṃ*)—that moves
- तव इदं (*tava idaṃ*)—to this body of yours
- एहि (*ehi*)—come and enter
- निरिहि (*nirihi*)—come out from the enclosure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Subandhu, this Agni is himself your mother and father. This Agni, who fills you with life, has come here. Come and enter your body, which is of a moving nature. Come out of the enclosure.
Or else:
O Subandhu, hearing of your death, your mother, father and child have all come, grieving. Enter the body again and live. Become a bringer of happiness to them. Sāyaṇa has indicated that another meaning of this kind is possible.

##### English translation
This (Agni) your mother, this your father, this the giver of life to
you, has arrived ; come back, Subandhu, to this your (body) that is
capable of motion; come forth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the explanation of this Ṛk the commentator has quoted a passage of the Śāṭyāyana Brāhmaṇa: अथाग्निं द्वैपदेन सूक्तेनास्तुवन् अग्निः स्तुत आजगाम। अगत्य चाह किंकामा मागच्छतेति। सुबंधोरेवासुं पुनर्वनुयामेत्यब्रुवन् । एषांतःपरिधीत्यब्रवीत्तमादध्वमिति । तन्निराह । अयं मातायं पितेति । (*athāgniṃ dvaipadena sūktenāstuvan agniḥ stuta ājagāma| agatya cāha kiṃkāmā māgacchateti| subaṃdhorevāsuṃ punarvanuyāmetyabruvan | eṣāṃtaḥparidhītyabravīttamādadhvamiti | tannirāha | ayaṃ mātāyaṃ piteti |*)

### Printed p. 394
The kinsmen and others praised Agni with a sūkta in the Dvipadā Virāj metre (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-24). Agni, pleased with it, came there and asked, "What is your wish? Why did you summon me?" They said, "We wish that the breath of this Subandhu should return." Agni said that Subandhu's breath was in his inner enclosure, and they prayed that it be brought. That prayer is what is said in this Ṛk beginning आयं माता (*āyaṃ mātā*).
The great sage Śaunaka too, in his work the Bṛhaddevatā, has described this matter, beginning with स्तुतः स राजा सुप्रीतः (*stutaḥ sa rājā suprītaḥ*) and ending with चेतसो धारणाय ते (*cetaso dhāraṇāya te*). We have explained this in the introduction to Sūkta 57 (pp. 352-353).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ यु॒गं व॑र॒त्रया॒ नह्यं॑ति ध॒रुणा॑य॒ कं ।  
> ए॒वा दा॑धार ते॒ मनो॑ जी॒वात॑वे॒ न मृ॒त्यवेऽथो॑ अरि॒ष्टता॑तये ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । युगं । वरत्रया । नह्यंति । धरुणाय । कं ।  
> विव । दाधार । ते । मनः । जीवातवे । न । मृत्यवे । अथो इति । अरिष्टतातये ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यथा युगं वरत्रया पाशेन नह्यंति बध्यंति धरुणाय रथादिधारणाय ।
> कमिति पादपूरणः । एवैवं ते मनो दाधार परिधावग्निः । किमर्थं । जीवातवे
> जीवनाय न मृत्यवे मरणाय न अथो अपि चारिष्टतातयेऽविनाशाय ॥
> स्वार्थिकस्तातिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As men bind the yoke with a cord, a bond, for the holding of the chariot and the like, so Agni has held your mind in the enclosure. For what? For life, not for death, and also for non-destruction. कं (*kaṃ*) is a metrical filler. The affix तातिः (*tātiḥ*) is used without added sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- युगं (*yugaṃ*)—the yoke
- धरुणाय (*dharuṇāya*)—so that it stands firm
- वरत्रया (*varatrayā*)—with a rope
- नह्यंति (*nahyaṃti*)—they bind
- एव (*eva*)—in the same manner
- ते मनः (*te manaḥ*)—your consciousness
- जीवातवे (*jīvātave*)—for living
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—he has joined and established in the enclosure
- अरिष्टतातये (*ariṣṭatātaye*)—for welfare only
- न मृत्यवे (*na mṛtyave*)—not established for dying

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As men bind the yoke with a rope so that it stands firm, in the same way Agni has joined and established your consciousness in the enclosure so that it may live. He has established it for the gain of welfare, not for its death.

As men bind the yoke with cords for its support, so has (Agni) placed your spirit (in the body) for life, not for death, but for security.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वातो वायुर्द्युलोकान्नग्नीचीनमव वाति। गच्छति। सूर्यश्च न्यक् तपति।
> अघ्नाहननीया गौर्निचीनं दुहे । दुग्धे। एवं ते रपः पापं न्यग्नीचीनं भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wind blows downward from the heavenly world; the sun too burns downward. The unslayable cow, the one not to be killed, yields milk downward. So let your sin (रपः (*rapaḥ*)) be turned downward.

- न्यक् (*nyak*)—downward-facing

- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- न्यक् (*nyak*)—with downward-turned rays
- तपति (*tapati*)—burns
- अघ्ना (*aghnā*)—the cow worthy of protection
- नीचीनं (*nīcīnaṃ*)—from the udder in the lower part
- दुहे (*duhe*)—yields milk
- ते (*te*)—your
- रपः (*rapaḥ*)—sin
- न्यक् भवतु (*nyak bhavatu*)—let it be one that goes downward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### English translation

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । मे । हस्तः । भगवान् । अयं । मे । भगवत्तरः ।  
> अयं । मे । विश्वभेषजः । अयं । शिवअभिमर्शनः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया बंध्वादयो लब्धजीवं सुबंधुं पाणिभिरस्पृशन् । अयं मे हस्तो
> भगवान् यस्मात्सजीवं सुबंधुं स्पृशति तस्मात् । तथायं मे हस्तो भगवत्तरः ।
> अतिशयेन भगवान् । तथायं मे हस्तो विश्वभेषजो जीवचिकित्सासाधनसर्वौषधवान् तत्स्थानीयो वा । अयं शिवाभिमर्शनो मंगलस्पर्शनः । यतो जीवंतं
> स्पृशत्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk the kinsmen and others touched Subandhu, who had regained life, with their hands. "This hand of mine is blessed (भगवान् (*bhagavān*))", since it touches the living Subandhu. So "this hand of mine is more blessed", blessed in the highest degree. So "this hand of mine is the all-healing one", possessing all the medicines that serve for the healing of the living, or standing in their place. "This is the touch of auspiciousness", the touch that brings good fortune; the meaning is that it touches one who is alive, hence so.

### Printed p. 398
## Sūkta 61 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—my (the one who touches the living Subandhu)
- अयं हस्तः (*ayaṃ hastaḥ*)—this hand
- भगवान् (*bhagavān*)—is blessed
- मे (*me*)—my
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—the other hand
- भगवत्तरः (*bhagavattaraḥ*)—is still more blessed
- अयं मे (*ayaṃ me*)—this hand of mine
- विश्वभेषजः (*viśvabheṣajaḥ*)—possesses the medicine that makes a dead man live
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this hand of mine
- शिवाभिमर्शनः (*śivābhimarśanaḥ*)—has a touch that brings welfare

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This hand of mine, which touches the living Subandhu, is blessed. My other hand is still more blessed. This hand of mine possesses the medicine that makes a dead man live. This hand of mine has a touch that brings welfare.

##### English translation
(The Rishis speak :) This my hand is fortunate ; this my (other hand) is (still) more fortunate : this my (hand) has all medicaments : this has a blessed touch.

**Introduction**
An account concerning this sūkta is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 22-14) and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4). It is set out here.

At the time of reciting the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, many sūktas addressed to several deities have to be recited. Among them two sūktas addressed to the Viśvedevas must also be recited:

इदमित्था रौद्रं गूर्तवचा ये यज्ञेन दक्षिणया समक्ता इति वैश्वदेवं ॥ (*idamitthā raudraṃ gūrtavacā ye yajñena dakṣiṇayā samaktā iti vaiśvadevaṃ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 22-13)

These are: the 61st sūkta of the 10th Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, beginning इदमित्था रौद्रं गूर्तवचा (*idamitthā raudraṃ gūrtavacā*), and the 62nd sūkta, beginning ये यज्ञेन दक्षिणया समक्ता (*ye yajñena dakṣiṇayā samaktā*), are to be recited.

नाभानेदिष्टं शंसति । (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ śaṃsati |*) (Ai. Brā. 22-14)

These sūktas are called the Nābhānediṣṭa sūktas, because the seer (draṣṭṛ) of these sūktas is the ṛṣi named Nābhānediṣṭa. It is customary to name a sūkta after its ṛṣi; therefore these sūktas are called Nābhānediṣṭa sūktas. There is an account concerning this ṛṣi Nābhānediṣṭa. It is set out here:

### Printed p. 399
नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजन्सोब्रवी- देत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्येतमेव निष्ठावमववदितारमित्यब्रुवंस्तस्माद्धाष्येतर्हि पितरं पुत्रा निष्ठावोऽववदितेत्येवाचक्षते ॥ म (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ bhrātaro nirabhajansobravī- detya kiṃ mahyamabhāktetyetameva niṣṭhāvamavavaditāramityabruvaṃstasmāddhāṣyetarhi pitaraṃ putrā niṣṭhāvo 'vavaditetyevācakṣate ‖ ma*)

Nābhānediṣṭa, the son of Manu, as soon as he had undergone the upanayana, lived in the teacher's house in brahmacarya and studied the Veda. While he was away from his father's house, his elder brothers reflected selfishly: "Our younger brother Nābhānediṣṭa is still a boy; he is studying in the teacher's house. He has no need of wealth. So let us share our father's wealth and property among ourselves." Leaving nothing for Nābhānediṣṭa, they divided all the property that there was among themselves. After some time Nābhānediṣṭa finished his studies, came back from the teacher's house and said to his elder brothers: "Brothers, you have shared out the whole property among yourselves. You have left nothing for me. Where is my share of the property?" At this they pointed with the hand to their father Manu, who was standing there, and said: "Nābhānediṣṭa, ask your father; we know nothing of this matter. Your father is one who has fixed the Dharmaśāstra itself and knows well the secret of dharma. Ask him." (Ai. Brā. 22-14)

Here the words निष्ठावः (*niṣṭhāvaḥ*) and अववदिता (*avavaditā*) are used. It is necessary to explain them.

धनविभागादेर्धर्मरहस्यं निःशेषेण स्थितिनिर्णयो निष्ठा । सा यस्मिन्नस्ति स निष्ठावः । तादृशं धर्मरहस्यनिर्णेतारमित्यर्थः ॥ (*dhanavibhāgāderdharmarahasyaṃ niḥśeṣeṇa sthitinirṇayo niṣṭhā | sā yasminnasti sa niṣṭhāvaḥ | tādṛśaṃ dharmarahasyanirṇetāramityarthaḥ ‖*) (Sā. Bhā.) **NOTE**

The making of a decision, in the division of wealth, by knowing the secret of dharma and acting according to it, is called niṣṭhā. A man in whom such niṣṭhā exists is called niṣṭhāvat. That is, the meaning is a man able to know the secret of dharma and accordingly to divide the wealth among sons and others.

अववदितारं । ज्येष्ठपुत्रस्यैतावत् । द्वितीयस्यैतावत् । अन्यस्यैतावत् ! इत्यवच्छिद्य वदितुं समर्थोऽवनवदिता । तादृशं । आयं मनुर्धर्मशास्त्रकर्तृत्वाद्धर्मरहस्यनिर्णयवान्पितृत्वेन तनैतावदित्यवच्छिद्य वक्तुं समर्थश्च ॥ (*avavaditāraṃ | jyeṣṭhaputrasyaitāvat | dvitīyasyaitāvat | anyasyaitāvat ! ityavacchidya vadituṃ samartho 'vanavaditā | tādṛśaṃ | āyaṃ manurdharmaśāstrakartṛtvāddharmarahasyanirṇayavānpitṛtvena tanaitāvadityavacchidya vaktuṃ samarthaśca ‖*) (Sā. Bhā.)

One who divides separately—so much for the eldest son, so much for the second, so much for the third—and states it before them. Here, since Manu is the author of the Dharmaśāstra, he knows the secret of dharma and has divided the property among his sons accordingly. In this matter he is himself competent. Therefore the elder brothers said to their younger brother Nābhānediṣṭa: "Ask him about your property." This is the meaning.

### Printed p. 400
स पितरमेत्याब्रवीत्वां ह वाव मह्यं त (ता) ताभाक्षुरिति तं पिताब्रवीन्मा पुत्रक तदादृथा अंगिरसो वा इमे स्वर्गाय लोकाय सत्रमासते ते षष्ठं पष्ठमेवाहरागत्य मुह्यंति तानेते सूक्ते षष्ठेऽहनि शंसय तेषां यत्सहस्रं सत्रपरिवेषणं तत्ते स्वयंतो दास्यंतीति तथेति ॥ (*sa pitarametyābravītvāṃ ha vāva mahyaṃ ta (tā) tābhākṣuriti taṃ pitābravīnmā putraka tadādṛthā aṃgiraso vā ime svargāya lokāya satramāsate te ṣaṣṭhaṃ paṣṭhamevāharāgatya muhyaṃti tānete sūkte ṣaṣṭhe 'hani śaṃsaya teṣāṃ yatsahasraṃ satrapariveṣaṇaṃ tatte svayaṃto dāsyaṃtīti tatheti ‖*)

Then, according to his brothers' word, Nābhānediṣṭa came to his father and said: "Father, my elder brothers said, 'It is you who divided the property for us, so my share is with you; take it from him.' Therefore give me the share of the property that remains with you." Hearing this, his father Manu said: "Boy, do not put faith in your brothers' word; what they said is not true. The share due to you is not with me. They took everything themselves. Yet do not worry. I shall tell you a way by which you may obtain wealth; listen. In a place near here the great ṛṣis called Aṅgirases, desiring to go to heaven, are performing a sattra sacrifice for that purpose. Though they began the sattra many times before, they were not able to complete it. On the sixth day of that sacrifice, at the time of reciting the mantras, they do not know which mantra suited to the occasion should be recited, and are in doubt. Without the completion of the sattra they have not obtained heaven. Therefore they are greatly anxious. On the sixth day of the sattra go to their sacrifice and recite the sūktas इदमित्था (*idamitthā*) and ये यज्ञेन (*ye yajñena*) (the 61st and 62nd sūktas of the 10th Maṇḍala). Thereby the sattra they are performing will be completed, and they will give you whatever remains of the wealth, a thousand in number, gathered for the sacrifice." Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭa agreed, "So be it," and set out for their sacrifice.

तानुपैत्यतिगृभ्नीत मानवं सुमेधस इति तमब्रुवन्निंकामो वदसीतीदमेव वः षष्ठमहः प्रज्ञापयानीत्यब्रवीदथ यद्व एतत्सहस्रं सत्रपरिवेषणं तन्ने स्वर्यंतो दत्तेति तथेति तानेते सूक्ते पष्ठेऽहन्यशंसयत्ततो वै ते प्र यज्ञमजानन्द्र स्वर्गं लोकं तद्यदेते सूक्ते षष्ठेऽहनि शंसति यज्ञस्य प्रज्ञात्यै स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यैः ॥ (*tānupaityatigṛbhnīta mānavaṃ sumedhasa iti tamabruvanniṃkāmo vadasītīdameva vaḥ ṣaṣṭhamahaḥ prajñāpayānītyabravīdatha yadva etatsahasraṃ satrapariveṣaṇaṃ tanne svaryaṃto datteti tatheti tānete sūkte paṣṭhe 'hanyaśaṃsayattato vai te pra yajñamajānandra svargaṃ lokaṃ tadyadete sūkte ṣaṣṭhe 'hani śaṃsati yajñasya prajñātyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyaiḥ ‖*)

Then Nābhānediṣṭa went to the place where the Aṅgirases were sacrificing, and addressing them prayed: प्रति गृभ्नित मानवं सुमेधसः (*prati gṛbhnita mānavaṃ sumedhasaḥ*) (this is the last pāda of the Ṛks 1-4 of Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-62). "O wise ṛṣis, accept me, the son of Manu (Nābhānediṣṭa)." Hearing this, the Aṅgirases asked: "Nābhānediṣṭa, what do you desire? For what have you come to us and speak thus?" Nābhānediṣṭa replied: "O ṛṣis, this is the sixth day of the sattra that you are now performing. I shall remove the doubt that you have as to which mantras are to be recited today and how the rite is to be performed, and I shall tell you what is to be done next. When you have thus completed the sattra and are going to heaven, give me the thousand cows left over from what was gathered for the sacrifice, and the other wealth."

### Printed p. 401
The ṛṣis agreed, "So be it", and Nābhānediṣṭa recited the sūkta इदमित्था रौद्रं (*idamitthā raudraṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10 61) and the sūkta ये यज्ञेन (*ye yajñena*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 11-62) **NOTE** and had them recited by them too. Thereby the ṛṣis' sacrifice was completed in all its parts, and they came to know the form of the performance of the sacrifice and the attainment of the heavenly world. Therefore on the sixth day of the sacrifice the hotṛ must recite these two sūktas. Thereby the performance of the sacrifice and the attainment of heaven come about.

तं स्वर्यंतोऽब्रवन्नेतत्ते ब्राह्मण सहस्रमिति तदेनं समाकुर्वाणं पुरुषः कृष्णशवास्युत्तरत उपोत्थायाब्रवीन्मम ना इदं मम वै वास्तुहमिति सोऽब्रवीन्मह्यं ना इदमदुरिति तमब्रवीत्तद्वैन्‌ तनैव पितरि प्रश्नॆ इति स पितरमैत्तं पिताब्रवीन्ननु ते पुत्रकादू ३ रित्यदुरेव म इत्यब्रवीत्तत्तु मे पुरुषः कृष्णशवास्युत्तरत उपोदतिष्ठन्मम ना इदं मम वै वास्तुहमित्यादितेति तं पिताब्रवीत्तस्यैव पुत्रकॆ तत्तत्तु स तुभ्यं दास्यतीति स पुनरेत्याब्रवीत्तव ह वाव किल भगव इदमिति मे पिताहेति सोऽब्रवीत्तदहं तुभ्यमेव ददामि य विव सत्यमवादीरिति ॥ (*taṃ svaryaṃto 'bravannetatte brāhmaṇa sahasramiti tadenaṃ samākurvāṇaṃ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśavāsyuttarata upotthāyābravīnmama nā idaṃ mama vai vāstuhamiti so 'bravīnmahyaṃ nā idamaduriti tamabravīttadvain tanaiva pitari praśnè iti sa pitaramaittaṃ pitābravīnnanu te putrakādū 3 rityadureva ma ityabravīttattu me puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśavāsyuttarata upodatiṣṭhanmama nā idaṃ mama vai vāstuhamityāditeti taṃ pitābravīttasyaiva putrakè tattattu sa tubhyaṃ dāsyatīti sa punaretyābravīttava ha vāva kila bhagava idamiti me pitāheti so 'bravīttadahaṃ tubhyameva dadāmi ya viva satyamavādīriti ‖*)

When the sacrifice was completed, the ṛṣis called Nābhānediṣṭa and said: "Brāhmaṇa, we are going to heaven. So we have no need of these cows. As said before, we have given you these thousand cows. Take them." [Here, in the Brāhmaṇa sentence above, only the word सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*) occurs. As to how the word सहस्र (*sahasra*) comes to mean a thousand cows, the commentator cites a Brāhmaṇa sentence of another śākhā:] ते सुवर्गं लोकं यंतो य एषां पशव आसंस्तानस्मा अददुः (*te suvargaṃ lokaṃ yaṃto ya eṣāṃ paśava āsaṃstānasmā adaduḥ*). According to the ṛṣis' word Nābhānediṣṭa was gathering the cows they had given to himself, when on the northern side of that sacrificial ground a man wearing dirty clothes appeared and said to Nābhānediṣṭa: (In the original it is कृष्णशवासी (*kṛṣṇaśavāsī*).)

अतिशयेन कृष्णं मलिनं वस्त्रं कृष्णशं तद्वस्त्र आच्छादयतीति कृष्णशवासी । (*atiśayena kṛṣṇaṃ malinaṃ vastraṃ kṛṣṇaśaṃ tadvastra ācchādayatīti kṛṣṇaśavāsī |*) अत्रायं मलिनवस्त्रः पुरुषः पशुस्वामी रुद्र इत्यवगंतव्यं । (*atrāyaṃ malinavastraḥ puruṣaḥ paśusvāmī rudra ityavagaṃtavyaṃ |*) तथा च शाखांतरे पठ्यते—तं पशुभिश्चरंतं यज्ञवास्तौ रुद्र आसच्छत् । (*tathā ca śākhāṃtare paṭhyate—taṃ paśubhiścaraṃtaṃ yajñavāstau rudra āsacchat |*)

That which is extremely dirty is called kṛṣṇaśa, and one who wears such a dirty garment is called kṛṣṇaśavāsī. Here the wearer of the dirty garment is none other than Rudra. On this the śruti sentence is: तं पशुभिश्चरंतं यज्ञवास्तौ रुद्र आगच्छत् (*taṃ paśubhiścaraṃtaṃ yajñavāstau rudra āgacchat*). He said: "Nābhānediṣṭa, all the animals that remain in this sacrificial ground are mine. You must not take them." (In the original

### Printed p. 402
the word वास्तुहं (*vāstuhaṃ*) is used. वास्तु (*vāstu*) means the sacrificial ground.)

वास्तौ यज्ञभूमौ हीनं कर्मांते परित्यक्तं वास्तुहं तादृशं सर्वं ममैव स्वं (*vāstau yajñabhūmau hīnaṃ karmāṃte parityaktaṃ vāstuhaṃ tādṛśaṃ sarvaṃ mamaiva svaṃ*)—after the completion of the rite, all that is left in the sacrificial ground is my property and so must come to me: such is Rudra's statement.

Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭa said to that man: "Rudra, the Aṅgirases gave me these thousand cows. Therefore they are mine." Then Rudra said: "Nābhānediṣṭa, since I say these cows are mine and you say they must belong to you, the settlement of this question must come from your father. So go to your father, ask whose these cows are, and come back." According to Rudra's word Nābhānediṣṭa went to his father. His father Manu asked him: "Boy, did the Aṅgirases not give you cows?" Nābhānediṣṭa said: "The Aṅgirasa ṛṣis gave me cows." Manu asked: "Then what is the matter now? Why have you come empty-handed, without bringing the cows?" Nābhānediṣṭa said: "The ṛṣis gave me the cows. When I was taking them, a man in dirty clothes came from the northern direction of the sacrificial ground and said, 'All these thousand cows are mine, for I am the owner of what remains in the sacrificial ground after the rite is completed,' and he took all those cows himself." Having said this he stood silent. Then his father said: "Son, what that man in dirty clothes says is right. Rudra is the owner of the cows and other wealth that remain in the sacrificial ground; for Rudra is the lord of animals, and he is also the owner of what remains of the sacrifice. Even so, do not worry about this matter. That Rudra will give the cows to you himself." So he sent him back. Hearing his father's word, Nābhānediṣṭa came again to Rudra and told him his father's word thus: "All these animals belonged to the Aṅgirases during the sacrifice. After the completion of the sacrifice, Rudra is the master of the remaining animals and wealth. Therefore the Aṅgirases have no authority to give them to others. So, revered one, all this is yours." Thus he told Rudra his father's statement. (The commentator cites a śruti sentence for Rudra's statement in another śākhā:) न वै तस्य तदीशत इत्यब्रवीद्यज्ञवास्तौ हीयते मम वै तत् (*na vai tasya tadīśata ityabravīdyajñavāstau hīyate mama vai tat*). Rudra was pleased with Nābhānediṣṭa's word and said: "Brāhmaṇa, since you have spoken the truth without telling a lie, I give you those thousand cows; take them." And he gave him the thousand cows.

तस्मादेवं विदुषा सत्यमेव वदितव्यं स एष सहस्रनिर्मंत्रो यन्नाभानेदिष्यः उपैनं सहस्रं नमति प्र षष्ठेनाह्ना स्वर्गं लोकं जानाति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tasmādevaṃ viduṣā satyameva vaditavyaṃ sa eṣa sahasranirmaṃtro yannābhānediṣyaḥ upainaṃ sahasraṃ namati pra ṣaṣṭhenāhnā svargaṃ lokaṃ jānāti ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 22-14)

### Printed p. 403
Therefore a learned man, who knows everything, should always speak the truth. Since this mantra recited by Nābhānediṣṭa gives things a thousand in number, it is famous as सहस्रसनिः (*sahasrasaniḥ*). The man who knows this mantra and its meaning obtains wealth a thousand in number, and also comes to know the method of reaching the heavenly world by performing the rite accordingly on the sixth day of the sacrifice.

This matter is also treated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. In explaining the Manthi-saṃsrāva homa, this account is given to show its necessity:

मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत्स नाभानेदिष्टं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं निरभजत्स आगच्छत्सोऽब्रवीत्कथा मा निरभागिति न त्वा निरभाक्षमित्यब्रवीदंगिरस इमे सत्रमासते ते सुवर्गं लोकं न प्र जानंति तेभ्य इदं ब्राह्मणं ब्रूहि ते सुवर्गं लोकं यंतो य एषां पशवस्ताग् स्ते दास्यंतीति तदेभ्योऽब्रवीत्ते सुवर्गं लोकं यंतो य एषां पशव आसन्तानस्मा अददुस्तं पशुभिश्चरंतं यज्ञवास्तौ रुद्र आगच्छत्सोऽब्रवीन्मम वा इमे पशव इत्यदुर्वै मह्यमिमानित्यब्रवीन्न वै तस्य त ईशत इत्यब्रवीद्यज्ञवास्तौ हीयते मम वै तदिति तस्माद्यज्ञवास्तु नाभ्यवेत्यग्ं सोऽब्रवीद्यज्ञे माभजाथ ते पशून्नाभि मग्गस्य इति तस्मा एतं मंथिनस्सग्ं स्रावमजुहोत्ततो वै तस्य रुद्रः पशून्नाभ्यमन्यत यत्रैतमेवं विद्वान्मंथिनस्सग्स्रावं जुहोति न तत्र रुद्रः पशूनभि मन्यते ॥ (*manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ vyabhajatsa nābhānediṣṭaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ nirabhajatsa āgacchatso 'bravītkathā mā nirabhāgiti na tvā nirabhākṣamityabravīdaṃgirasa ime satramāsate te suvargaṃ lokaṃ na pra jānaṃti tebhya idaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūhi te suvargaṃ lokaṃ yaṃto ya eṣāṃ paśavastāg ste dāsyaṃtīti tadebhyo 'bravītte suvargaṃ lokaṃ yaṃto ya eṣāṃ paśava āsantānasmā adadustaṃ paśubhiścaraṃtaṃ yajñavāstau rudra āgacchatso 'bravīnmama vā ime paśava ityadurvai mahyamimānityabravīnna vai tasya ta īśata ityabravīdyajñavāstau hīyate mama vai taditi tasmādyajñavāstu nābhyavetyagṃ so 'bravīdyajñe mābhajātha te paśūnnābhi maggasya iti tasmā etaṃ maṃthinassagṃ srāvamajuhottato vai tasya rudraḥ paśūnnābhyamanyata yatraitamevaṃ vidvānmaṃthinassagsrāvaṃ juhoti na tatra rudraḥ paśūnabhi manyate ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4,5,6,7)

In former times Manu divided his property among his sons. At that time his youngest son, Nābhānediṣṭa, was not with his father; he was with his teacher, observing the vow of brahmacarya and studying the Veda. So, whether because he was not remembered, or at the prompting of his elder brothers, or for some other reason, Manu divided and distributed all the property among the sons other than Nābhānediṣṭa. After some time Nābhānediṣṭa, who was in the teacher's house, finished his studies and came to his father. Seeing that all the property had gone to his elder brothers and that he had nothing, he asked his father: "Father, why did you not give me a share in the property?" Manu answered: "Son, I have not left you without a share in the property. I shall tell you what you have; listen. The ṛṣis called Aṅgirases, desiring to go to heaven, are now performing a sattra. But they do not know which mantra is to be recited for the attainment of heaven, or what is the means of reaching heaven, and are in perplexity

### Printed p. 404
Continuing the narrative (Manu to his son): "You go to the sacrificial ground where they are performing the sacrifice and make this mantra (the 61st and 62nd sūktas of the 10th Maṇḍala of the Ṛ. Saṃ.) known to them. Thereby they will complete the sacrifice in full, and will give you the animals left over from those gathered for the sacrifice. That is your share." So Nābhānediṣṭha went to the Aṅgirases and taught the mantra his father had told him. They were pleased, completed the sacrifice, and at the time of going to heaven gave Nābhānediṣṭha all the cows left over as the remainder of the sacrifice. While he was taking those animals, Rudra, who was moving about there on the sacrificial ground, came and stopped him: "O Nābhānediṣṭha, these animals are mine; you must not take them." Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭha said: "O Rudra, the Aṅgirases have given these animals; therefore they must belong to me." Rudra replied: "The Aṅgirases are not the owners of the animals left over at the close of the sacrifice. They have no authority over them, and therefore no authority to give them to others. The ownership of them belongs to me." And he added: "O Nābhānediṣṭha, if you want these cows, worship me in the sacrifice, that is, offer the manthi-saṃsrāva oblation to me. Then I shall be pleased and shall consent to your taking the animals." Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭha offered the manthi-saṃsrāva oblation and obtained the cows. Therefore, if a wise man offers the manthi-saṃsrāva oblation to Rudra, Rudra puts no obstacle in his way in the matter of obtaining animals.

The account in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa differs a little in its last part; in the main points there is no difference. The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa describes as follows the Aṅgirases' performance of the sattra mentioned in this account:

अंगिरसो वै सत्रमासत । तेषां पृश्नि र्घर्मधुगासीत् । सर्जिषेणाजीवत् । तेऽब्रुवन् । कस्यै नु सत्रमास्महे । येऽस्या ओषधीर्न जनयाम इति । ते दिवो वृष्टिमसृजंत । यावंतस्तोका अवापद्यंत । तावतीरोषधयोऽजायंत । ता जाताः पितरो विषेणालिंपन् । तासां जग्ध्वा रुष्यंत्यैत् । तेऽब्रुवन् । क इदमित्तमकरिति । वयं भागधेयमिच्छमाना इति पितरोऽब्रुवन् । किं वो भागधेयमिति । अग्निहोत्र एव नोऽप्यस्तित्यब्रुवन् । तेभ्य एतद्भागधेयं प्रायच्छन् । यद्दुत्वा निमार्ष्टि । ततो वै त ओषधीरसद्वयन् । य एवं वेद । स्वदंतेऽस्मा ओषधयः । ते वत्समुपावासृजन् । इदं नो हव्यं प्रदापयेति । सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै । दश मा रात्रीर्जातं न दोहन् । आसंगवं मात्रा सह चराणीति । तस्माद्वत्सं जातं दश रात्रीर्न दुहंति । आसंगवं मात्रा सह चरति । वारे- (*aṃgiraso vai satramāsata | teṣāṃ pṛśni rgharmadhugāsīt | sarjiṣeṇājīvat | te 'bruvan | kasyai nu satramāsmahe | ye 'syā oṣadhīrna janayāma iti | te divo vṛṣṭimasṛjaṃta | yāvaṃtastokā avāpadyaṃta | tāvatīroṣadhayo 'jāyaṃta | tā jātāḥ pitaro viṣeṇāliṃpan | tāsāṃ jagdhvā ruṣyaṃtyait | te 'bruvan | ka idamittamakariti | vayaṃ bhāgadheyamicchamānā iti pitaro 'bruvan | kiṃ vo bhāgadheyamiti | agnihotra eva no 'pyastityabruvan | tebhya etadbhāgadheyaṃ prāyacchan | yaddutvā nimārṣṭi | tato vai ta oṣadhīrasadvayan | ya evaṃ veda | svadaṃte 'smā oṣadhayaḥ | te vatsamupāvāsṛjan | idaṃ no havyaṃ pradāpayeti | so 'bravīdvaraṃ vṛṇai | daśa mā rātrīrjātaṃ na dohan | āsaṃgavaṃ mātrā saha carāṇīti | tasmādvatsaṃ jātaṃ daśa rātrīrna duhaṃti | āsaṃgavaṃ mātrā saha carati | vāre-*)

### Printed p. 405
वृतग् ह्यस्य । तस्माद्वत्सग्ं सग्‌ंसृष्टधयग्ं रुद्रो घातुकः । अति हि संधां धयति ॥ (*vṛtag hyasya | tasmādvatsagṃ sagṃsṛṣṭadhayagṃ rudro ghātukaḥ | ati hi saṃdhāṃ dhayati ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 2-1-1-1, 2, 3)

To explain the Agnihotra, the matter of the sattra performed by the Aṅgiras sages is introduced as a preface. When the Aṅgirases performed the sattra, a white cow named Pṛśni (renowned as the mother of the Marut deities; we have explained this at length earlier) was being milked for the Pravargya. At that time, because of drought, there was a want of grass, the food of cows; so the cow Pṛśni had to live on the husks of Soma plants from which the juice, called ṛjīṣa, had been pressed. Seeing Pṛśni in this distress for food, the Aṅgiras sages said among themselves: "For what purpose are we performing the sattra? This cow suffers for want of grass and the like; what is to be done? We must make green grass and other plants and herbs grow abundantly. For this we must bring rain from the sky." So they reflected and produced rain. As many drops as fell on the earth from that rain, so many plants and herbs came into being. Then the Pitṛ deities, wishing to have a share in the Agnihotra for themselves, and to obtain it, smeared the plants produced by the rain with poison and made them bitter. Eating the bitter grass, Pṛśni fell into a swoon. Seeing this, the Aṅgirases asked: "Who made this grass bitter?" The Pitṛs answered: "Wishing a share in the oblation, we ourselves made it bitter for that purpose." Asked again, "What is your share? What do you want?", they said: "Let us too have a share in the Agnihotra." The Aṅgirases said "So be it" and gave the Pitṛs a share (the oblation "svadhā to the Pitṛs"); the Pitṛs then removed the bitterness from the grass and made it sweet and tasty. For the man who knows this, grass, creepers and the like are always sweet (tasty).

Afterwards the Aṅgirases brought the calf to the cow in order to milk her and said: "O calf, milk is needed for preparing the oblation in the sacrifice; give it to us." The calf replied: "If you want milk, you must grant me a boon: after a calf is born, the cow must not be milked for ten nights (ten days); and even after the ten days, whenever she is milked, I must, every day, drink milk along with my mother for half a prahara and move about happily." The sages agreed, "So be it," and granted the boon. Therefore even now, when a cow is milked for the sacrifice,

### Printed p. 406
a cow that has newly calved is not milked for ten days, and the calf stays by its mother drinking the milk. If, contrary to this, anyone milks for the oblation before ten days have passed, or after the ten nights milks out all the milk in the udder and leaves none for the calf, Rudra himself punishes such a man and destroys his sacrifice. Such is the explanation of this account.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पंचमेऽनुवाकेऽष्टौ सूक्तानि । तत्रेदमित्थेति सप्तविंशत्यचं प्रथमं
> सूक्तं मानवस्य नाभानेदिष्टस्यार्षं त्रिष्टुभं।इदमादीनि षट् सूक्तानि वैश्वदेवानि।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । इदमित्था सप्ताधिका नाभानेदिष्टो मानवो वैश्वदेवं तदिति ॥
> पृष्ठस्यषष्ठेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र अभिप्लविकातिदेशप्राप्तस्योषासानक्केत्यस्य स्थान इदं
> सूक्तं सूत्रितं च। उद्धृत्य चोत्तमं सूक्तं त्रीणेदमित्था रौद्रमिति। आ.८-१। इति॥
> अत्रैतरेयब्राह्मणं । नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजंत्सोऽब्रवीदेत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्येतमेव निष्कामवनवदितारमित्यब्रुवन्नित्यादि।
> ऐ. ब्रा. ५-१४ ॥ तत्र नाभानेदिष्टो भ्रातृभिर्भागे निराकृतः पितृसामीप्यमागत्य किं
> मह्यं भागं न कल्पितवानसीत्यपृच्छत् । स च किमनेन भागेन । अंगिरसः स्वर्गार्थं
> सत्त्रमासीनाः षष्ठाहःपर्यंतमनुष्ठाय मुह्यंति । तानिदमित्थेति सूक्ते शंसय ते
> स्वर्गं यंतो वसिष्ठा गाः सहस्रसंख्याकान्दास्यंतीति पित्रा प्रेरितोऽंगिरसां समीपमागत्य तेभ्यः सत्प्रपरिवेषणं गोसहस्रमुत्कोचं परिकल्प्य तानेते सूक्ते षष्ठेऽहन्यशंसयत् । ते च तत्तूक्तसामर्थ्याद्यज्ञं पारं प्रापय्य स्वर्जिगमिषवोऽस्मै
> गोसहस्रं प्रादुः । शं च तद्योसहस्रं स्वीकुर्वाणं कश्चन कृष्णशवासी पुरुष
> उत्तरत उत्थाय ब्राह्मण मदीयं यज्ञशेषभागं मा स्वीकुर्वित्यब्रवीत् । स च
> मह्यमंगिरसः प्राद्दुरिति प्रत्यब्रवीत् । तर्हि ब्राह्मण तव पितरमेव पृच्छ कस्यॆ भागः
> प्राप्पुयादित्युक्तः पितृसमीपनागत्य पित्रा रुद्रायायं न्याय्य इति तेनोक्तस्तवैवायं भाग इति मम पिताब्रवीदिति प्रत्युवाच । ततो यथार्थकथनेन तुष्टः
> पुरुषो नाभानेदिष्टायैव स्वं भागं प्रादादित्युक्तं॥ तथाध्वर्युब्राह्मणेऽपि मनुः
> पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत् स नाभानेदिष्टं । तै. सं. ३-१-९-४ । इत्यादिनायमर्थ
> उक्तः । तत्सर्वमत्रानुसंधेयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth anuvāka there are eight sūktas. Of these the first, इदमित्था (*idamitthā*), has twenty-seven ṛks; its seer is Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The six sūktas beginning with this are addressed to the Viśvedevas, as the Anukramaṇī says: इदमित्था सप्ताधिका नाभानेदिष्टो मानवो वैश्वदेवं तदिति (*idamitthā saptādhikā nābhānediṣṭo mānavo vaiśvadevaṃ taditi*). Use: on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭhya rite, in the Vaiśvadeva śastra, this sūkta is recited in place of उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), which would come by extension from the Abhiplava; it is also prescribed by the sūtra: उद्धृत्य चोत्तमं सूक्तं त्रीणेदमित्था रौद्रमिति (*uddhṛtya cottamaṃ sūktaṃ trīṇedamitthā raudramiti*) (Ā. Sū. 8-1). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (5-14) begins: नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजंत्सोऽब्रवीदेत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्येतमेव निष्कामवनवदितारमित्यब्रुवन्न (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ bhrātaro nirabhajaṃtso 'bravīdetya kiṃ mahyamabhāktetyetameva niṣkāmavanavaditāramityabruvanna*) and so on. According to it, Nābhānediṣṭha, rejected by his brothers in the partition, came to his father and asked why no share had been fixed for him. The father said: what need of that share? The Aṅgirases, seated at a sattra for heaven, grow bewildered when they reach the sixth day; have them recite these two sūktas beginning इदमित्था (*idamitthā*); going to heaven they will give a thousand cows. Sent by his father, he went to the Aṅgirases, had them prepare a thousand cows, and made them recite the two sūktas on the sixth day. By the power of that recitation they carried the sacrifice to its end and, wishing to go to heaven, gave him the thousand cows. As he took them, a man in dark garments rose from the north and said: "Brahmin, do not take my share of the sacrificial remainder." He answered that the Aṅgirases had given it to him. The man said: ask your father to whom the share falls. Having gone to his father, he was told that it rightly belongs to Rudra, and so reported to the man that his father said it was his. Pleased at the truthful speech, the man gave the share to Nābhānediṣṭha himself. In the Adhvaryu Brāhmaṇa also, मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत् स नाभानेदिष्टं (*manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ vyabhajat sa nābhānediṣṭaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4), this matter is stated. All that is to be borne in mind here.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

In the fifth anuvāka of the tenth Maṇḍala there are eight sūktas; of them this sūkta इदमित्था (*idamitthā*) is the first, with twenty-seven ṛks. Its seer is Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The six sūktas from this one onward are addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says: *idamitthā saptādhikā nābhānediṣṭo

### Printed p. 407
mānavo vaiśvadevaṃ tat*. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (8-1), उद्धृत्य चोत्तमं सूक्तं त्रीणेदमित्था रौद्रमिति (*uddhṛtya cottamaṃ sūktaṃ trīṇedamitthā raudramiti*), explains that on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭha rite, in the Vaiśvadeva śastra mantra, this sūkta is to be recited in place of the Abhiplava-related sūkta उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*). Regarding this sūkta the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says: नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजन्सोऽब्रवीदेत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्यतमेव निष्ठावनववदितारमित्यब्रुवन् (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ bhrātaro nirabhajanso 'bravīdetya kiṃ mahyamabhāktetyatameva niṣṭhāvanavavaditāramityabruvan*) (Ai. Brā. 5-14), and so on. The commentator has stated that same matter briefly here. Manu had a son named Nābhānediṣṭha, who was studying the Veda in his teacher's house as a celibate student. Meanwhile his elder brothers divided the property of their father Manu and shared it among themselves. When Nābhānediṣṭha returned after finishing his Vedic study and saw that his brothers had shared out even his portion, he asked them where his share was; they said, "Ask your father." He asked his father, who said: "O son, if your brothers have taken all the property, let them take it; do not worry. The Aṅgiras sages are now performing a sattra. They have performed it up to the sixth day and, not knowing what to do on that day, are in doubt. Go there and recite this sūkta इदमित्था (*idamitthā*). Their sacrifice will proceed, and they will give you a thousand cows and go to heaven." As his father said, Nābhānediṣṭha went to the Aṅgirases and recited this sūkta at their sacrifice. Their sacrifice was thereby completed and they gave him a thousand cows. As he was returning with those cows, a man in soiled garments met him on the way and said: "O Nābhānediṣṭha, these thousand cows you are now taking, the remainder of the sacrifice, are mine." Nābhānediṣṭha said, "How so? The Aṅgirases themselves gave me these cows in the sacrifice." The man said, "Then ask your father about this." So Nābhānediṣṭha came to his father, told what had happened, and asked to whom the cows should belong. His father Manu said: "O son, as that man said, it is right that these cows belong to that man, who is Rudra." Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭha went to the man and said: "As you said, these cows must belong to you; my father has said so. You may take them." Pleased at hearing Nābhānediṣṭha speak the truth, the man gave those thousand cows back to Nābhānediṣṭha. This is the main purport of the account. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā too, by sentences such as मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत्सनाभानेदिष्टं (*manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ vyabhajatsanābhānediṣṭaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4), this matter is set out; one may see it there.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Nābhānediṣṭha, of uplifted speech, गूर्तवचा (*gūrtavacā*), makes this hymn, ब्रह्म (*brahma*) = stotra, Rudra's, रौद्रं (*raudraṃ*) = composed by Rudra, in the manner now being done, इत्था (*itthā*); "makes" is to be supplied. Having fashioned it by his insight, क्रत्वा (*kratvā*) = प्रज्ञानेन (*prajñānena*), he makes it in the rite, शच्यामंतः (*śacyāmaṃtaḥ*), in the midst of the sattra, आजौ (*ājau*), in the assembly of the Aṅgirases. The hymn which his parents, क्राणा (*krāṇā*) = making the share, and the brothers, मंहनेष्ठा (*maṃhaneṣṭhā*) = engaged in giving the share, made the means of obtaining cows (the verb "made" is to be supplied). By it Nābhānediṣṭha, on the day to be matured, पक्षे अहन् (*pakṣe ahan*), that is the sixth day, since the Brāhmaṇa says (Ai. Brā. 5-14): "They are bewildered when they reach the sixth day; have them recite these two sūktas on the sixth day." सप्त होतृन् (*sapta hotṛn*): the seven priests, Hotṛ, Praśāstṛ, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the rest, he पर्षत् (*parṣat*) filled on every side; that is, by the two sūktas इदं (*idaṃ*) and इत्था (*itthā*) he brought the sacrifice to its end.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- क्राणा (*krāṇā*)—those engaged in making the partition
- अस्य पितरा (*asya pitarā*)—Nābhānediṣṭha's parents
- मंहनेष्ठाः (*maṃhaneṣṭhāḥ*)—his brothers, engaged in giving the shares
- यत् (*yat*)—which hymn they made the means of obtaining cows;

### Printed p. 409
- रौद्रं (*raudraṃ*)—praising Rudra
- इदं ब्रह्म (*idaṃ brahma*)—this hymn
- गूर्तवचाः (*gūrtavacāḥ*)—Nābhānediṣṭha of uplifted voice
- इत्था (*itthā*)—as will be told below
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by the power of his insight
- शच्यां अंतः (*śacyāṃ aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of the rite
- आजौ (*ājau*)—among the Aṅgirases he fashioned it
- पक्ष्ये अहन् (*pakṣye ahan*)—(with the help of this mantra) on the sixth day, when the rite reaches completion
- सप्त होत्यन् (*sapta hotyan*)—the seven priests, Hotṛ and the rest
- आ पर्षत् (*ā parṣat*)—he made ready so that the sacrifice became complete

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Nābhānediṣṭha's parents, engaged in making the partition, and his brothers, engaged in giving the shares, made a certain hymn the means of obtaining cows. This hymn in praise of Rudra, Nābhānediṣṭha of uplifted voice, as will be told below, fashioned by the power of his insight in the midst of the rite among the Aṅgirases. With the help of this mantra, on the sixth day, when the rite reaches completion, he prepared the sacrifice to be made complete by the seven priests, Hotṛ and the rest.

##### English translation
The fierce-voiced (Nabhanedishtha repeated) through his intelligence this praise of Rudra, in the midst of the ceremony at the assembly (of the Angirasas), which (praise)his parents, making (the partition)and his brothers engaged in giving (the shares accomplished); he perfected the seven priests (therewith) on the day on which the rite was to be matured.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स इत् (*sa it*): that man in dark garments, called Rudra, दानाय (*dānāya*) for giving wealth to those who praise him, and दभ्याय (*dabhyāya*) for the slaying of enemies, वन्सन् (*vansan*) favouring the praisers, सूदैः (*sūdaiḥ*) with the cooks, the destroyers (the sentence is cut off here).
